```text
1	/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
2	/* hostlink: an app's own SysEx conversation with a program on the computer, over fm1-base, by USB or Bluetooth.
3	 *
4	 * Frames are F0 7D <id0> <id1> <ver> <type> <payload...> F7. 7D is the MIDI non-commercial ID; pick
5	 * id0/id1 so you stay apart from fm1-base's own 7D 4C .. frames (Conductor uses 43 4E, "CN").
6	 * The device says HELLO once a second (on every transport that has a computer) until the host answers, then a
7	 * HEARTBEAT once a second on the transport the answer came by; the host counts as present while frames keep
8	 * coming (HOSTLINK_TIMEOUT_MS).
9	 *
10	 * Transports:
11	 *   USB  frames in through APP_SYSEX (app_sysex), out through plat_sysex_send.
12	 *   BLE  fm1-base's own stack (ble_stack = "own") turns BLE-MIDI SysEx into USB-MIDI SysEx packets (CIN 4..7) on
13	 *        PORT_BLE; hl_sx_packet puts them back together. Out: the frame cut into such packets, plat_midi_send to
14	 *        TO_BLE_HOST. (JieLi's stack drops incoming SysEx: Bluetooth needs the own stack.)
15	 *
16	 * Use (unity build: app.c includes hostlink.c; fm1.toml include = ["../common"]):
17	 *   static hostlink_t hl;  static hl_sx_t ble_rx;
18	 *   hl_init(&hl, 0x43, 0x4E, 1);
19	 *   int app_sysex(const uint8_t *p, uint32_t n) { return my_frame(p, n, HL_USB); }
20	 *   main loop: while (plat_midi_in(&pkt, &port)) if (port == PORT_BLE && hl_sx_packet(&ble_rx, pkt, &f, &n))
21	 *                  my_frame(f, n, HL_BLE);
22	 *   my_frame: d = hl_match(&hl, p, n, &t, &len); if (!d) return 0; hl_seen(&hl, now); on HELLO_ACK
23	 *             hl_acked(&hl, now, transport); ...
24	 *   each frame: hl_tick(&hl, now, T_HELLO, T_HEARTBEAT, hello_payload, n);
25	 * HELLO carries the app's payload and then the transport byte (HL_USB / HL_BLE); HEARTBEAT carries ver, transport.
26	 */
27	#pragma once
28	#include <stdint.h>
29	
30	#define HOSTLINK_TIMEOUT_MS 10000u
31	#define HOSTLINK_EVERY_MS 1000u
32	#define HOSTLINK_MAX 64u                 /* the longest payload an app sends through hl_send */
33	#define HOSTLINK_RX_MAX 640u             /* the longest frame taken from Bluetooth (fm1-base's APP_SYSEX limit) */
34	
35	enum { HL_USB, HL_BLE, HL_NTRANSPORTS };
36	
37	typedef struct {
38	    uint8_t id0, id1, ver;
39	    uint8_t acked;                       /* the host answered our HELLO since it was last lost */
40	    uint8_t transport;                   /* HL_USB / HL_BLE: where the answer came from, where we reply */
41	    uint32_t seen;                       /* plat_ms of the last frame from the host (0: never) */
42	    uint32_t sent;                       /* plat_ms of the last HELLO / HEARTBEAT */
43	    uint32_t session;                    /* plat_usb_session when acked over USB: a new cable means a new HELLO */
44	} hostlink_t;
45	
46	/* a SysEx frame put back together from USB-MIDI packets (Bluetooth) */
47	typedef struct {
48	    uint8_t b[HOSTLINK_RX_MAX];
49	    uint32_t n;
50	    uint8_t open, over;                  /* inside a frame; it ran past HOSTLINK_RX_MAX (dropped at its end) */
51	} hl_sx_t;
52	
53	void hl_init(hostlink_t *h, uint8_t id0, uint8_t id1, uint8_t ver);
54	/* one of ours (p: the bytes between F0 and F7): its type and payload; 0 when it is someone else's */
55	const uint8_t *hl_match(const hostlink_t *h, const uint8_t *p, uint32_t n, uint8_t *type, uint32_t *len);
56	void hl_seen(hostlink_t *h, uint32_t now);
57	void hl_acked(hostlink_t *h, uint32_t now, int transport);
58	int hl_host(const hostlink_t *h, uint32_t now);   /* 1: the host is there */
59	int hl_send(hostlink_t *h, uint8_t type, const uint8_t *payload, uint32_t n);   /* to the host's transport; 0 = queued */
60	int hl_send_to(hostlink_t *h, int transport, uint8_t type, const uint8_t *payload, uint32_t n);
61	void hl_tick(hostlink_t *h, uint32_t now, uint8_t hello, uint8_t heartbeat, const uint8_t *hello_p, uint32_t hello_n);
62	/* 1 when pkt (a USB-MIDI event packet) ended a SysEx frame: *frame, *n are its bytes between F0 and F7 */
63	int hl_sx_packet(hl_sx_t *s, uint32_t pkt, const uint8_t **frame, uint32_t *n);
64	/* a whole frame F0 .. F7 as USB-MIDI SysEx packets (CIN 4, then 5 / 6 / 7 at the end): how many went into out */
65	uint32_t hl_sx_packets(const uint8_t *f, uint32_t n, uint32_t *out, uint32_t max);
66
```
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# firmware/common
2	
3	Small modules shared by this repo's fm1-base apps. MIT. Each is a `.h` with the
4	API and usage, and a `.c` that the app includes into fm1-base's unity build.
5	
6	| Module | What it does |
7	|---|---|
8	| `hostlink` | An app's own SysEx conversation with a program on the computer, over USB or Bluetooth: framing under `F0 7D id0 id1 ver`, HELLO on every transport until the host answers, HEARTBEAT after on the transport it answered by, host presence with a timeout, a new HELLO after a new USB session or a lost Bluetooth link. Bluetooth needs `ble_stack = "own"` (JieLi's stack drops incoming SysEx); `hl_sx_packet` puts the SysEx packets back together. |
9	| `ledfx` | Per-LED patterns on the single-colour LEDs: off, glow, mid, lit, pulse, blink, double blink, fast. Turns them into `plat_lights` + `plat_lights_mid` once a frame. |
10	| `chime` | A two-operator FM voice with a short note queue for notification sounds, mixed into the app's render. |
11	
12	## Using them in an app
13	
14	`fm1.toml`:
15	
16	```toml
17	include = ["../common"]
18	```
19	
20	`app.c`, after `#include "fastmath.h"` (chime needs `fm_sinf`, `fm_exp2f`):
21	
22	```c
23	#include "hostlink.c"
24	#include "ledfx.c"
25	#include "chime.c"
26	```
27	
28	They call fm1-base's `plat_*` functions, which are in scope in the unity build.
29	They keep no flash state.
30	
31	`just fw-common-test` builds and runs `tests/` on the computer (hostlink's packet
32	cutting and reassembly). `firmware/conductor` is the first user; its `tests/basic.txt` exercises all three
33	in the host simulator. `firmware/morse` uses `hostlink` (its own `7D 4D 4F` frames) and `ledfx`.
34
````
</details></tool-use>

1	/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
2	/* ledfx: per-LED patterns on the FM-1's single-colour LEDs (fm1-base's off / glow / mid / lit), timed in
3	 * software, so a key can say how urgent it is without colour.
4	 *
5	 *   ledfx_t k = {0}, b = {0};
6	 *   ledfx_set(&k, key, FX_BLINK, now);   ...
7	 *   ledfx_show(&b, &k, extra_lit_buttons);   (once a frame: plat_lights + plat_lights_mid)
8	 *
9	 * PLAY has two LEDs: its bit B_PLAY is the red one, LED_PLAY_GREEN (bit NB) the green one. */
10	#pragma once
11	#include <stdint.h>
12	
13	enum {
14	    FX_OFF,
15	    FX_GLOW,                             /* dim, steady */
16	    FX_MID,                              /* between glow and lit, steady */
17	    FX_LIT,                              /* full, steady */
18	    FX_PULSE,                            /* glow - mid - lit - mid, 1.6 s round: alive, busy */
19	    FX_BLINK,                            /* on / off at 2 Hz: needs you */
20	    FX_DBLINK,                           /* two short flashes every 1.2 s: something broke */
21	    FX_FAST,                             /* on / off at 6 Hz */
22	    FX_N
23	};
24	
25	typedef struct {
26	    uint32_t lit, mid, dim;              /* the bits at each level, built by ledfx_set */
27	} ledfx_t;
28	
29	int ledfx_level(int fx, uint32_t now);   /* 0 off, 1 glow, 2 mid, 3 lit */
30	void ledfx_set(ledfx_t *o, uint32_t bit_index, int fx, uint32_t now);
31	void ledfx_show(const ledfx_t *buttons, const ledfx_t *keys);
32

```text
1	/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
2	/* hostlink: see hostlink.h */
3	#include "hostlink.h"
4	
5	void hl_init(hostlink_t *h, uint8_t id0, uint8_t id1, uint8_t ver)
6	{
7	    h->id0 = id0;
8	    h->id1 = id1;
9	    h->ver = ver;
10	    h->acked = 0;
11	    h->transport = HL_USB;
12	    h->seen = h->sent = h->session = 0;
13	}
14	
15	const uint8_t *hl_match(const hostlink_t *h, const uint8_t *p, uint32_t n, uint8_t *type, uint32_t *len)
16	{
17	    if (n < 5u || p[0] != 0x7Du || p[1] != h->id0 || p[2] != h->id1 || p[3] != h->ver)
18	        return 0;
19	    *type = p[4];
20	    *len = n - 5u;
21	    return p + 5;
22	}
23	
24	void hl_seen(hostlink_t *h, uint32_t now) { h->seen = now ? now : 1u; }
25	
26	void hl_acked(hostlink_t *h, uint32_t now, int transport)
27	{
28	    hl_seen(h, now);
29	    h->acked = 1;
30	    h->transport = (uint8_t)(transport == HL_BLE ? HL_BLE : HL_USB);
31	    h->session = plat_usb_session();
32	}
33	
34	int hl_host(const hostlink_t *h, uint32_t now) { return h->acked && h->seen && now - h->seen < HOSTLINK_TIMEOUT_MS; }
35	
36	/* ---------------------------------------------------------- USB-MIDI SysEx packets --- */
37	int hl_sx_packet(hl_sx_t *s, uint32_t pkt, const uint8_t **frame, uint32_t *n)
38	{
39	    uint32_t cin = pkt & 0x0Fu, k, nb;
40	    if (cin == 0x4u || cin == 0x7u)
41	        nb = 3;
42	    else if (cin == 0x6u)
43	        nb = 2;
44	    else if (cin == 0x5u)
45	        nb = 1;
46	    else
47	        return 0;                        /* not SysEx */
48	    for (k = 0; k < nb; k++) {
49	        uint8_t b = (uint8_t)(pkt >> (8u + 8u * k));
50	        if (b == 0xF0u) {
51	            s->open = 1;
52	            s->over = 0;
53	            s->n = 0;
54	        } else if (b == 0xF7u) {
55	            int whole = s->open && !s->over;
56	            s->open = 0;
57	            if (whole) {
58	                *frame = s->b;
59	                *n = s->n;
60	                return 1;
61	            }
62	        } else if (s->open) {
63	            if (s->n < HOSTLINK_RX_MAX)
64	                s->b[s->n++] = b;
65	            else
66	                s->over = 1;
67	        }
68	    }
69	    return 0;
70	}
71	
72	uint32_t hl_sx_packets(const uint8_t *f, uint32_t n, uint32_t *out, uint32_t max)
73	{
74	    uint32_t i = 0, k = 0;
75	    while (i < n && k < max) {
76	        uint32_t left = n - i, take = left > 3u ? 3u : left, cin, j, pkt;
77	        if (left > 3u)
78	            cin = 0x4u;                  /* start / continue */
79	        else
80	            cin = 0x4u + take;           /* the end: 5, 6, 7 for 1, 2, 3 bytes */
81	        pkt = cin;
82	        for (j = 0; j < take; j++)
83	            pkt |= (uint32_t)f[i + j] << (8u + 8u * j);
84	        out[k++] = pkt;
85	        i += take;
86	    }
87	    return k;
88	}
89	
90	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------- sending --- */
91	int hl_send_to(hostlink_t *h, int transport, uint8_t type, const uint8_t *payload, uint32_t n)
92	{
93	    uint8_t f[HOSTLINK_MAX + 7u];
94	    uint32_t i, k = 0;
95	    if (n > HOSTLINK_MAX)
96	        return -1;
97	    f[k++] = 0xF0;
98	    f[k++] = 0x7D;
99	    f[k++] = h->id0;
100	    f[k++] = h->id1;
101	    f[k++] = h->ver;
102	    f[k++] = type & 0x7Fu;
103	    for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
104	        f[k++] = payload[i] & 0x7Fu;
105	    f[k++] = 0xF7;
106	    if (transport == HL_BLE) {
107	#if FM1B_BLE
108	        uint32_t pk[(HOSTLINK_MAX + 7u + 2u) / 3u + 1u], np = hl_sx_packets(f, k, pk, sizeof pk / sizeof pk[0]);
109	        if (!plat_ble_connected() || plat_midi_out_room(TO_BLE_HOST) < np)
110	            return -1;                   /* whole or not at all: a frame cut short is worse than one late */
111	        for (i = 0; i < np; i++)
112	            plat_midi_send(pk[i], TO_BLE_HOST);
113	        return 0;
114	#else
115	        return -1;
116	#endif
117	    }
118	    return plat_sysex_send(f, k);
119	}
120	
121	int hl_send(hostlink_t *h, uint8_t type, const uint8_t *payload, uint32_t n)
122	{
123	    return hl_send_to(h, h->transport, type, payload, n);
124	}
125	
126	void hl_tick(hostlink_t *h, uint32_t now, uint8_t hello, uint8_t heartbeat, const uint8_t *hello_p, uint32_t hello_n)
127	{
128	    if (h->acked && !hl_host(h, now))
129	        h->acked = 0;                    /* lost: say HELLO again */
130	    if (h->acked && h->transport == HL_USB && plat_usb_session() != h->session)
131	        h->acked = 0;                    /* a new cable */
132	#if FM1B_BLE
133	    if (h->acked && h->transport == HL_BLE && !plat_ble_connected())
134	        h->acked = 0;                    /* the Bluetooth link went */
135	#endif
136	    if (h->sent && now - h->sent < HOSTLINK_EVERY_MS)
137	        return;
138	    h->sent = now ? now : 1u;
139	    if (h->acked) {
140	        uint8_t hb[2] = {h->ver, h->transport};
141	        hl_send(h, heartbeat, hb, 2);
142	        return;
143	    }
144	    {
145	        uint8_t b[HOSTLINK_MAX];             /* the app's HELLO, then the transport it goes by */
146	        uint32_t i;
147	        if (hello_n >= HOSTLINK_MAX)
148	            return;
149	        for (i = 0; i < hello_n; i++)
150	            b[i] = hello_p[i];
151	        if (plat_usb_session()) {
152	            b[hello_n] = HL_USB;
153	            hl_send_to(h, HL_USB, hello, b, hello_n + 1u);
154	        }
155	#if FM1B_BLE
156	        if (plat_ble_connected()) {
157	            b[hello_n] = HL_BLE;
158	            hl_send_to(h, HL_BLE, hello, b, hello_n + 1u);
159	        }
160	#endif
161	    }
162	}
163

1	# Flash 配置圖
2	
3	FM-1 的 flash 是 1 MiB，分成 256 個 4 KiB 的 sector。誰把什麼放在哪裡，決定了換韌體時什麼會留下、什麼會被蓋掉。這頁把各個來源的說法和我自己備份的比對放在一起。
4	
5	## 總覽
6	
7	| 位址 | 內容 | 來源 |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| `0x00000`–`0x03FFF` | **boot head**：bootloader 與 boot 設定（16 KiB）。壞了就開不了機 | `[上游]` M-Flasher、Unbricker |
10	| `0x04000`–`0x92FFF` | **韌體區**。多數韌體（原廠 V15、SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1）佔這段 | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的寫入計畫 |
11	| `0x93000`–`0xE8FFF` | 原廠 V15 的**設定區**。社群韌體也把資料放在這裡面 | `[上游]` |
12	| `0xE9000` | Bluetooth 資料（配對） | `[上游]` |
13	| `0xEA000`–`0xFBFFF` | 原廠音色（factory voices） | `[上游]` |
14	| `0xFC000`–`0xFEFFF` | M-Flasher 的圖上標為 free；Felucca 系拿來放全域設定 | `[實機]` |
15	| `0xFF000`–`0xFFFFF` | key / MAC，裝置自己的資料 | `[上游]` |
16	
17	M-Flasher 的 flash map 用顏色標的就是這些：BOOT `00–03`、FIRMWARE `04–92`、SETTINGS `93–E8`、PAIRINGS `E9`、SOUNDS `EA–FB`、free `FC–FE`、MAC `FF`。
18	
19	## 韌體區不一定只到 `0x92FFF`
20	
21	| 韌體 | 佔用範圍 | 來源 |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| SLOOP 2.8.5、Agent Deck 0.7、CTL-1 1.0.3 | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入到 `0x8FFFF`） | `[實機]` |
24	| Conductor 0.1（自製，fm1-base） | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入 `0x04000`–`0x8EFFF`、`0x91000`–`0x91FFF`） | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：140 sectors |
25	| Morse 0.1 / 0.2（自製，fm1-base） | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入：Conductor 0.3 → 0.1 是 `0x04000`–`0x21FFF`，0.1 → 0.2 是 `0x04000`–`0x23FFF`） | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：30、32 sectors |
26	| **ChoralRoot 0.41** | `0x04000`–**`0x9EFFF`** | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：152 sectors |
27	| **原廠 V16** | 到 **`0xA8FFF`** | `[上游]` Unbricker |
28	
29	超出 `0x92FFF` 的韌體會直接蓋掉別人放在 `0x93000` 之後的資料。
30	
31	## Felucca 系韌體的資料位置
32	
33	Felucca、SLOOP、ChoralRoot 以及 Dinghy、fm1-base 系的韌體大多沿用同一套位址 `[上游]`：
34	
35	| 位址 | 內容 |
36	|---|---|
37	| `0x97000` 起 | project（曲子） |
38	| `0x9F000` | SLOOP 的 autosave（和 ChoralRoot 的 FM6 bank 是同一個物件編號） |
39	| `0xA0000` 起 | samples |
40	| `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF` | 自製 [Morse](../dev/morse.md#flash) 的設定與學習進度（這台機器的備份裡這兩個 sector 都是空的） |
41	| `0xDC000` 起 | user preset bank；CTL-1 與 fm1-base 的 app（含 Conductor）用來放面板校正 |
42	| `0xDE000` | CTL-1 的 Bluetooth 設定 |
43	| `0xE0000` | 更新時暫存 update loader |
44	| `0xF2000`–`0xF3FFF` | RemoteFM1 第一次開 Bluetooth 時寫入 |
45	| `0xFC000` | 全域設定。**SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1 都寫這裡** |
46	| `0xFE000` | SLOOP autosave 的另一份 |
47	
48	因為位址共用，韌體之間會互相踩到對方的資料，也會讀到對方留下的東西。
49	
50	## 我的機器上實際發生的 `[實機]`
51	
52	用各階段的完整備份逐 sector 比對：
53	
54	| 動作 | 改變的 sector |
55	|---|---|
56	| 原廠 015 → 裝 SLOOP 並玩過 | 韌體區，加上 `0x97000`、`0x9F000`、`0xFC000`、`0xFD000`、`0xFE000` |
57	| → Agent Deck | 韌體區，加上 `0xFC000`（蓋掉 SLOOP 的設定） |
58	| → 回 SLOOP | 韌體區，加上 `0xFE000`。曲子還在 |
59	| → CTL-1 | 韌體區，加上 `0xDE000`、`0xDF000`、`0xFC000`、`0xFD000` |
60	| → ChoralRoot | `0x04000`–`0x9EFFF`，蓋掉了 `0x97000` 的 SLOOP project（已執行，尚未用備份比對確認其他 sector） |
61	| → Conductor | 韌體區 140 個 sector（`0x04000`–`0x8EFFF`、`0x91000`–`0x91FFF`）。開機後不寫任何資料（預演 `[模擬]`；實機尚未用備份比對） |
62	
63	原廠出廠時 `0x93000`、`0xE9000`–`0xF2000`、`0xFA000`、`0xFB000` 有資料，`0xFC000`–`0xFE000` 是空的。
64	
65	## 自己比對兩份備份
66	
67	```python
68	S = 4096
69	a = open("backups/A/x.bin", "rb").read()
70	b = open("backups/B/y.bin", "rb").read()
71	print([hex(i * S) for i in range(256) if a[i * S:(i + 1) * S] != b[i * S:(i + 1) * S]])
72	```
73	
74	## 這對操作的意義
75	
76	- **只重裝韌體會保留資料區**，所以 SLOOP ↔ Agent Deck 來回曲子還在。
77	- **韌體比較大的（ChoralRoot、V16）會吃掉資料區**，回去時要還原備份。
78	- **共用的 `0xFC000` 每換一次就被蓋一次**，各韌體的全域設定不會跨韌體保留。
79	- **原廠音色在 `0xEA000`–`0xFBFFF`**，有些韌體會寫這一段。只有原廠備份救得回來。
80	- 更完整的後果見[變磚的原理與分級](../getting-started/bricking.md)與[多韌體切換](../firmware/switching.md)。
81

# 摩斯電碼機（Morse）

把 FM-1 變成隨身的摩斯電碼機：琴鍵當電鍵發報、即時解碼成文字、琴鍵當字母鍵盤把文字播成摩斯、用閃卡隨身練習，也能接電腦和 [Vail](https://vailmorse.com/) 跟網路上的人互傳。韌體在 `firmware/morse/`，電腦端在 `host/morse/`，都是 MIT。

**狀態（2026-11-18）：機器上是韌體 0.2（00:14 刷入）。0.1 時已在實機確認發報、解碼、TYPE、PRACTICE、和電腦連線；0.2 的 RHYTHM、KEY 三種顯示、TYPE、LISTEN、PRESET 本人試過覺得不錯，升級後學習進度也還在 `[實機]`。韌體 0.3（修 TYPE 鍵上點劃的排版）、host 0.3.0 已在模擬器驗證，還沒刷。** 操作方式見[操作速查](morse-cheatsheet.md)。

## 有沒有人做過 { #prior-art }

2026-11-17 查過，**沒有**找到 FM-1 上的摩斯作品，也沒有讓兩台 FM-1 互傳訊息的韌體 `[調研]`：

- [Firmware Hub catalog](https://thefirmwarehub.com/catalog.json) 的 244 個套件裡沒有 Morse、CW、keyer（電報意義的）、trainer。
- [FM1 Developers' Wiki](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/) 沒有相關頁面。
- GitHub 搜尋 `fm1 morse`、`m-vave morse`、`fm1-base morse` 都沒有結果（code search 只涵蓋 default branch，可能漏掉）。

相近的作品：SPELLBOX 把琴鍵當 A–Z 鍵盤；MIDIMON（fm1-base）同時當 BLE peripheral、central 與 USB host，作者說用它來 debug 另一台 FM-1。設計時參考的是其他平台的摩斯機：[Morserino-32](https://github.com/oe1wkl/Morserino-32)（模式分類、收發用不同音高）、[LCWO](https://lcwo.net/)（Koch 順序）、Vail（MIDI 格式）。只參考做法，沒有複製程式碼。

## 功能

| 頁面 | 做什麼 | 版本 |
|---|---|---|
| **PRACTICE** | 開機直接進來。一回合 20 張閃卡（10–30 可調），幾分鐘做完 | 0.1 |
| **LISTEN** | 一直播下去：你開放的 Koch 字組、常用英文字、QSO 範例、縮寫和意思、諺語。可以顯示正在播的字，或隱藏起來當抄收練習 | 0.2 |
| **KEY** | 自由發報：琴鍵是電鍵，解出來的字、你的速度、dah:dit 比例、字內停頓。三種顯示：TEXT（字）、CODE（每個字下面是你實際打的點劃）、TIMING（每一下照實際長短畫成條） | 0.1；顯示方式 0.2 |
| **RHYTHM** | 練長短：只打 dit、只打 dah、交替、SOS、自由按。每一下和目標長度比對，給提示和建議的發報速度 | 0.2 |
| **TYPE** | 琴鍵是字母，`OCT-`／`OCT+` 翻三頁：字母、數字和符號、片語。鍵上可以顯示點劃；LIVE（按一個字送一個）或 COMPOSE（打好一行再送） | 0.1；翻頁、片語、COMPOSE 0.2 |
| **CHART** | 像五十音表的字表，依熟練度上色 | 0.1 |
| **SETTINGS** | 速度組合（PRESET）、聽的速度、間隔、發報速度、音高、keyer（直鍵、iambic A、iambic B）、paddle 左右、聲音、每回合張數、學習方式、TYPE 的排列 | 0.1；PRESET、發報速度 0.2 |

電鍵有兩種：**直鍵**是任一琴鍵按下就發；**iambic paddle** 是左半邊琴鍵（F3–F4）發 dit、右半邊（F#4–G5）發 dah，兩邊同時按會交替（squeeze）。Mode B 會記住在一個 element 中途按的另一邊，放開後補發一個。

聲音是兩個 sine voice：自己發的用設定的音高（預設 600 Hz），收到的高一個大三度，聽得出是誰在發。靜音時所有琴鍵的燈會跟著節奏亮（自己發的全亮、收到的半亮），畫面上也有一條燈號。

## 速度：WPM 是什麼、該設多少 { #speed }

WPM 是每分鐘幾個字，以 PARIS 這個字（50 個單位）為準：**dit 的長度 = 1200 ÷ WPM 毫秒**。摩斯沒有規定一定要多快，重要的是比例：

| 元素 | 長度 |
|---|---|
| dit | 1 單位 |
| dah | 3 單位 |
| 字裡面的停頓 | 1 單位 |
| 字和字之間 | 3 單位 |
| 字詞之間 | 7 單位 |

| WPM | dit | dah | 大概是 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 240 ms | 720 ms | 很慢，看得清楚每一下 |
| 10 | 120 ms | 360 ms | 新手手打 |
| 13 | 92 ms | 277 ms | 以前美國業餘無線電 General 考試的速度 |
| 20 | 60 ms | 180 ms | Koch 建議的字元速度 |
| 25 | 48 ms | 144 ms | 熟練的通聯 |

0.2 起分成兩個速度（0.1 只有一個）：

- **聽的速度**（K1，加上 K2 的間隔）：FM-1 播給你聽的速度。Koch 的做法是字本身用 20 WPM 左右播，聽起來是一整個聲音；字和字之間用 **Farnsworth** 拉開（例如「20/8」是字用 20 WPM，整體像 8 WPM），讓你有時間想。
- **發報速度**（K4）：你手打的速度，用來設定 iambic keyer 的節奏、解碼器的起點、RHYTHM 頁和 TIMING 檢視的目標長度。新手的手通常比耳朵慢，所以這個要另外設低一點。

**推薦的組合**（SETTINGS 最上面的 PRESET，轉的時候畫面會說明）：

| PRESET | 聽 | 發 | 適合 |
----
### 時序

- **1 kHz tick**（`APP_TICK`，timer interrupt）：讀琴鍵 → keyer → 開關 sidetone 的 gate、送 MIDI、讀 MIDI in，按鍵變化連同時間戳放進 ring buffer。main loop 解碼、跑頁面和閃卡、畫畫面。
- **Sidetone 的抖動**：gate 每個 audio block 讀一次（256 frames = 5.8 ms），按下到出聲最多差一個 block。
- **琴鍵的 debounce**：按下約 1–2 ms 後看到、放開約 9 ms 後看到，所以直鍵的每個 mark 會被量長約 7 ms（fm1-base `bsp/boards/fm1/fm1_input.h`）。韌體在實機 build 時從直鍵的 mark 扣掉 7 ms 再解碼。fm1-emu 裡看到的是按下 +3 ms、放開 +10 ms，和預期一致 `[模擬]`。
- **解碼器**：分別追蹤 dit、dah 和字間間隔的平均，取中間當門檻，所以跟得上偏離設定 ±30% 的發報速度，也能讀 Farnsworth 拉開的間隔（單元測試：5／15／25／35 WPM 加 ±20% 抖動全對）。0.2 起，同一個字裡出現兩下長度差 2 倍以上時，會直接把它們當成一個 dit 一個 dah，並回頭修正前一下的判斷：新手太慢的 dit 被當成 dah，遇到第一個真正的 dah 就會改回來。但如果手打得比發報速度慢很多，連字裡的停頓都會超過切字的門檻，所以發報速度還是要設得接近你的手。
- **實機上看到的** `[實機]`：手打的 O（三個 dah）一次被讀成 M + T，因為 dah 之間停了 146、175 ms，和那次字與字之間的 169–224 ms 一樣長；字裡面的間隔應該只有一個 dit。另一次 dah 之間 124、133 ms 就讀對。也看到一次 9 ms 的按鍵彈跳：解碼器扣掉 debounce 偏差後當成雜訊忽略，但 MIDI 照送（Vail 會看到一下極短的按下）。

### 存檔 { #flash }

一筆紀錄（設定 + 學習進度，約 280 bytes）放在 `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF`，透過 fm1-base 的 storage 層存（A/B 兩份、CRC）。在回合結束或離開、改設定 3 秒後才寫。不碰 SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1 共用的 `0xFC000`。這台機器所有備份的 `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF` 都是空的。

0.2 沿用 0.1 的紀錄格式：0.1 留下的空位改放 KEY／TYPE／LISTEN 的顯示選項、發報速度、LISTEN 的節目。從 0.1 升級時設定和進度都保留，發報速度從 0 補成預設的 10（fm1-emu 兩種晶片驗證過 `[模擬]`）。

預演 `[模擬]`：把 `firmware/morse/build/morse.fwsc` 疊在 `backups/2026-11-17-2052-pre-conductor/` 上開機、改一個設定、玩完一回合：

| | sector |
|---|---|
| 安裝（和目前機上的 Conductor 不同的部分） | `0x04000`–`0x1EFFF`，27 個；套件映像範圍是 `0x04000`–`0x92FFF` |
| 執行時寫入 | `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF`，只有這 2 個 |

### 大小

`just fw-build morse`（2026-11-17）：

| 版本 | app | `.data+.bss` |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 109,508 B | 27,180 / 98,304 B |
| 0.2 | 127,712 B | 28,444 / 98,304 B |
| 0.3 | 127,880 B | 28,444 / 98,304 B |

上限是 581,564 B；RAM code 5,100 / 32,768 B；套件 616,003 B，identity `FM-1_1300`。這兩版都沒有開藍牙；加上 own BLE stack 和 central 大約再多 55–70 KB，仍然很寬裕。

````text
1	# Flash 配置圖
2	
3	FM-1 的 flash 是 1 MiB，分成 256 個 4 KiB 的 sector。誰把什麼放在哪裡，決定了換韌體時什麼會留下、什麼會被蓋掉。這頁把各個來源的說法和我自己備份的比對放在一起。
4	
5	## 總覽
6	
7	| 位址 | 內容 | 來源 |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| `0x00000`–`0x03FFF` | **boot head**：bootloader 與 boot 設定（16 KiB）。壞了就開不了機 | `[上游]` M-Flasher、Unbricker |
10	| `0x04000`–`0x92FFF` | **韌體區**。多數韌體（原廠 V15、SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1）佔這段 | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的寫入計畫 |
11	| `0x93000`–`0xE8FFF` | 原廠 V15 的**設定區**。社群韌體也把資料放在這裡面 | `[上游]` |
12	| `0xE9000` | Bluetooth 資料（配對） | `[上游]` |
13	| `0xEA000`–`0xFBFFF` | 原廠音色（factory voices） | `[上游]` |
14	| `0xFC000`–`0xFEFFF` | M-Flasher 的圖上標為 free；Felucca 系拿來放全域設定 | `[實機]` |
15	| `0xFF000`–`0xFFFFF` | key / MAC，裝置自己的資料 | `[上游]` |
16	
17	M-Flasher 的 flash map 用顏色標的就是這些：BOOT `00–03`、FIRMWARE `04–92`、SETTINGS `93–E8`、PAIRINGS `E9`、SOUNDS `EA–FB`、free `FC–FE`、MAC `FF`。
18	
19	## 韌體區不一定只到 `0x92FFF`
20	
21	| 韌體 | 佔用範圍 | 來源 |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| SLOOP 2.8.5、Agent Deck 0.7、CTL-1 1.0.3 | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入到 `0x8FFFF`） | `[實機]` |
24	| Conductor 0.1（自製，fm1-base） | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入 `0x04000`–`0x8EFFF`、`0x91000`–`0x91FFF`） | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：140 sectors |
25	| Morse 0.1 / 0.2（自製，fm1-base） | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入：Conductor 0.3 → 0.1 是 `0x04000`–`0x21FFF`，0.1 → 0.2 是 `0x04000`–`0x23FFF`） | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：30、32 sectors |
26	| **ChoralRoot 0.41** | `0x04000`–**`0x9EFFF`** | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：152 sectors |
27	| **原廠 V16** | 到 **`0xA8FFF`** | `[上游]` Unbricker |
28	
29	超出 `0x92FFF` 的韌體會直接蓋掉別人放在 `0x93000` 之後的資料。
30	
31	## Felucca 系韌體的資料位置
32	
33	Felucca、SLOOP、ChoralRoot 以及 Dinghy、fm1-base 系的韌體大多沿用同一套位址 `[上游]`：
34	
35	| 位址 | 內容 |
36	|---|---|
37	| `0x97000` 起 | project（曲子） |
38	| `0x9F000` | SLOOP 的 autosave（和 ChoralRoot 的 FM6 bank 是同一個物件編號） |
39	| `0xA0000` 起 | samples |
40	| `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF` | 自製 [Morse](../dev/morse.md#flash) 的設定與學習進度（這台機器的備份裡這兩個 sector 都是空的） |
41	| `0xDC000` 起 | user preset bank；CTL-1 與 fm1-base 的 app（含 Conductor）用來放面板校正 |
42	| `0xDE000` | CTL-1 的 Bluetooth 設定 |
43	| `0xE0000` | 更新時暫存 update loader |
44	| `0xF2000`–`0xF3FFF` | RemoteFM1 第一次開 Bluetooth 時寫入 |
45	| `0xFC000` | 全域設定。**SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1 都寫這裡** |
46	| `0xFE000` | SLOOP autosave 的另一份 |
47	
48	因為位址共用，韌體之間會互相踩到對方的資料，也會讀到對方留下的東西。
49	
50	## 我的機器上實際發生的 `[實機]`
51	
52	用各階段的完整備份逐 sector 比對：
53	
54	| 動作 | 改變的 sector |
55	|---|---|
56	| 原廠 015 → 裝 SLOOP 並玩過 | 韌體區，加上 `0x97000`、`0x9F000`、`0xFC000`、`0xFD000`、`0xFE000` |
57	| → Agent Deck | 韌體區，加上 `0xFC000`（蓋掉 SLOOP 的設定） |
58	| → 回 SLOOP | 韌體區，加上 `0xFE000`。曲子還在 |
59	| → CTL-1 | 韌體區，加上 `0xDE000`、`0xDF000`、`0xFC000`、`0xFD000` |
60	| → ChoralRoot | `0x04000`–`0x9EFFF`，蓋掉了 `0x97000` 的 SLOOP project（已執行，尚未用備份比對確認其他 sector） |
61	| → Conductor | 韌體區 140 個 sector（`0x04000`–`0x8EFFF`、`0x91000`–`0x91FFF`）。開機後不寫任何資料（預演 `[模擬]`；實機尚未用備份比對） |
62	
63	原廠出廠時 `0x93000`、`0xE9000`–`0xF2000`、`0xFA000`、`0xFB000` 有資料，`0xFC000`–`0xFE000` 是空的。
64	
65	## 自己比對兩份備份
66	
67	```python
68	S = 4096
69	a = open("backups/A/x.bin", "rb").read()
70	b = open("backups/B/y.bin", "rb").read()
71	print([hex(i * S) for i in range(256) if a[i * S:(i + 1) * S] != b[i * S:(i + 1) * S]])
72	```
73	
74	## 這對操作的意義
75	
76	- **只重裝韌體會保留資料區**，所以 SLOOP ↔ Agent Deck 來回曲子還在。
77	- **韌體比較大的（ChoralRoot、V16）會吃掉資料區**，回去時要還原備份。
78	- **共用的 `0xFC000` 每換一次就被蓋一次**，各韌體的全域設定不會跨韌體保留。
79	- **原廠音色在 `0xEA000`–`0xFBFFF`**，有些韌體會寫這一段。只有原廠備份救得回來。
80	- 更完整的後果見[變磚的原理與分級](../getting-started/bricking.md)與[多韌體切換](../firmware/switching.md)。
81
````

```text
**Speech/singing synthesis:** The page doesn't name the synthesizer, so I can't say whether it uses SAM, formant, LPC, eSpeak, or phoneme rules. It says "The singing voice is its own project, [386 DX Engine](https://github.com/seajaysec/386-DX-ENGINE)," built for this firmware. The robot's face follows the voice: the mouth opens with the sound, and the eyes and head track pitch and vibrato.

**Typing text:** You type lines on the FM-1 itself and sing them to notes you play on its keys. The page doesn't describe the typing mechanics. Keys, Bass, and Drums are written a phrase at a time and arranged into songs.

**Uploading from a computer:** The web page (Chrome or Edge, FM-1 connected) installs the firmware and puts songs into the FM-1's eight slots. You can use thirteen bundled public-domain standards or import a .kar or .mid file. The page doesn't say how lyrics are handled during import.

**Licence:** GPL-3.0. The page says LICENSING.md explains where the code comes from, but doesn't summarize it.

**Memory/CPU:** No figures are given. The build script checks flash, RAM, and pool budgets, but the page doesn't report the numbers.
```

<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/pjac1810/spellbox`

```text
**SPELLBOX** is a talking spelling game for the M-VAVE FM-1, built on the foma firmware (Felucca platform).

- **Speech method:** It uses LPC synthesis with 10 coefficients at 8 kHz and an 8-bit converter, modeled on the 1978 Speak & Spell. The page doesn't mention TMS5220 emulation, talkie, or MAME. Its own integer "speech chip" (`src/speech.c`) runs a 10-stage lattice filter, interpolated 8 times per frame, with chirp or noise excitation.
- **Data source:** The author says no data from the original TI ROMs is used. The words and 42 phonemes were spoken by the open-source espeak-ng synthesizer, then analyzed into LPC frames by `tools/gen_speech.py`. The output goes to `src/speech.h`.
- **Vocabulary:** There are 100 words in 4 levels of 25, each up to 8 letters. The word choices come from wordfreq frequency lists.
- **Pronunciation for SPEAK:** A compressed dictionary of about 12,000 common English words, then suffix handling (-S, -ED, -ING, etc.), then letter-to-sound rules. The rules alone reach about 83% correct phonemes.
- **Storage:** The page doesn't say where the word list or audio sits on the device beyond the generated `src/speech.h`. Flash and RAM usage are not stated.
- **Adding words:** Yes. Edit the lists at the top of `tools/gen_speech.py`, install the listed Python packages, and rerun the script.
- **Games:** SPELL, LETTER, SAY IT, SECRET CODE, MYSTERY WORD, SING, LETTER SYNTH, and SPEAK.
- **Keyboard:** Alphabetical. A is the lowest key (F3), then B, C, and so on through Z. The highest key (G5) is ENTER. The display shows each key's letter.
- **Display:** An 8-character blue-green fluorescent display behind a red window. The code uses a 14-segment display driver.
- **License:** GPL-3.0-only. espeak-ng (GPL-3.0) is used only to build the data. wordfreq word lists are CC BY-SA 4.0.
- **Installation:** Via a web installer in Chrome or Edge over USB. Rescue mode (hold OCT− at power-on) restores M-VAVE V15 firmware.
```
</details></tool-use>

- **Sample rate:** Note lengths are counted at 22050 Hz. Output is 11025 Hz, 16-bit mono.

- **Target CPU:** The M-VAVE FM-1 karaoke hardware, described as a small processor with a second core for singing. The engine also builds to WebAssembly for the browser demo, and a `DX_HOST` build runs on a desktop thread.

## 這台機器是什麼

- 口袋大小的 6-operator FM 合成器，SoC 是 JieLi AC791N，內建 1 MiB SPI NOR flash。
- 27 個發光琴鍵、240×240 彩色螢幕、7 個 encoder 加一個 master 旋鈕、一排功能鍵、喇叭與電池。
- USB-C（MIDI、依韌體支援 audio）、3.5 mm TRS MIDI IN、3.5 mm 音訊輸出、Bluetooth MIDI（依韌體）。細節見[接口與連線](hardware/io.md)。
- 有活躍的開源韌體社群，可以變成 groovebox、鼓機、sampler、MIDI controller，甚至 coding agent 的實體控制台。

## 證據標記

這個生態每週都在變，所以頁面上會標出資訊的可信程度：

- `[實機]`：在我自己的機器上看到的，日期記在[我的機器](device-log.md)。
- `[上游]`：上游 repo 或文件寫的，附連結。
- `[模擬]`：在 fm1-emu 裡看到的，不等於實機。
- `[調研]`：來自調研筆記，還沒對過上游。

----
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Kerem Kilic (Ellic Studio): checked start, stop/restart, the sample and rate contract */
/* FM-1 audio out: ALNK0 I2S -> external codec, double-buffered DMA
 * Fixed format: stereo L,R interleaved, signed Q23 in int32_t (sign-extended
 * low 24 bits, NOT shifted left by 8). Silence = 0, range -8388608..8388607.
 * Fixed 44.1 kHz family: stock clock is 24000000/544 ~= 44117.647 Hz.
 * This is not exact 44100 Hz, nor a 48 kHz/resampling API.
 * Application owns two halves of half_words int32_t; init clears both.
 *
 *   fm1_audio_init_checked(buf, buffer_words, half_words, rate, isr, prio)
 *                         validates capacity, RAM range, alignment and clock;
 *                         returns 0 or FM1_AUDIO_ERR_* (warn_unused_result:
 *                         a refused start is silence). IRQs must be off.
 *   fm1_audio_init(buf, half_words, isr, prio) compatibility wrapper, assumes
 *                         capacity >= 2 * half_words; now returns status too.
 *                         isr = asm wrapper (fm1_isr.S) for FM1_IRQ_ALNK0
 *   in the ISR:   p = fm1_audio_pending();  fm1_audio_ack_aux(p);
 *                 if (p & FM1_AUDIO_HALF) { fill fm1_audio_free_half();
 *                                           fm1_audio_ack_half(); }
 *   fm1_audio_stop()      IRQ masked, DMA off, pending cleared. Repeatable.
 * Restart = stop then init (both halves cleared, DMA position reset).
 * Underrun = DMA repeats stale samples; no automatic silence or detection.
 * See docs/BOARD_IO.md for deadlines, races and application recovery.
 */
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include "fm1_cc.h"
#include "fm1_time.h"
#include "fm1_irq.h"
#include "fm1_gpio.h"

#ifndef FM1_AUDIO_REG
#define FM1_AUDIO_REG(type, addr) (*(volatile type *)(addr))
#endif
#define FM1_ALNK 0x12E00u
#define FM1_ALNK_CON0 FM1_AUDIO_REG(uint16_t, FM1_ALNK + 0x00u)
#define FM1_ALNK_CON1 FM1_AUDIO_REG(uint16_t, FM1_ALNK + 0x04u)
#define FM1_ALNK_CON2 FM1_AUDIO_REG(uint8_t, FM1_ALNK + 0x08u)
#define FM1_ALNK_CON3 FM1_AUDIO_REG(uint8_t, FM1_ALNK + 0x0Cu)
----

"""A dictation hotkey held down from the FM-1: the daemon presses keys on this Mac as
if from the keyboard, so Wispr Flow, Handy or macOS Dictation start listening.

Hold mode (push-to-talk): key down while the device's button is held, up on release.
Toggle mode: a quick press and release on the button's press (for apps that toggle).
The keys are always let go: on release, after max_hold seconds, when the device
restarts, and when the daemon exits. Needs Accessibility permission for the app the
daemon runs in (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import sys
import time

_FW = "/System/Library/Frameworks/{0}.framework/{0}"

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/genkigenki/Speak37`

```text
**What it does:** Speak37 is unofficial firmware that replaces the stock firmware on the M-Vave SMK-37 and FM-1. It's described as "A speech synthesizer in the style of the Speak & Spell." Each key speaks the next word of a sentence at that key's pitch, and it includes drums, effects, and MOPE, a robot that comments on what you play.

**Engine:** It's not SAM or general text-to-speech. It's an LPC engine in the style of the TI TMS5220, with a ten-stage lattice filter. The words are prerecorded at build time: "the free speech synthesizer espeak-ng" speaks them, and Speak37's own encoder converts them into TMS5220-style frames.

**Arbitrary words:** Not directly. It speaks only words in its built-in vocabulary (2759 on the SMK-37 build, 2576 on the FM-1). In the USER editor, a word that isn't in the vocabulary is spelled letter by letter. You can add new words by editing the bank text and rebuilding, which requires espeak-ng for words not already cached.

**FM-1 build:** Yes. The package is `speak37-fm1-1.0.fwsc`, and the FM-1 has its own build target.

**Licence:** Speak37 is GPL-3.0-only. The word lists in `assets/speak/words_*.txt` are CC BY-SA 4.0. The RHYTHM 808 drum voices come from M-VAVE's FM1 Open under MIT. Felucca, the platform it's built on, is GPL-3.0-only.
```
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/shan-sherif/fm-1-chimera-vocal`

```text
**Studio-to-FM-1 transfer:** The page says the Studio sends words "to yours over USB" and names a "Studio's SysEx" test, so SysEx appears to be the transport. It doesn't describe the message format or any file format. Words can also be typed directly on the device through EDIT.

**Synthesis:** It is physical modelling of a vocal tract, not sample playback. The page says "Every sound comes from a simulated airway (lungs, vocal folds, throat, mouth and nose), not from samples." On the FM-1, the tract is a waveguide: the port keeps CHIMERA's vocal folds, anatomy, and noise sources, and "drives a waveguide tract instead" of CHIMERA's full airway physics, which ran at about twice the affordable cost.

**English:** Yes. The page lists an "English front end," a text-to-speech front end, and built-in CMU Pronouncing Dictionary entries. Korean and Russian lyrics and IPA input are listed as future work.

**Licence:** The page does not give one licence. It names several: the voice engine and voice files are MIT, the files based on fm1-base's template are MPL-2.0, the project's own files are MIT, and the firmware package is "MPL-2.0 AND MIT," with JieLi SDK files under Apache-2.0. The LICENSE file, which the page links, sets out which covers which files.

**Memory usage:** The page gives no RAM or flash figures. It reports CPU load instead: both cores stay under 60% of an audio block while singing and speaking. The flash chip holds 1 MB, and the built-in dictionary has about 480 words.
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Read Conductor CJK bitmap rendering details

`sed -n 1,15p host/conductor/render.py; echo ----; sed -n 15,40p firmware/conductor/app.c; echo ----; grep -n "DETAIL\|549\|bitmap\|0x0\|throughput\|bytes/s\|KB/s" host/conductor/PROTOCOL.md | head -30`

```text
"""Lines of any script drawn on the host, sent to the device as 1-bit pictures.

The FM-1's fonts are ASCII only, and a CJK font would not fit in the firmware, so the
host draws each DETAIL line (Chinese, Japanese, symbols) with a system font into a
240 x 16 bitmap and the device only paints it. One line packs into 549 bytes of 7-bit
SysEx: within fm1-base's 640-byte frame.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

W, H = 240, 16
BITS = W * H
PACKED = (BITS + 6) // 7  # 549
----
       OP_VOICE_DOWN, OP_VOICE_UP };
#define F_QUESTION 0x01u
#define F_REMOTE 0x02u
#define FW_MAJOR 0u
#define FW_MINOR 3u
#define NAME_MAX 20u
#define DETAIL_LINES 8u
#define LINE_MAX 36u
/* a DETAIL line drawn by the host (any script: our fonts are ASCII): 240 x 16 dots, 7 per byte, pixel i at bit
 * 6 - i % 7 of byte i / 7 (host/conductor/render.py) */
#define BMP_W 240u
#define BMP_H 16u
#define BMP_BYTES ((BMP_W * BMP_H + 6u) / 7u)

typedef struct {
    uint8_t state, kind, flags, seen;    /* seen: a DONE looked at (selected) since it came */
    uint16_t tag, age;
    char name[NAME_MAX + 1];
} slot_t;

static slot_t slots[NKEYS];
static hostlink_t link;
static struct {
    uint16_t total, hidden;
    char backend[9];
} meta;
----
18:- Frames are at most 46 bytes, except DETAIL_BMP (558 bytes, inside fm1-base's
28:| `04` | DETAIL | `slot`, `line` (0–7), `text` (≤ 36) |
32:| `08` | DETAIL_BMP | `slot`, `line` (0–7), 549 bytes: a 240 × 16 1-bit picture of the line, 7 dots a byte, dot *i* at bit `6 - i % 7` of byte `i / 7` (row-major). Firmware 0.2 and later; the host sends DETAIL text to 0.1 |
49:| `44` | SELECT | `slot`, optional `scroll` (KNOB 1 detents back, 4 lines each) — the host answers with DETAIL lines for it |
66:USB port when it hears the device on both, and sends DETAIL as text over Bluetooth
67:(a DETAIL_BMP is 558 bytes).
```

**FM-1 display summary**

- **Colour depth:** RGB565 (16-bit), high byte first. **[HW]**
- **Bus:** SPI1, write-only. CLK PC9, MOSI PC10, CS PC7 (active low), D/C PC8. Registers at `0x11D00`. **[HW]**
- **Refresh:** The page cites a 16.7 ms refresh period (about 60 Hz). There is no tearing-effect (TE) line, so hardware vsync sync isn't available. **[CODE]**
- **SPI speed:** The clock is the peripheral clock divided by `baud + 1`. At `baud` 4 (12 MHz) a 240×72 strip took 23 ms and tore. At `baud` 0 the measured effective rate is about 44 MHz. **[CODE] [HW]**
- **Framebuffer:** No framebuffer size is stated. The page describes drawing into a RAM canvas in 240×72 strips sent by DMA, with DMA sources required in RAM. From the stated figures, a strip is 34,560 bytes and a full 240×240 RGB565 frame would be 115,200 bytes (my arithmetic, not the page's).
- **Fonts:** Not covered. The page doesn't mention bitmap or vector fonts, font sizes, or libraries such as plutovg or u8g2. It only notes that fonts may be read from flash and that heavy drawing can push audio code out of the instruction cache.
- **Unicode / CJK:** Not mentioned.
- **Backlight (for context):** PA2, active low, shared with the key matrix enable, so it can't be switched off without also stopping the keys. **[HW] [?]**

**Tag key:** [HW] hardware-observed, [CODE] from firmware source or code notes, [?] unverified.

```text
**Summary: FM-1 flash storage**

- **Total flash:** "The FM-1 has one 1 MiB SPI NOR flash." This sentence has no evidence tag.
- **Free for user data:** The page gives no free-space total. The app slot is 581,564 bytes. Stock regions that hold user data are VM (`0x93000`-`0xE9000`) and USR (`0xEA000`-`0xFC000`) **[RE] [HW]**. Other firmwares reuse these areas, and the page warns that gaps may not be free.
- **Regions used for samples and user data:**
  - Felucca family: songs and sounds at `0x97000`-`0xDFFFF`, inside the stock VM range **[CODE]**.
  - Felucca settings and globals at `0xFC000`-`0xFEFFF`, panel calibration at `0xDC000`, autosave at `0xE5000`-`0xE6FFF`, and an FM6 voice bank at `0xE7000` **[CODE]**.
  - Baud Girl moves its VM area to `0xD9000` **[CODE]**.
  - Never store data at `0xE0000` onward, which is the update loader staging area. M-VAVE's V15 stages its loader at `0xE6000` **[CODE] [?]**.
- **Write and erase granularity:** Felucca uses 4 KiB sectors. Each object has two sectors (A/B), and the 32-byte header is written last, with the payload starting at offset 256 **[CODE]**. A 4 KiB erase takes tens of milliseconds on typical NOR parts, but this is not measured on the FM-1 **[?]**. Programming granularity is not stated.
- **Endurance:** Not mentioned.
- **Storage API:**
  - Felucca's `src/storage.c`, `hal/fm1_flash.h` and `hal/fm1_xip.h` **[CODE]**.
  - SDK flash driver calls: `enter_spi_code`, `norflash_erase`, `norflash_wait_ok`, `exit_spi_code` **[SDK]** (the page does not state the tag for this line).
  - fm1-base provides `plat_data*` with a data area and two more windows.
  - No object-number API is described. Objects are identified by a header with type, slot and sequence number.
- **Runtime reads of large data:** Yes. Data can be read through the XIP window (`0x02000120` maps to the start of app.bin) or by SPI reads. Data outside Felucca's plain window is decrypted on the fly **[CODE]**.
- **Bigger flash:** felucca-bsp has experimental code for a larger flash part. It has never run on a device, and how much the XIP window maps is unknown **[?]**.
- **External storage (m-card microSD):** Not mentioned.
```

  - Felucca's HAL says "ALNK0 I2S → external codec." [CODE]
  - FM-1-RE describes an "internal audio DAC." [RE]
  - The FM-1 resource hub describes an external codec on I2S, plus the chip's DACL pin as an auxiliary line. This is inferred from board photos, with no part number. [?]
  - Both may be partly true. [?]
- **Sample rate:** Felucca assumes 44,100 Hz. [CODE] The stock firmware reportedly runs at 44,118 Hz. [RE] The true rate is unconfirmed. [?]
- **USB audio rate:** The kmplngj Felucca fork offers 44.1 or 48 kHz, with 48 kHz on by default. [CODE]
- **Bit depth:** Internally, 24-bit left-justified samples in `int32_t` (L, R) pairs. [CODE] USB audio is 16-bit. [CODE]
- **Block size:** 256 stereo frames per half-buffer at 44.1 kHz, or 5.8 ms per block. Measure the worst-case block, not the average. [CODE]
- **Channels:** Stereo (L, R). Mono is not mentioned.
- **Built-in speaker / headphone out:** Not covered.
- **USB audio:** Felucca 1.0 and fm1-base expose the master output as a USB Audio Class 1 input, so a computer can record the FM-1 (16-bit stereo, 44.1 kHz). [CODE] fm1-base also supports playback from the computer through the FM-1. [CODE]
- **Sample playback from flash:** Not covered. The page only notes that flash erases run with interrupts off, so the audio buffer should be zeroed first. [CODE]
- **Output stage bring-up:** Felucca's `fm1_audio_init()` toggles GPIOs PC0, PC1, PC2, and PC6, including PC6 to switch the output stage on. The roles of these lines are undocumented. [CODE] [?]

````text
# Using both cores

The FM-1's chip has two cores. Your app runs on the first. The second core, when you turn it on, is a worker for
the render: in each audio block you hand it one job, do your own share on the first core, and wait for it. LOOM-8
renders half its voices and its effects this way. The second core comes from felucca-bsp's `chip/fm1_cpu1.h`
(Melodee's, by keremimo, under MPL-2.0 by agreement on felucca-bsp#5); fm1-base adds when it may start and the
calls in `include/plat.h`.

## Turn it on

Add this to your app's `fm1.toml`:

```toml
cpu2 = true
```

Two more keys change how it behaves. `tools/build.py` describes every key.

- `cpu2_fallback = true` keeps the FM-1 running on one core after the second core fails, until it is switched off.
  Without it, a failure restarts the FM-1 (see "When it fails").
- `cpu2_stack = 4096` gives the second core's jobs a bigger stack, in bytes (a multiple of 8, 1024 to 16384). The
  default is 2816. Use `plat_cpu2_stack()` to see how deep your jobs went.

Then start it in `app_init`. It can only start at power-on, before the audio and the timers, and `app_init` is that
moment:

```c
void app_init(void)
{
    /* ... */
    if (plat_cpu2_set(1) == 0)
        two_cores = 1;              /* else one core: do all the work yourself */
}
```

`plat_cpu2_set(1)` returns 0 when the second core runs, and -1 when it doesn't: it didn't answer, it was barred
after an earlier failure, or it's too late to start it. Your render has to work either way.

## Hand it a job
````
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base`

```text
## fm1-base feature summary

**Display and graphics:** The platform covers "the screen, drawing and fonts, panel, LEDs, audio, MIDI over USB and TRS, storage, the screen reader." Screen drawing is done in strips: `APP_CANVAS_PX` is set to `(240u * 48u)`, so apps draw in strips 48 rows high or less. The page doesn't name the drawing API.

**Fonts (tools/gen_font.py):** The page doesn't mention `tools/gen_font.py`, and it gives no font names, sizes, glyph ranges, or Unicode/CJK support. The only font-related details are:
- Lower case in the large fonts is enabled with `font_full = ["L"]`, which the table describes as "Lower case in the big fonts".
- Big fonts are a flash cost: `APP_BIG_FONT FONT_M` saves 20 KB in a WiFi build, since fm1-base's large font is used on the splash and panel screens.
- An app can supply its own fonts for system screens via `APP_SYS_TEXT`, which removes fm1-base's faces (18 KB in LOOM-8).

**Storage:**
- Saved objects use the store: `plat_store_size` and `plat_store_head` report on an object, which is saved "whole or not at all".
- Larger data goes through `plat_data*`, in "the data area and two more windows" (`PLAT_XDATA0`, `PLAT_XDATA1`), plus a third window, `PLAT_XDATA2` (0xFC000..0xFEFFF, about 12 KB), when `xdata2 = true`.
- Known sizes: the app flash slot is 581 KB, RAM for `.data` and `.bss` is 96 KB (128 KB with WiFi), and the RAM pool for big buffers is 336 KB. The size of the data area itself isn't given.

**Audio:** There is no sample-playback API on the page. Audio features are:
- App output goes to MASTER.
- USB audio in (recording the FM-1 over the cable) and USB audio out (a computer playing through the FM-1), with `plat_usb_play_gain` and `plat_usb_audio_full` as settings.
- Bluetooth audio to headphones and speakers (A2DP) via `plat_bta_*` calls.

**USB:**
- MIDI both ways over USB and TRS, plus Bluetooth MIDI. Message counts are available through `plat_midi_count`.
- SysEx is used by the screen reader and by RemoteFM1 for `.rfm1` files.
- USB audio in and out, as above.
- The FM-1 can read a connected USB host's product name (`plat_usb_host_name`) and exchange app commands (`APP_USB_CMD`).
- Backup and restore over USB are optional (`backup = true`).
- Mass storage isn't mentioned.

**Host simulator and emulator:** The host simulator runs the same app on a computer. A browser emulator runs the template at charlesvestal.github.io/fm1-base/emu/. The `.rfm1` format compiles the host simulator to WebAssembly for host apps such as RemoteFM1 for iOS. The page describes the simulator as running "the same app" as the FM-1.

**Licence:** The page says "MPL-2.0: an app built on it may use any licence." Felucca-based GPL-3.0 firmwares can move onto fm1-base and keep their licence. Relicensing to MPL-2.0 is needed only to link JieLi's Bluetooth or WiFi libraries. The own Bluetooth stack links nothing from JieLi. The page is in beta, and `include/plat.h` and `fm1.toml` settings may change before 1.0.
```
</details></tool-use>

106: * column it has just latched and takes the result at the next tick, so each key on those rows is read once per two
111: *   FM1_INPUT_ANALOG(col, rowbit, v, driven)   rowbit 3 = PA7, 4 = PA8; the key is FM1_KEYMAP[rowbit][col]
112: * With fm1_an.drive set, a key for which FM1_INPUT_DRIVE(col, rowbit) is nonzero (a held key) is read with its row
114: * reads the pill's resistance. The row is an input with its pull-up again at the next tick, before the rows are read.
115: * With fm1_an.probe set, a third frame phase reads the top row, PA6 (keys 20..26, columns 0..6, no converter of its
117: * low level, the more the harder it is pressed. FM1_INPUT_PROBE(col, rowbit, v, pressed) gets each reading, with
118: * the scan's last view of that key. A lit LED in a column lifts its keys' readings: FM1_INPUT_LED_OK(col, rowbit)

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/zvenson/zp12`

```text
**Sample rate and bit depth:** 12-bit samples at 26.04 kHz or 27.5 kHz. The Sound section describes them as "12-bit linear samples, packed, at 26.04 / 27.5 kHz."

**Compression:** The page mentions no lossy compression. The samples are "packed." Storage is also "stored fast, played slow": 45→33 per sound, and own samples at ×2 or ×2.7, which saves memory at the cost of grit.

**Playback:** Pitch changes the playback rate with a zero-order hold, so there is no interpolation and the aliasing is part of the sound. Channels 1–2 have a resonant low-pass filter, channels 3–6 a fixed low-pass, and 7–8 none.

**Memory and seconds:** The page gives no total capacity. It states:
- On the device, about 1.8 s at 26 kHz is free, with more from sloopDX's bank room.
- The editor says 2.5 s free, or 6.3 s with sloopDX's bank room. These figures differ from the device figure, and the page doesn't explain why.

**Flash addresses:** The samples live in flash starting at 0xC4000. This is a room that sloopDX leaves free. Stock SLOOP stores its own samples there, so back them up first. Recording erases flash first, shown as "ERASE %."

**Upload paths:**
- **On the machine, over USB:** The FM-1 appears to the computer as a speaker ("zp12 FM-1"). Set LFO (or GLO → SAMPLE), then press REC to record whatever the computer plays.
- **Browser editor:** It records from a microphone, audio interface or line-in, or accepts a dropped WAV. It then trims the sample, converts it to 26/27.5 kHz and 45→33, and puts it on a pad. The page's install and backup tools use Chrome or Edge over USB.
- The page does not say whether the browser path uses SysEx.

**Licence:** The project is GPL-3.0. Factory sounds are CC0, from VSCO-2 CE, VCSL and Sonic Pi. Bank D comes from SLOOP's hip-hop pack, and the E-piano is by Greg Sullivan under CC BY 3.0 (see `assets/samples-cc0/HIPHOP/CREDITS.txt`). The project is not affiliated with M-VAVE.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Charles Vestal */
/* An fm1-base firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1: one compilation unit for the platform and the app
 * (Felucca's layout: the chip and board layers are header-only, so everything that touches them is here).
 * An app's heavy code (its DSP) may be separate units at -O2 (fm1.toml: o2); this one is -Os. Order matters.
 *
 * The app provides, on the include path:
 *   app.h  its configuration (below) and the contract: app_init, app_render, app_panic, app_ui_init,
 *          app_frame, app_input_only, app_say; its store objects (OBJ_PANEL among them, OBJ_NOBJ) and their
 *          flash map APP_STORE_MAP
 *   app.c  the app itself (its own unity build), compiled here after the platform
 * Configuration, each with a default:
 *   APP_NAME "TEMPLATE"     on the splash, crash and safe-mode screens and for the screen reader
 *   APP_VERSION "DEV"       a release build passes its own (tools/build.py --release)
 *   APP_BLOCK 256           frames per audio half (5.8 ms at 44.1 kHz), the render's block
 *   FM1B_CDC 0              USB serial console (a second USB function; fm1.toml usb_console = true): the app's text over
 *                           plat_console_* (console.c)
 *   FM1B_UAC 1              USB audio input: the master output, recordable over the cable at 44.1 kHz (checked on an
 *                           FM-1 2026-10-16: no lost frame); FM1B_UAC_48K 0 (48 kHz too: needs the resampler's filter)
 *   FM1B_UAC_DEEP 0         1: the USB audio input keeps a half more in hand, for renders that take most of
 *                           their time (its 4 KB ring in the app's pool; 5.8 ms more latency)
 *   FM1B_UAC_RING_POOL 0    1: the USB audio input's 2 KB ring in the pool, its RAM left to the app
 *   FM1B_UAC_OUT 1          USB audio output: the computer plays through the FM-1, mixed after the app and after the
 *                           USB recording's tap, at MASTER and plat_usb_play_gain (device/uac_mix.h)
 *   FM1B_TRS 1              MIDI in on the TRS jack
 *   APP_TOUCH               velocity and pressure from the keys (lib/touch.h)
 *   FM1B_BLE 0              Bluetooth MIDI (fm1.toml ble = true; tools/build.py --no-ble leaves it out)
 *   FM1B_MIRROR 0           the screen and panel mirrored over USB (fm1.toml mirror = true: mirror.c)
 *   FM1B_MSC 0              disk mode: the FM-1 as a USB drive of the app's blocks (fm1.toml msc = true: msc.c)
 *   FM1B_BACKUP 0           backup and restore of the app's objects over USB (fm1.toml backup = true: backup.c)
 *   FM1B_RES 0              the resource region (fm1.toml resources = FILE: res.c; with backup)
 *   FM1B_CPU2 0             the second core (fm1.toml cpu2 = true: cpu2.c, felucca-bsp's fm1_cpu1.h)
 *   FM1B_CACHE_RAM 0        data-cache ways as RAM, 2, 4 or 7 (fm1.toml cache_ram_ways: plat_cache_ram, felucca-bsp's
 *                           fm1_cache_ram.h; set and tested in fm1_cstart, main_fm1.c) */
#include <stdint.h>
#include "plat.h"
#include "app.h"                  /* first: the scan's hooks below may call the app */
#ifdef APP_TOUCH
#include "touch.h"                /* velocity and pressure from the keys (lib/touch.c) */
#endif
#ifdef APP_KEY_SENSE              /* the keys' readings (plat_sense) to the app, by key: 0..26 */
#define FM1_KEY_OF(col, rowbit) ((uint32_t)FM1_KEYMAP[rowbit][col] - 14u)
#define FM1_INPUT_ANALOG(col, rowbit, v, driven) \
    (FM1_KEYMAP[rowbit][col] >= 14 ? app_key_sample(FM1_KEY_OF(col, rowbit), (v), fm1_ticks(), (int)(driven)) : (void)0)
#define FM1_INPUT_DRIVE(col, rowbit) (FM1_KEYMAP[rowbit][col] >= 14 && app_key_drive(FM1_KEY_OF(col, rowbit)))
#define FM1_INPUT_PROBE(col, rowbit, v, pressed) \
    (FM1_KEYMAP[rowbit][col] >= 14 ? app_key_probe(FM1_KEY_OF(col, rowbit), (v), (pressed)) : (void)0)
#define FM1_INPUT_LED_OK(col, rowbit) (FM1_KEYMAP[rowbit][col] < 14 || app_key_led_ok(FM1_KEY_OF(col, rowbit)))
#endif
#include "fm1_time.h"
#include "fm1_sys.h"
#include "fm1_irq.h"
#include "fm1_guard.h"
/* The input scan's rate (fm1.toml input_hz: FM1B_INPUT_HZ, felucca-bsp's FM1_INPUT_HZ: keys, knobs and LEDs, one column
 * a tick) and TIMER5's (FM1B_T5_HZ), which also polls USB and runs the app's tick. TIMER5 never runs slower than
 * 2 kHz, so USB is polled at 2 kHz or more at every input rate (MIDI as before, USB audio's one packet per 1 ms frame
 * with a poll to spare); with usb_audio_channels it stays at 10 kHz (the stream serviced every 0.1 ms). The scan then
 * runs on 1 tick in FM1B_T5_SCAN_DIV (input_hz 1000: every other 2 kHz tick).
 *   input_hz  TIMER5  scan       USB poll        app tick
 *   10000     10 kHz  each tick  each 5th: 2 kHz each 10th
```

````text
# Morse

The FM-1 as a pocket Morse code machine, on [fm1-base](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base). MIT.

- **KEY**: key on the piano keys, as a straight key (any key) or iambic A/B paddles
  (left half dit, right half dah), and read what you sent: as text, as each letter over
  the dits and dahs you keyed, or as bars to scale. A sidetone, or silence and the lights.
  Your speed, dah:dit ratio and the gaps inside letters as you go.
- **RHYTHM**: drills of short and long presses measured against the send speed, with a
  hint and a send speed that fits your hand.
- **TYPE**: three pages of keys (letters, digits and signs, CW phrases and prosigns such
  as `<SK>`) turned with OCT- / OCT+, three layouts, the code shown on the keys, LIVE
  (each key goes out) or COMPOSE (PLAY sends the line).
- **LISTEN**: plays on and on: Koch groups of your letters, common words, a made-up QSO,
  abbreviations with their meaning, sayings; shown, or hidden for copying.
- **PRACTICE**: flash cards a few minutes at a time. Leitner boxes per character, two
  cards each (recognise it, send it), new letters five at a time in Koch order, a round
  counter instead of days (the FM-1 has no clock through a power-off). Learning **by
  sound** is the default: no dots and dashes on the screen. By sight is a setting.
- **CHART**: the course as a grid coloured by how well you know each letter.
- **USB-MIDI**: keying out and in as note 0 on channel 1, the Vail adapter's format, so
  [Vail](https://vailmorse.com/) and its training tools take it. Text to and from
  `host/morse` over SysEx: see [`host/morse/PROTOCOL.md`](../../host/morse/PROTOCOL.md).

Docs (Traditional Chinese): [design](../../docs/dev/morse.md),
[cheatsheet](../../docs/dev/morse-cheatsheet.md).

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `morse.c` / `.h` | code table, PARIS / Farnsworth timing, text player, iambic keyer, adaptive decoder; no platform |
| `learn.c` / `.h` | flash cards: Leitner boxes, rounds, Koch groups, the four choices; no platform |
| `content.c` / `.h` | what LISTEN plays and TYPE's phrases: word lists, abbreviations, a QSO generator; no platform |
| `tone.c` / `.h` | two sine voices (sent, received) with 5 ms ramps, mute |
| `app.c` / `.h` | the pages, the 1 kHz tick (key, keyer, players, MIDI), storage, drawing |
| `tests/morse_test.c` | `just morse-unit`: the platform-free parts on the computer |
| `tests/basic.txt` | `just fw-test morse`: the whole app in fm1-base's host simulator |

## Build and test

```sh
just morse-unit          # morse.c, learn.c
just fw-test morse       # the app in the host simulator (screenshots in build/host/)
just fw-build morse      # build/morse.fwsc
just morse-emu           # in fm1-emu with the virtual USB cable
```

Flashing it is a firmware write: owner approval each time (see `AGENTS.md`).

Hearing and sending have their own speeds (K1/K2 and K4): Koch wants the characters heard
fast, a beginner's hand is slow. Presets in SETTINGS.

Storage: one record (settings and progress, about 300 bytes) at `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF`,
written when a round ends or is left, and 3 s after a setting changes. The panel
calibration at `0xDC000` is the platform's.
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* content: what the LISTEN page plays and the TYPE page's phrases. Lines made up on the spot from small lists:
 * groups of the letters you have open (Koch), common English words, a made-up QSO between two random stations,
 * the usual CW abbreviations with what they mean, and proverbs (old sayings, nobody's text). No platform, no libc. */
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

#define CT_LINE_MAX 120u

enum { LP_KOCH, LP_WORDS, LP_QSO, LP_ABBR, LP_TEXT, LP_N };
extern const char *const LP_NAME[LP_N];

typedef struct {
    uint32_t rng;
    uint8_t step;                        /* QSO: the next of its six lines */
    char a[8], b[8];                     /* QSO: the two calls */
    uint8_t na, nb, qa, qb, ra, rb;      /* QSO: their names, places, reports (indexes) */
    uint8_t last;                        /* the list entry given last (not twice in a row) */
} ct_gen_t;

void ct_init(ct_gen_t *g, uint32_t seed);
/* the next line of program p (LP_*) into out (CT_LINE_MAX + 1); open: the Koch letters open (KOCH); *gloss: what it
 * means, for an abbreviation (ABBR), else 0 */
void ct_line(ct_gen_t *g, int p, uint32_t open, char *out, const char **gloss);
const char *ct_gloss(const char *abbr);  /* what an abbreviation means, 0 when it is not in the list */

/* the TYPE page's phrase keys: one each, white keys left to right, then black */
#define CT_PHRASE_WHITE_N 16u
#define CT_PHRASE_BLACK_N 11u
extern const char *const CT_PHRASE_WHITE[CT_PHRASE_WHITE_N];
extern const char *const CT_PHRASE_BLACK[CT_PHRASE_BLACK_N];

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0
# Copyright (C) 2026 Kerem Kilic (Ellic Studio)
# Portions Copyright (C) 2026 Charles Vestal (LZMA, every SRAM load image)
# From Melodee (github.com/keremimo/melodee, tools/boot_audio.py), under MPL-2.0 here with permission; fm1-base's
# sections (.ram_text, .data: device/main_fm1.c fm1_cstart) and names, the rest as Melodee has it.
"""Pack the SRAM load images for boot and verify their decoder's XIP closure."""
import lzma
import re
import struct

MAGIC = 0x31414D4C  # LMA1: device/boot_lzma.h BOOT_LZMA_MAGIC
# Raw LZMA1, as boot_lzma.h decodes it: lc 1, lp 1, pb 1 (instructions are
# halfword aligned), with the end marker. The dictionary is the whole image.
FILTERS = [{'id': lzma.FILTER_LZMA1, 'preset': 9 | lzma.PRESET_EXTREME,
            'lc': 1, 'lp': 1, 'pb': 1, 'dict_size': 1 << 20}]
# The sections fm1_cstart unpacks, in their load order from _rt_load (device/app.ld, device/main_fm1.c)
SECTIONS = ('ramtext.bin', 'data.bin')


def pack(raw):
    """one load image: [MAGIC, packed bytes, raw bytes, 0], the stream, padded to a word"""
    data = lzma.compress(raw, format=lzma.FORMAT_RAW, filters=FILTERS)
    if lzma.decompress(data, format=lzma.FORMAT_RAW, filters=FILTERS) != raw:
        raise ValueError('boot image compression round trip failed')
    return struct.pack('<4I', MAGIC, len(data), len(raw), 0) + data + b'\0' * (-len(data) % 4)


def pack_images(blobs):

def ldr_head(dcrc, a, b, attr, name):
    body = struct.pack("<HIIBBH16s", dcrc, a, b, attr, 0, 0, name)
    return struct.pack("<H", crc16(body)) + body


def ldr_wrap(image):
    """ota.bin = outer JLFS head (32 B) + inner head (32 B, load address) +
    blocks [clen u32][dlen u32][LZ4 block], dlen 4096 except the last"""
    blocks = bytearray()
    for i in range(0, len(image), 4096):
        raw = image[i:i + 4096]
        c = lz4blk.compress(raw)
        if len(c) > 4096 or lz4blk.decompress(c) != raw:
            raise SystemExit(f"loader: block {i // 4096} does not compress below 4096 B")
        blocks += struct.pack("<II", len(c), len(raw)) + c
    inner = ldr_head(crc16(image), len(image), LOADER_LOAD, 0, LOADER_NAME)
    body = inner + bytes(blocks)
    return ldr_head(crc16(body), 0x20, len(body), 0x41, LOADER_NAME) + body


def build_loader():

    src = BSP / "loader"

```text
**m-card** is a microSD add-on board for the M-VAVE FM-1, about 30 × 25.2 mm.

- **Connection:** The board sits under the audio jacks and plugs between the FM-1's LCD and main board, so no soldering to the FM-1 is needed. The card shares the LCD's SPI bus through the 10-pin J12 connector. It taps MISO (shared with the LCD's D/C line), MOSI, CLK, and an inverted LCD chip select, plus 3.3 V and GND. Series resistors limit current and clock speed.
- **Status:** "untested prototype." The fit was checked with a paper template, but no board has been made or tested.
- **Firmware:** The card needs FM-1 firmware that supports it, and that support is still being worked on in the m-bootloader project. The page doesn't say which firmware can read the card or what filesystem it uses.
- **Capacity:** Not stated.
- **Licence:** The scripts, board design, and generated files are CC0 1.0 (public domain). KiCad's standard footprints and the 3D models used for renders are CC-BY-SA 4.0 and aren't part of the repository.
- **Audio streaming from SD:** Not covered. The only related guidance is that firmware should start the card at a slow SPI clock and raise it only after reads return good checksums.
```

- **Codec support:** The AC6951C datasheet lists SBC and AAC decoding for Bluetooth audio, and mSBC for voice calls. It does not mention WTG or SIN. Its DSP section lists SBC and AAC decoding for Bluetooth audio, and mSBC voice codecs for Bluetooth phone use.
- **WTG and tone files:** A third-party engineering blog for the AC696N and AC6966B says WTG prompt tones fail where MP3 works, and that the codec must be enabled in the configuration tool. The same post recommends MP3 for prompt tones. Because the post is not official, treat it as a practical report rather than a specification.
- **Custom tones:** A second blog post describes registering custom tone names and paths in tone_player.h and playing them through tone_play(). It is also unofficial.
- **Not found:** I found no mention of SIN as a tone format, and no official list of which formats tone_player accepts.

For authoritative answers, check the doc.zh-jieli.com AC63 pages directly, or the SDK's own tone_player source and configuration tool.

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Read mirror and usb.c SysEx transport notes

`cd /Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/M-VAVE_FM-1/third_party/fm1-base && sed -n 40,62p device/mirror.c; sed -n 360,410p bsp/chip/usb.c`

```text
 * colours all 0x0000):
 *   0nnnnnnn          n + 1 more pixels of the colour now (1..128)
 *   10iiiiii          the colour now = cache[i]; one pixel of it
 *   11nnnnnn hi lo    the colour now = hi << 8 | lo, put in cache[MR_HASH(colour)]; n + 1 pixels of it (1..64)
 *   MR_HASH(c) = (c * 40503) >> 10 & 63 (32-bit unsigned)
 * A flat UI with anti-aliased text codes to a few hundred bytes for most bands.
 *
 * Bandwidth first for the music: the frames go to their own ring (felucca-bsp usb.c mr_q, MRQ bytes), sent after the
 * SysEx ring (updates, backups, this file's input reports) and after the notes and clock, whole (nothing in the middle
 * of a SysEx message). A rectangle that does not fit in the ring now is dropped and its rows marked dirty; the
 * screen has no framebuffer to send them from later, so the app is asked to draw everything again (APP_REDRAW), and
 * what the viewer already has is skipped: a 32-bit hash of each MR_SEGW-pixel segment of each full-width row sent is kept;
 * a row drawn again sends only its segments that changed (a playhead moving: a narrow rect, not the band). So a busy
 * screen on a slow link loses frames, never the picture (with APP_REDRAW; without it, until the app draws there again).
 *
 * Input reports go in the SysEx ring (before the screen: the panel feels live), when something changed, 50 a
 * second at most (encoder turns add up meanwhile), and every MR_INPUT_IDLE_MS anyway.
 *
 * Cost: in the main loop only (lcd_blit / lcd_fill callers and mirror_step), never in the audio interrupt.
 *
 * Hooks (the platform's: unity.c on the device, host/plat_host.c in the simulator):
 *   mr_free()         bytes free in the frame ring
 *   mr_put(p, n)      one whole F0..F7 frame into the frame ring (it fits: mr_free checked)
    uint8_t sysex[16];
    uint8_t sx_len, sx_on;
    uint8_t rx_pend;             /* EP1 OUT packet seen, not yet taken (the MIDI ring was too full) */
    volatile uint8_t uboot_req;
    volatile uint8_t ota_req;    /* F0 22 24 35 7F F7: M-UPGRADE upgrade command (FELUCCA_OTA) */
} usb;

#if FELUCCA_OTA
/* M-UPGRADE SysEx (ota.c): the received frames (7-bit bytes between F0 and
 * F7) queued for the main loop, and a TX ring of SysEx event packets sent
 * before any MIDI. The queue: each frame its length (2 bytes, little-endian)
 * and its bytes, one after another; a frame that would run past the end goes
 * to the start instead (a length of 0 left where it would have been, or no
 * room for one: the reader goes on from the start), and one arriving when none
 * waits starts the buffer over (sx_epoch moves: the reader too), so a frame of
 * FELUCCA_SX_IN - 2 bytes always fits then. A frame with no room is dropped
 * (the host retries). The ISR writes and counts sx_made; the main loop reads
 * and counts sx_taken (sx_r, sx_ep its own). */
#ifndef FELUCCA_SX_IN
#if FELUCCA_LOADER
#define FELUCCA_SX_IN 4744u                       /* the update loader's fast install: a 4 KiB read's reply (4111 B,
                                                   * 4699 as it comes in, 7-bit packed) whole (loader.c checks it) */
#else
#define FELUCCA_SX_IN 648u                        /* an M-UPGRADE frame (640) whole; shorter ones several at once */
#endif
#endif
static uint8_t sx_frame[FELUCCA_SX_IN];
static uint32_t sx_pos, sx_at, sx_top, sx_w;      /* the ISR's: the frame's bytes so far, where they go, where it
                                                   * started (its length's place), where the next goes */
static uint8_t sx_from0, sx_moved;                /* it starts the buffer over; it went to the start */
static volatile uint32_t sx_made, sx_taken, sx_r; /* frames queued, taken; the oldest's place (the reader's) */
static volatile uint8_t sx_epoch, sx_ep;          /* the buffer started over (the ISR's), seen (the reader's) */
static volatile uint8_t sx_collect, sx_busy;
#ifndef SXQ
#define SXQ 64u                                   /* a firmware may give it more (a long screen-reader message whole) */
#endif
static uint32_t sx_out_q[SXQ];
static volatile uint32_t so_w, so_r;
#endif
#ifndef FELUCCA_MIRROR
#define FELUCCA_MIRROR 0
#endif
#if FELUCCA_MIRROR
/* a ring for big SysEx frames that must never hold up the music (a screen mirrored to the host): whole F0..F7
 * frames as bytes, sent last (after the SysEx ring and the notes), each whole: tx_mid says a frame is half sent
 * (nothing else goes in between) */
#ifndef MRQ
#define MRQ 4096u
#endif
static uint8_t mr_q[MRQ];
static volatile uint32_t mr_w, mr_r;
```
</details></tool-use>

搜尋結果顯示，WordBit 英語（自動學習）的核心是把鎖屏時間變成單字學習，功能上包括分級詞庫、例句、發音與測驗。不過多數資料來自第三方應用商店整理網站，且大多是英文頁面，並非官方繁中說明。

- **鎖屏學習**：有評論指出，每次開啟手機時，應用程式會覆蓋在鎖屏畫面上，提供多選題翻譯或單字卡。使用者可以關閉它回到鎖屏，也可以直接作答（You can choose to close the app to access the lock screen, or respond to the prompt.）。
- **分級詞庫**：官方的英文描述指出，詞彙依程度分類，詞庫超過一萬個單字，涵蓋初級到進階。另一篇評測也提到詞彙分類涵蓋 A1 至 C2 等級（there is a large vocabulary category bank to choose from, including vocabulary from each of the levels A1-C2）。
- **例句**：例句能展示單字在真實生活中的用法，以及常和哪些字搭配。
- **發音與音標**：有版本列出自動發音與音標顯示（Pronunciation - Automatic pronunciation and phonetic transcription）。針對台灣使用者，開發者也表示已更新為台灣用戶熟悉的 KK 音標。
- **其他功能**：包括測驗與拼寫模式、間隔重複（依遺忘曲線安排複習）以及同義詞、反義詞等延伸內容（interval repetition system (taking into account the forgetting curve)；Synonyms, Antonyms）。
- **費用**：官方描述寫明內容免費（Plus, all content is free!），但有第三方審查指出它採 freemium 模式，這點說法不一致，建議到 Google Play 或 App Store 確認。

注意：各語言版本的功能描述略有差異，上述內容多來自英文或其他語言版本的頁面，台灣繁中版本的實際功能請以應用商店當前說明為準。

The search results describe WordBit's lock-screen design and some features, but none of them mention spaced repetition, so I couldn't confirm that.

- **Lock-screen delivery:** When you unlock or check your phone, the app overlays the lock screen with either multiple-choice translation prompts or flashcards. You can dismiss it or answer it. (Each time you open your phone, the app will overlay the lock screen and present you with either multiple choice translations for a given word, or a flashcard.)
- **Study modes and alarms:** Practice includes matching games, multiple-choice questions, and spelling questions. Users can schedule study alarms for word matching, daily reports, and flashcard review at a chosen time.
- **Levels and content:** The developer's listing describes a vocabulary list running from A1 to C1, plus IELTS and TOEFL material and idioms. A third-party analysis site says the app categorizes over 10,000 words and phrases by proficiency level.
- **Daily review:** The Google Play listing says you can review as many words as you want within 24 hours. This reads as an unlimited daily review, not an interval-based schedule.
- **Cost and volume:** The developer's listing says the app is free and claims 100 words a day over 30 days, or 3,000 words a month.

Source reliability is mixed. The developer and store listings are promotional. The marlvel.ai pages are auto-generated analyses with low confidence scores, so treat their claims (such as the 10,000-word count) as unverified. For a clear answer on spacing algorithms, check the app's own documentation or a recent hands-on review.

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	Canonical instructions for any coding agent working in this repository.
4	`CLAUDE.md` only imports this file.
5	
6	## What this repo is
7	
8	A personal knowledge base for one **M-VAVE FM-1** pocket synth: resources,
9	flashing procedures, firmware notes (SLOOP first), usage notes, and the context
10	agents need to help operate the device safely. It also holds the owner's own
11	experimental firmware apps under `firmware/`, built on the `fm1-base` submodule.
12	
13	## Layout
14	
15	| Path | Purpose |
16	|---|---|
17	| `docs/` | The notes site (Zensical, published to GitHub Pages). Source of truth for curated knowledge. |
18	| `docs/device-log.md` | **Current state of the owner's physical unit**: flash chip, firmware, backups, flash history. Read it before any device operation; update it after. |
19	| `docs/getting-started/` | Install M-Flasher, back up, flash SLOOP, recovery, cautions. |
20	| `docs/firmware/` | Firmware map; one section per firmware worth using (`sloop/`). |
21	| `docs/agentic/` | Automation boundaries, M-Flasher CLI, emulator, skills, agent-controller firmwares. |
22	| `docs/resources.md` | Repo map and the **single version table** (with a "last checked" date). |
23	| `docs/notes/` | Dated usage notes and impressions. |
24	| `.specstory/references/` | Raw research exports (e.g. the ChatGPT conversation). **Unverified, lossy** — see below. |
25	| `.specstory/history/` | Agent session transcripts. Never edit. |
26	| `tools/`, `vendor/`, `build/` | Git-ignored. Emulator binaries and state, upstream checkouts, firmware build output. |
27	| `firmware/<app>/` | Own firmware apps (fm1-base template layout: `app.c`, `app.h`, `fm1.toml`, `tests/`). `firmware/hello` is the unmodified template, kept as the toolchain smoke test. |
28	| `firmware/conductor/` | Own agent-console firmware (MIT). Design: `docs/agentic/conductor.md`. |
29	| `firmware/morse/` | Own pocket Morse code machine (MIT): keyer, decoder, flash cards. Design: `docs/dev/morse.md`. |
30	| `firmware/common/` | Modules shared by own apps (`hostlink`, `ledfx`, `chime`; MIT). Apps add `include = ["../common"]`. |
31	| `host/conductor/` | Conductor's host daemon (Python, MIT): backends `hc`, `herdr`, `fake`. Protocol spec in `PROTOCOL.md`; tests in `host/tests/`. |
32	| `host/morse/` | Morse's host (Python, MIT): types what the FM-1 reads into the Mac, sends text for it to play. Protocol in `PROTOCOL.md` (keying is Vail-format MIDI note 0). |
33	| `third_party/fm1-base` | Git submodule (MPL-2.0, beta). Do not edit; bump deliberately. |
34	| `docs/dev/` | Firmware development environment and its current state. |
35	| `docs/hardware/flash-map.md` | Who stores what where in the 1 MiB flash, with sector diffs from this unit's backups. Update it when a new firmware is tried. |
36	| `docs/watch.md` | Ledger of upstream checks for things on hold (m-bootloader on the new chip, SLOOP 3). Append, do not rewrite. |
37	| `backups/`, `downloads/` | Git-ignored. Flash backups and downloaded installers/firmware. Never commit. Off-machine copies of backups go to GitHub Release assets (`just fm1-backup-release`). |
38	| `zensical.toml`, `scripts/check-docs-site.py`, `Justfile` | Site config, output checker, task runner. |
39	| `.agents/skills/` | Installed agent skills (`zensical-site-bootstrap`). |
40	
41	## Commands
42	
43	```sh
44	just docs-build        # uv run zensical build --strict
45	just docs-check        # build, then scripts/check-docs-site.py
46	just docs-serve        # preview on 127.0.0.1:8000 (just docs-serve 8769 for another port)
47	
48	just emu-fetch         # fm1-emu into tools/fm1-emu/ (git-ignored), digest-verified
49	just emu-run FILE [CHIP]   # play a .fwsc in a window; CHIP defaults to uc25hq80 (this unit)
50	just emu-shot FILE [CHIP] [MS]  # headless boot: LCD image + flash write count
51	just agtdeck-fetch     # Agent Deck package, digest + attestation verified
52	just fm1-fetch-more    # CTL-1, ChoralRoot, RemoteFM1 packages, digest-verified
53	just emu-rehearse PKG BACKUP.bin  # boot PKG's firmware over a real backup in the emulator
54	just agtdeck-doctor    # Agent Deck host daemon self-check (clones upstream into vendor/)
55	just agtdeck-sim       # Agent Deck daemon without an FM-1 (interactive; prints frames)
56	just agtdeck-run       # daemon against a MIDI device: real unit, or `just emu-run … --usb`
57	just fm1-versions      # latest upstream releases, to refresh docs/resources.md and docs/watch.md
58	
59	just cond-test         # Conductor daemon unit tests
60	just cond-sim [BACKEND]    # daemon with a text stand-in for the FM-1 (fake, hc, herdr)
61	just cond-it           # hc end to end with two fake agents (label conductor-test=1), cleaned up after
62	just cond-emu [CHIP]   # Conductor firmware in fm1-emu with the virtual USB cable
63	just cond-run [BACKEND]    # daemon against a CONDUCTOR MIDI device (emulator or real unit)
64	just fw-common-test    # firmware/common unit tests on this computer (hostlink BLE packets)
65	
66	just morse-unit        # firmware/morse platform-free parts (morse.c, learn.c) on this computer
67	just morse-test        # Morse host unit tests (protocol vectors shared with tests/basic.txt)
68	just morse-emu [CHIP]  # Morse firmware in fm1-emu with the virtual USB cable
69	just morse-type [--dry-run]  # what the FM-1 reads, typed into the focused Mac app
70	just morse-send TEXT   # the FM-1 plays TEXT as received
71	
72	just fw-setup          # submodules + Python tools (needs `brew install libraqm`)
73	just fw-test [APP]     # host simulator build + tests/basic.txt; no toolchain, no hardware
74	just fw-build [APP]    # device package via JieLi toolchain in Docker (see docs/dev/ for current blockers)
75	
76	just fm1-fetch         # download M-Flasher + SLOOP into downloads/, verify against release digests
77	just fm1-find          # read-only: units in download mode / on USB MIDI
78	just fm1-info          # read-only: what is on the unit
79	just fm1-backup LABEL  # read-only: full-flash backup into backups/<date>-LABEL/
80	just fm1-verify-backups
81	just fm1-download-mode # mode switch
82	just fm1-restart       # mode switch
83	just fm1-flash FILE    # WRITE: owner runs this, never an agent without approval
