```text
The search didn't turn up the pschatzmann arduino-codec2 repository or any 1200 bps benchmark. It did surface one relevant RP2040 Codec2 port, the talkberry project.

- **Memory footprint:** The talkberry README reports a build with about 128 KB of flash used (6.14% of 2 MB) and about 88 KB of RAM used (33.83% of 256 KB). Memory region Used Size Region Size %age Used FLASH: 128684 B 2 MB 6.14% RAM: 88676 B 256 KB 33.83%
- **Trade-off:** The same README says moving the FFT lookup tables from constant storage into RAM costs roughly 30% of RAM but gains about 9% speed and 12% flash.
- **Approach:** The port uses fixed-point arithmetic to speed up execution on constrained chips like the RP2040.
- **API:** Usage is a one-time init call followed by a decode call that takes an encoded packet and returns raw signed audio.
- **Hardware baseline:** The RP2040 has 264 KiB RAM and 2 MiB flash (up to 16 MiB), per the RIOT OS board documentation.

I found no benchmark for the 1200 bps mode specifically, and the talkberry figures don't say which Codec2 mode they were measured with. A follow-up search on the pschatzmann repository or Codec2 1200 bps benchmarks on microcontrollers may be needed.
```

```text
- **Codec2 mode:** 1300 bps. The README says it "Supports 1300bps mode."
- **Fixed-point:** Yes. The port aims to speed up execution by "implementing the math with fixed-point arithmetic."
- **Flash/RAM:**

| Configuration | Flash | RAM |
|---|---|---|
| Initial build | 380,284 B (18.13%) | 11,396 B (4.35%) |
| FFT LUTs moved to RAM | 128,684 B (6.14%) | 88,676 B (33.83%) |

  Moving the LUTs to RAM trades roughly 30% more RAM for about 9% more speed and 12% less flash.
- **CPU load / decode time:** The README reports about 25% total CPU usage, "plenty of room for other code." It gives no per-frame decode time. The only timing is an encoding benchmark: 0.473 s to encode 1 s of audio in fixed-point, versus 3.542 s in floating-point, on one core at 125 MHz.
- **Encoder/decoder:** Decoder only. The README says the library provides encoding and decoding functions, "well, just decoding for now," and a TODO item reads "Finish the encoder."
- **Licence:** LGPL-2.1 (GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 or, at your option, any later version).
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/pschatzmann/arduino-simple-tts`

```text
**Approach:** The library plays pre-recorded audio rather than synthesizing speech. Text-generation classes such as `NumberToText`, `TimeToText`, and `NumberUnitToText` turn input into words, and those words select the matching recordings. The README says the words are used to "identify the pre-recorded audio files." Output goes through I2S, built on the Arduino Audio Tools.

**Codec:** MP3. The examples use `MP3DecoderHelix` from arduino-libhelix, which the README describes as "A **MP3 and AAC Decoder** from Realnetworks."

**Memory:** The README gives one example, a sketch with talking time and number support that stores all audio as MP3 in PROGMEM on an ESP32:
- "Sketch uses 740438 bytes (23%) of program storage space."
- "Global variables use 23632 bytes (7%) of dynamic memory, leaving 304048 bytes for"

The author says this leaves "plenty of headroom."

**Supported boards:** The page doesn't include a list. The only board named is the ESP32, in the memory example.

**Licence:** GPL-3.0, shown in the sidebar and as a "GPL-3.0 license" link in the repository files.

**Vocabulary storage:** The prerecorded MP3 files are stored in program memory (PROGMEM) through `ExampleAudioDictionaryValues`, loaded into an `AudioDictionary`. The README notes that audio can instead be stored "on an SD drive" and mentions optional SdFat support.
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/festvox/flite`

```text
**License**

The page does not include the license text. It links to a "License" section and lists a `COPYING` file, but neither is reproduced here. The only licensing-related text is the copyright notice: "Copyright Carnegie Mellon University 1999-2022" and "All rights reserved."

**Footprint and size**

- Comparison table (Flite vs. Festival): core code 60K vs. 2.6M; lexicon 600K vs. 5M; diphone 1.8M vs. 2.1M; runtime "<1M" vs. 16-20M.
- Memory: for standard diphone voices, peak runtime memory is roughly under twice the size of the generated waveform, which "effectively means under 1M" on 32-bit architectures.
- Voices, lexicons, and language data are compiled as const data that can sit in ROM: "All voices, lexicons and language model data are const and in the text segment (i.e. they may be put in ROM)."
- Because this data is linked at compile time, startup delay is negligible.
- Voices can also load from a single file, locally or over HTTP.
- The project describes Flite as "the answer to the complaint that Festival is too big, too slow, and not portable enough."

**Embedded and small devices**

- Flite is designed for "very small devices, such as phones, portables, PDAs," and also for large servers handling many ports.
- It is all ANSI C, with no C++ or Scheme.
- Reported platforms include Android devices, OpenWrt devices, and an iPaq running Linux.
- The project cross-compiled for various ARM and MIPS processors. Big-endian or new byte-order architectures may need field reordering.
- The project reports about 9.79× real-time speed on an iPaq using 16 kHz diphones, versus about 70.6× on a 500 MHz PIII.
- Audio output can be disabled with `-DCST_AUDIO_NONE` for devices without audio support.
- WASI (WebAssembly) support is experimental.
- PalmOS and Windows CE are no longer actively supported.
```

Before writing up, one design-critical gap: whether the FM-1 has a real-time clock. Day-based SRS depends on it.

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-17 18:21:52Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Clocks-and-Power.html`

```text
**Short answer: the page doesn't say.** It doesn't mention a real-time clock, a 32 kHz crystal, sleep modes, or what "off" means. Anything beyond the points below would be guesswork.

- **RTC:** Not covered. The only crystal-based timer is TIMER4, which runs from the 24 MHz crystal and "Wraps every 178.9 s; use unsigned differences." It's an interval timer, not a wall clock. **[CODE]**
- **Retention across reset:** The always-on domain is documented, but only for resets. "The always-on P33 domain keeps these across a reset." **[HW]** The page doesn't say whether this holds across a full power-off.
- **Sleep and power-down:** No information. The page doesn't describe sleep modes or whether the device stays powered when switched off.
- **Battery:** The battery divider is on ADC channel 3 (PB1). "Never drive or pull PB1 low": held low for 8 s, it resets the chip. **[CODE]** The page gives no battery life figures. It says the higher core voltages cost battery life, but "not measured here." **[HW]**

For RTC, sleep, and off-state behaviour, check [Open Questions](/fm1-dev-wiki/Open-Questions.html) or measure it on hardware.
```
</details></tool-use>

# FM-1 vocabulary app (WordBit-style, spaced repetition, Anki import): research findings

Researched 2026-11-18. Tags: **[V]** means I checked it at the source (a page, a source file, an API or the catalog JSON). **[U]** means unverified, or the claim comes from a third party. **[E]** means my own arithmetic or inference.

**Bottom line:**
- No FM-1, SMK-37 or other JieLi firmware does flashcards, vocabulary or Anki today. But the two hardest parts already exist on this hardware: English speech in small flash, and an owner-built MIT flashcard app with Leitner scheduling.
- Raw recorded audio for thousands of words won't fit in the 1 MiB flash. Synthesised speech (LPC) or host audio over USB will.
- Read Anki files with your own small reader (zip + zstd + SQLite), and add AnkiConnect for two-way sync.

## 1. FM-1 ecosystem

The closest prior art is your own Morse trainer, `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/M-VAVE_FM-1/docs/dev/morse.md`:
- MIT, built on fm1-base.
- Leitner boxes 0–5; box n comes back every 2ⁿ rounds.

### Relevant packages: speech and words [V]
| Package | What it proves | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| **SPELLBOX** ([repo](https://github.com/pjac1810/spellbox)) | A Speak & Spell clone. Software LPC speech chip (10-coefficient lattice filter at 8 kHz). Words and 42 phonemes were spoken by espeak-ng at build time and converted to LPC frames. Has a SPEAK mode for arbitrary text: about a 12,000-word compressed dictionary, then suffix handling, then letter-to-sound rules (the rules alone get ~83% of phonemes right). Keys F3..Z are A–Z, G5 is Enter. Word lists come from wordfreq. Old chip only; the installer page showed "Build failed". | GPL-3.0 |
| **Speak37** ([repo](https://github.com/genkigenki/Speak37); FM-1 build `speak37-fm1-1.0.fwsc`) | Same espeak-ng → TMS5220-style LPC approach. **2759 words = 390 KB of frames, 19 minutes of speech** (≈141 B per word [E]). The FM-1 build holds 2576 words. It found 10 ms frames are needed for intelligibility. Word lists from FrequencyWords. | GPL-3.0; word lists CC BY-SA 4.0 |
| **386DX** ([repo](https://github.com/seajaysec/386-DX-FM1-KaraokeBot), [engine](https://github.com/seajaysec/386-DX-ENGINE)) | Sings typed lines. Uses eSpeak NG's English front end plus Klatt formant synthesis at 11,025 Hz, compiled in, no allocation after startup, fits in 96 KB RAM. | GPL-3.0 |
| **FM-1 Chimera Vocal** ([repo](https://github.com/shan-sherif/fm-1-chimera-vocal)) | Physical vocal-tract model. English front end with CMUdict entries (~480 words). Words typed in a browser are sent over USB SysEx. Both cores stay under 60% load. | Voice engine MIT, fm1-base parts MPL-2.0 (the catalog shows "null") |
| **EVIL GENIUS** ([repo](https://github.com/Quixotic7/evilgenius)) | SAM speech: 54 words, "or type your own". The package is 1,042,154 B. | MPL-2.0; SAM's own licence status is deferred to its LICENSING.md [U] |
| Miku-FM, MONK-1, FMLarynx | Japanese singing and formant voices | GPL-3.0 |

### Sample playback is proven [V]
These play PCM samples from flash: zp12, PIGEON, Bubba Machine, ECHOFIELD (MIT), Mini-Grain, XMOD, LUXR, Flyfish, M-PYRE, Manta, CHOPPAH and Amenity.

The catch is size. zp12 stores 12-bit samples at 26–27.5 kHz starting at `0xC4000` and has only **about 1.8 s free on the device** (2.5–6.3 s according to its editor) ([zp12](https://github.com/zvenson/zp12)). Carnac OS needs a separate installer just for its PCM waves.

### Developers' Wiki facts
- **Hardware** ([Hardware Overview](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Hardware-Overview.html)) [V]:
  - JieLi AC791N, two cores, 320–360 MHz.
  - Single-precision hardware float; double precision is emulated in software and slow.
  - 578 KB SRAM, of which firmware uses a 512 KB window.
  - 1 MiB SPI NOR flash, executed in place.
  - 240×240 RGB565 screen (ST7789-class), 27 keys, 14 buttons, 7 encoders.
  - BLE and WiFi. **No SD card.**
- **Audio** ([Audio Output](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Audio-Output.html)) [V]: 44.1 kHz stereo, 256-frame blocks. fm1-base can play audio sent from a computer out of the FM-1.
- **Speaker** [V, local docs]: the FM-1 has a built-in speaker, and host USB audio comes out of it with fm1-base firmwares (`docs/index.md`, `docs/firmware/ctl-1/index.md`). That makes a "pronounce with host text-to-speech while tethered" mode possible.
- **Storage** ([Flash Storage](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Flash-Storage.html), [fm1-base](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base)) [V]:
  - The app slot is 581,564 B; your Morse app uses ~128 KB of it.
  - Large data can be read in place through the XIP window.
  - fm1-base gives 96 KB of RAM for globals and a 336 KB pool for big buffers.
  - Felucca-family data sits at `0x97000`–`0xDFFFF`, and other firmwares share it.
- **Fonts** [V]:
  - The wiki's [Display](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Display.html) page says nothing about fonts or CJK.
  - fm1-base's `tools/gen_font.py` renders BDF/TTF into **contiguous codepoint ranges (32..126)** with 4-bit alpha and optional trimming and Huffman packing. Supporting Chinese would need a new sparse glyph table.
  - No catalog firmware renders Chinese text.
- **Clock** [V/U]: no real-time clock is documented ([Clocks and Power](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Clocks-and-Power.html) lists only a 24 MHz timer that wraps every 179 s). Day-based scheduling therefore needs the date from the host at sync time, or it has to count sessions the way Morse does.
- **m-card microSD** ([repo](https://github.com/jvitkauskas/m-card), CC0) [V]: an "untested prototype"; firmware support is still being worked on in m-bootloader.

## 2. WordBit (Traditional Chinese edition, `net.wordbit.entw`)
Google Play wouldn't render, so this comes from the [AppGoblin mirror](https://appgoblin.info/apps/net.wordbit.entw) and the [All Language Resources review](https://www.alllanguageresources.com/wordbit/). Treat it as [U].
- **Lock-screen learning:** a card or multiple-choice question appears every time the phone is unlocked; you can dismiss it or answer.
- **Content:** 30,000+ words, phrases and sentences from A1 to C2, plus TOEFL/IELTS/GRE and topic lists. Each word has example sentences, related words, synonyms and antonyms, KK phonetics, and text-to-speech pronunciation.
- **Self-sorting:** words go into unknown, confusing, known and error-note piles.
- **Review:** "spaced repetition (forgetting curve)", reviewing words from 1, 7, 15 and 30 days earlier, plus a daily repeat goal.
- **Quizzes:** matching, multiple choice and spelling.
- **Price:** free with ads (1.3M+ installs).

How it maps to the FM-1 [E]:
- The "glance on unlock" moment becomes "show a card at power-on".
- The four piles become four key presses, which also double as the review grades.
- Spelling quizzes can use SPELLBOX's A–Z key layout.

## 3. Anki import
**Package format**, checked against Anki's source ([meta.rs](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/blob/main/rslib/src/import_export/package/meta.rs), [import_export.proto](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/blob/main/proto/anki/import_export.proto)) [V]:
- An `.apkg` is a zip file.
- If it contains a `meta` file, that file is a protobuf `PackageMetadata{version}`. Version 3 ("latest") means a **zstd-compressed** `collection.anki21b` (schema V18), media files that are also zstd-compressed, and a `media` index stored as protobuf `MediaEntries{name,size,sha1}`.
- Without `meta`: if `collection.anki21` is present it's the legacy-2 format, otherwise `collection.anki2` (both schema V11, not compressed, media index as a JSON map).
- `.colpkg` uses the same package code [U on the details].

**Database schema** ([AnkiDroid wiki](https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/wiki/Database-Structure)) [V]:
- `notes.flds` holds the field values separated by `0x1f`.
- Field names live in the `fields` table (schema 15 and later, [V]) or in the `col.models` JSON (V11).
- `cards` has `type`, `queue`, `ivl`, `factor` (‰), `reps`, `lapses` and `due`. The meaning of `due` depends on the card: new = queue position; learning = epoch seconds; review = days since `col.crt`.
- `revlog` has `id` (ms), `cid`, `ease`, `ivl`, `lastIvl`, `factor`, `time` and `type`.
- **FSRS memory state** is in the `cards.data` JSON: `s` (stability), `d` (difficulty), `dr`, `decay`, `lrt` ([data.rs](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/blob/main/rslib/src/storage/card/data.rs)) [V].

**Host-side readers** (PyPI and GitHub, [V] unless marked):
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| Your own reader: `zipfile` + `zstandard` + `sqlite3` + a tiny protobuf decoder | **Recommended for an MIT repo.** The format is small enough to read directly. |
| `anki` 26.9.4 (2026-11-04) | Official, reads everything, but heavy and **AGPL-3.0-or-later** (the PyPI licence field is empty; the source headers say AGPL). Use it only as an optional dependency, never copy it into the repo. |
| `ankipandas` 0.3.15 (MIT, 2023) | Reads a local profile's database; its docs don't mention anki21b. |
| `anki-export` 0.1.4 (MIT, 2022) | Probably handles only the legacy formats [U]. |
| `genanki` (MIT) | Writes decks only, can't read them. |
| [anki-apkg-parser](https://github.com/74Genesis/anki-apkg-parser) (Node, MIT, 2026-10) | Explicitly supports `collection.anki21b`. |
| `spacedrep` 0.5.0 (MIT) | CLI and MCP server with `.apkg` import/export and FSRS; I didn't test it. |

**AnkiConnect** ([sourcehut](https://git.sr.ht/~foosoft/anki-connect); the GitHub copy is archived) [V]:
- GPL-3.0+. Needs **Anki Desktop 26.08 or later, running**.
- Two APIs: v1 JSON-RPC at `127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1` (94 methods) and the legacy action API (122 actions).
- Useful legacy actions:
  - `cardsInfo` returns fields, factor, interval, type, queue, due, reps, lapses, left, mod.
  - `getReviewsOfCards` and `cardReviews` return review-history rows.
  - `answerCards` (ease 1–4) can push FM-1 reviews back into Anki.
  - `insertReviews` imports history without rescheduling.
  - `setDueDate` changes a card's due date.
- v1 exposes `fsrsMemory{difficulty, stabilityDays}`.
- Best use: two-way sync while tethered; use `.apkg` files for offline import.
- Caveat [E]: `answerCards` probably records the answer at sync time, not when it happened on the FM-1. Check this before relying on it.

## 4. Scheduling algorithms small enough for the FM-1
| Algorithm | State per card [E] | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Leitner | 2–3 B (box number + day/round) | Already in Morse. Python reference: [leitner-box](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/leitner-box) (MIT). |
| SM-2 | ~6–7 B (ease, interval, reps, due day) | Python reference: [sm-2](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/sm-2) (MIT). Note `anki-sm-2` is AGPL. |
| FSRS-6 | ~8–12 B with floats, ~6 B quantised to 16-bit (stability, difficulty, state/step, due, last review) | 21 parameters (defaults are in [py-fsrs scheduler.py](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/py-fsrs), MIT). Needs only `expf` and `powf`, so use single-precision floats. |

**There's no official embedded C version of FSRS** [V]:
- [rs-fsrs-c](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/rs-fsrs-c) is a proof-of-concept binding, and [fsrs-rs-c](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/fsrs-rs-c) is a dynamic library. Both are MIT and both wrap Rust.
- The practical path is to hand-port py-fsrs's scheduler (a few hundred lines) and test it against py-fsrs's reference vectors. Several closed-source apps in [awesome-fsrs](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/awesome-fsrs) did exactly this.
- Anki's own FSRS (`fsrs-rs`) is BSD-3.
- **Recommendation:** run FSRS on the device and seed it from the `s`/`d` values in `cards.data`.

## 5. Embedded flashcard prior art
- [stackmemo](https://github.com/rberenguel/stackmemo) (MIT): M5Stack Core2, MicroPython + LVGL, SM-2. It has no clock, so cards are just sorted by interval — the same problem the FM-1 has.
- [Adafruit MagTag flashcards](https://learn.adafruit.com/magtag-flashcards.md?view=all) (code in an MIT repo): cards in `deck.json`, Forgot/Good buttons, re-queues misses within a session, no real spaced repetition. It **dropped kanji because the glyphs didn't fit in memory**.
- TuftyKani ([thread](https://community.wanikani.com/t/my-take-on-a-pocket-sized-wanikani-gadget/74649)): RP2350 badge for WaniKani reviews. Caches the review queue offline and syncs results back later. It stored kanji as PNGs because it had no CJK font. No licence stated.
- [RmAnki](https://github.com/Jayy001/RmAnki) (GPL-3.0, reMarkable, syncs through AnkiConnect) and [KAnki](https://github.com/crizmo/KAnki) (Kindle, no licence).
- The "Word Box" ESP32 e-ink device: hackster returned 403, so not verified.

## Flash budget (my estimates [E])
- **Recorded audio doesn't fit.** At 8 kHz 8-bit, about 5 KB per word, so ~15 MB for 3,000 words, against ~2–6 s of free sample room. It only becomes possible if m-card ever works.
- **LPC speech fits a few thousand words.** At Speak37's ~141 B per word, 3,000 words is ~420 KB. That's tight alongside everything else, so speak only the top N words with LPC and spell the rest letter by letter (Speak37 does this), or use SPELLBOX-style letter-to-sound rules for any word.
- **Text and glyphs:**
  - A word with KK phonetics and a Traditional Chinese gloss is ~40 B; adding an example sentence brings it to ~100 B. So 3,000 words is 120–300 KB before compression.
  - Only the characters the deck actually uses need storing: ~2,500 Chinese characters at 1 bit per pixel is ~45 KB at 12×12 or ~80 KB at 16×16.
- **Scheduling state:** 3,000 cards × 8 B is 24 KB, so 6 sectors, or 12 with the A/B copies. Write it once at the end of each session.

<result># FM-1 vocabulary app (WordBit-style, spaced repetition, Anki import): research findings

Researched 2026-11-18. Tags: **[V]** means I checked it at the source (a page, a source file, an API or the catalog JSON). **[U]** means unverified, or the claim comes from a third party. **[E]** means my own arithmetic or inference.

**Bottom line:**
- No FM-1, SMK-37 or other JieLi firmware does flashcards, vocabulary or Anki today. But the two hardest parts already exist on this hardware: English speech in small flash, and an owner-built MIT flashcard app with Leitner scheduling.
- Raw recorded audio for thousands of words won't fit in the 1 MiB flash. Synthesised speech (LPC) or host audio over USB will.
- Read Anki files with your own small reader (zip + zstd + SQLite), and add AnkiConnect for two-way sync.

These play PCM samples from flash: zp12, PIGEON, Bubba Machine, ECHOFIELD (MIT), Mini-Grain, XMOD, LUXR, Flyfish, M-PYRE, Manta, CHOPPAH and Amenity.

The catch is size. zp12 stores 12-bit samples at 26–27.5 kHz starting at `0xC4000` and has only **about 1.8 s free on the device** (2.5–6.3 s according to its editor) ([zp12](https://github.com/zvenson/zp12)). Carnac OS needs a separate installer just for its PCM waves.

### Developers' Wiki facts
- **Hardware** ([Hardware Overview](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Hardware-Overview.html)) [V]:
  - JieLi AC791N, two cores, 320–360 MHz.
  - Single-precision hardware float; double precision is emulated in software and slow.
  - 578 KB SRAM, of which firmware uses a 512 KB window.
  - 1 MiB SPI NOR flash, executed in place.
  - 240×240 RGB565 screen (ST7789-class), 27 keys, 14 buttons, 7 encoders.
  - BLE and WiFi. **No SD card.**
- **Audio** ([Audio Output](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Audio-Output.html)) [V]: 44.1 kHz stereo, 256-frame blocks. fm1-base can play audio sent from a computer out of the FM-1.
- **Speaker** [V, local docs]: the FM-1 has a built-in speaker, and host USB audio comes out of it with fm1-base firmwares (`docs/index.md`, `docs/firmware/ctl-1/index.md`). That makes a "pronounce with host text-to-speech while tethered" mode possible.
- **Storage** ([Flash Storage](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Flash-Storage.html), [fm1-base](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base)) [V]:
  - The app slot is 581,564 B; your Morse app uses ~128 KB of it.
  - Large data can be read in place through the XIP window.
  - fm1-base gives 96 KB of RAM for globals and a 336 KB pool for big buffers.
  - Felucca-family data sits at `0x97000`–`0xDFFFF`, and other firmwares share it.
- **Fonts** [V]:
  - The wiki's [Display](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Display.html) page says nothing about fonts or CJK.
  - fm1-base's `tools/gen_font.py` renders BDF/TTF into **contiguous codepoint ranges (32..126)** with 4-bit alpha and optional trimming and Huffman packing. Supporting Chinese would need a new sparse glyph table.
  - No catalog firmware renders Chinese text.
- **Clock** [V/U]: no real-time clock is documented ([Clocks and Power](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/Clocks-and-Power.html) lists only a 24 MHz timer that wraps every 179 s). Day-based scheduling therefore needs the date from the host at sync time, or it has to count sessions the way Morse does.
- **m-card microSD** ([repo](https://github.com/jvitkauskas/m-card), CC0) [V]: an "untested prototype"; firmware support is still being worked on in m-bootloader.

## 2. WordBit (Traditional Chinese edition, `net.wordbit.entw`)
Google Play wouldn't render, so this comes from the [AppGoblin mirror](https://appgoblin.info/apps/net.wordbit.entw) and the [All Language Resources review](https://www.alllanguageresources.com/wordbit/). Treat it as [U].
- **Lock-screen learning:** a card or multiple-choice question appears every time the phone is unlocked; you can dismiss it or answer.
- **Content:** 30,000+ words, phrases and sentences from A1 to C2, plus TOEFL/IELTS/GRE and topic lists. Each word has example sentences, related words, synonyms and antonyms, KK phonetics, and text-to-speech pronunciation.
- **Self-sorting:** words go into unknown, confusing, known and error-note piles.
- **Review:** "spaced repetition (forgetting curve)", reviewing words from 1, 7, 15 and 30 days earlier, plus a daily repeat goal.
- **Quizzes:** matching, multiple choice and spelling.
- **Price:** free with ads (1.3M+ installs).

How it maps to the FM-1 [E]:
- The "glance on unlock" moment becomes "show a card at power-on".
- The four piles become four key presses, which also double as the review grades.
- Spelling quizzes can use SPELLBOX's A–Z key layout.

## 3. Anki import
**Package format**, checked against Anki's source ([meta.rs](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/blob/main/rslib/src/import_export/package/meta.rs), [import_export.proto](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/blob/main/proto/anki/import_export.proto)) [V]:
- An `.apkg` is a zip file.
- If it contains a `meta` file, that file is a protobuf `PackageMetadata{version}`. Version 3 ("latest") means a **zstd-compressed** `collection.anki21b` (schema V18), media files that are also zstd-compressed, and a `media` index stored as protobuf `MediaEntries{name,size,sha1}`.
- Without `meta`: if `collection.anki21` is present it's the legacy-2 format, otherwise `collection.anki2` (both schema V11, not compressed, media index as a JSON map).
- `.colpkg` uses the same package code [U on the details].

**Database schema** ([AnkiDroid wiki](https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/wiki/Database-Structure)) [V]:
- `notes.flds` holds the field values separated by `0x1f`.
- Field names live in the `fields` table (schema 15 and later, [V]) or in the `col.models` JSON (V11).
- `cards` has `type`, `queue`, `ivl`, `factor` (‰), `reps`, `lapses` and `due`. The meaning of `due` depends on the card: new = queue position; learning = epoch seconds; review = days since `col.crt`.
- `revlog` has `id` (ms), `cid`, `ease`, `ivl`, `lastIvl`, `factor`, `time` and `type`.
- **FSRS memory state** is in the `cards.data` JSON: `s` (stability), `d` (difficulty), `dr`, `decay`, `lrt` ([data.rs](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/blob/main/rslib/src/storage/card/data.rs)) [V].

**Host-side readers** (PyPI and GitHub, [V] unless marked):
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| Your own reader: `zipfile` + `zstandard` + `sqlite3` + a tiny protobuf decoder | **Recommended for an MIT repo.** The format is small enough to read directly. |
| `anki` 26.9.4 (2026-11-04) | Official, reads everything, but heavy and **AGPL-3.0-or-later** (the PyPI licence field is empty; the source headers say AGPL). Use it only as an optional dependency, never copy it into the repo. |
| `ankipandas` 0.3.15 (MIT, 2023) | Reads a local profile's database; its docs don't mention anki21b. |
| `anki-export` 0.1.4 (MIT, 2022) | Probably handles only the legacy formats [U]. |
| `genanki` (MIT) | Writes decks only, can't read them. |
| [anki-apkg-parser](https://github.com/74Genesis/anki-apkg-parser) (Node, MIT, 2026-10) | Explicitly supports `collection.anki21b`. |
| `spacedrep` 0.5.0 (MIT) | CLI and MCP server with `.apkg` import/export and FSRS; I didn't test it. |

**AnkiConnect** ([sourcehut](https://git.sr.ht/~foosoft/anki-connect); the GitHub copy is archived) [V]:
- GPL-3.0+. Needs **Anki Desktop 26.08 or later, running**.
- Two APIs: v1 JSON-RPC at `127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1` (94 methods) and the legacy action API (122 actions).
- Useful legacy actions:
  - `cardsInfo` returns fields, factor, interval, type, queue, due, reps, lapses, left, mod.
  - `getReviewsOfCards` and `cardReviews` return review-history rows.
  - `answerCards` (ease 1–4) can push FM-1 reviews back into Anki.
  - `insertReviews` imports history without rescheduling.
  - `setDueDate` changes a card's due date.
- v1 exposes `fsrsMemory{difficulty, stabilityDays}`.
- Best use: two-way sync while tethered; use `.apkg` files for offline import.
- Caveat [E]: `answerCards` probably records the answer at sync time, not when it happened on the FM-1. Check this before relying on it.

## 4. Scheduling algorithms small enough for the FM-1
| Algorithm | State per card [E] | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Leitner | 2–3 B (box number + day/round) | Already in Morse. Python reference: [leitner-box](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/leitner-box) (MIT). |
| SM-2 | ~6–7 B (ease, interval, reps, due day) | Python reference: [sm-2](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/sm-2) (MIT). Note `anki-sm-2` is AGPL. |
| FSRS-6 | ~8–12 B with floats, ~6 B quantised to 16-bit (stability, difficulty, state/step, due, last review) | 21 parameters (defaults are in [py-fsrs scheduler.py](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/py-fsrs), MIT). Needs only `expf` and `powf`, so use single-precision floats. |

**There's no official embedded C version of FSRS** [V]:
- [rs-fsrs-c](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/rs-fsrs-c) is a proof-of-concept binding, and [fsrs-rs-c](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/fsrs-rs-c) is a dynamic library. Both are MIT and both wrap Rust.
- The practical path is to hand-port py-fsrs's scheduler (a few hundred lines) and test it against py-fsrs's reference vectors. Several closed-source apps in [awesome-fsrs](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/awesome-fsrs) did exactly this.
- Anki's own FSRS (`fsrs-rs`) is BSD-3.
- **Recommendation:** run FSRS on the device and seed it from the `s`/`d` values in `cards.data`.

## 5. Embedded flashcard prior art
- [stackmemo](https://github.com/rberenguel/stackmemo) (MIT): M5Stack Core2, MicroPython + LVGL, SM-2. It has no clock, so cards are just sorted by interval — the same problem the FM-1 has.
- [Adafruit MagTag flashcards](https://learn.adafruit.com/magtag-flashcards.md?view=all) (code in an MIT repo): cards in `deck.json`, Forgot/Good buttons, re-queues misses within a session, no real spaced repetition. It **dropped kanji because the glyphs didn't fit in memory**.
- TuftyKani ([thread](https://community.wanikani.com/t/my-take-on-a-pocket-sized-wanikani-gadget/74649)): RP2350 badge for WaniKani reviews. Caches the review queue offline and syncs results back later. It stored kanji as PNGs because it had no CJK font. No licence stated.
- [RmAnki](https://github.com/Jayy001/RmAnki) (GPL-3.0, reMarkable, syncs through AnkiConnect) and [KAnki](https://github.com/crizmo/KAnki) (Kindle, no licence).
- The "Word Box" ESP32 e-ink device: hackster returned 403, so not verified.

## Flash budget (my estimates [E])
- **Recorded audio doesn't fit.** At 8 kHz 8-bit, about 5 KB per word, so ~15 MB for 3,000 words, against ~2–6 s of free sample room. It only becomes possible if m-card ever works.
- **LPC speech fits a few thousand words.** At Speak37's ~141 B per word, 3,000 words is ~420 KB. That's tight alongside everything else, so speak only the top N words with LPC and spell the rest letter by letter (Speak37 does this), or use SPELLBOX-style letter-to-sound rules for any word.
- **Text and glyphs:**
  - A word with KK phonetics and a Traditional Chinese gloss is ~40 B; adding an example sentence brings it to ~100 B. So 3,000 words is 120–300 KB before compression.
  - Only the characters the deck actually uses need storing: ~2,500 Chinese characters at 1 bit per pixel is ~45 KB at 12×12 or ~80 KB at 16×16.
- **Scheduling state:** 3,000 cards × 8 B is 24 KB, so 6 sectors, or 12 with the A/B copies. Write it once at the end of each session.</result>

```text
 * n), if the app defines it: true for an old copy that holds nothing worth a sector (a placeholder of the layout
 * before the pool): the move into the pool drops the object instead (every copy of it erased).
 * The objects are the app's (app.h): an enum that includes OBJ_PANEL (the panel calibration, the platform's) and
 * ends with OBJ_NOBJ, and APP_STORE_MAP, each object's flash offset: two 4 KiB sectors (A/B) from there, inside the
 * data area (0x97000..0xDFFFF) or Felucca's settings sector pair at 0xFC000. An object's number is written in its
 * record, so an app keeps its numbering from one release to the next. */

                                        * turns the render's microseconds into instructions (a CPU guard's cost model);
                                        * built for an app with APP_CPU_KHZ (below) */

/* a free-running count of PLAT_TICKS_PER_US ticks a microsecond, for timing spans shorter than plat_ms can: a part of
 * the render, say. Device: TIMER4, from the 24 MHz crystal (one register read); host: its monotonic clock, at the same
 * rate. No lock and no state, so the audio interrupt and the tick may call it too. It wraps every 2^32 ticks (179 s):
 * a span is the unsigned difference of two reads */
#define PLAT_TICKS_PER_US 24u
uint32_t plat_ticks24(void);

/* Disk mode (fm1.toml msc = true: FM1B_MSC; device/msc.c on felucca-bsp's FELUCCA_MSC): the FM-1 shows the computer a
 * USB drive, the app's blocks, until it goes back to itself; meanwhile it has no USB MIDI or audio. The app keeps the
 * blocks (plat_disk_t) and calls plat_disk_poll from its main loop (APP_LOOP: every pass) while on. Host: nothing
 * comes (PLAT_DISK_WAITING) */
typedef struct {
    uint32_t blocks;                                   /* 512-byte blocks */
    const uint8_t *(*read)(uint32_t lba);              /* the block (512 bytes, kept until the next call); 0: zeros */
    int (*write)(uint32_t lba, const uint8_t *b);      /* 0 = written (it may hold it until flush) */
    void (*flush)(void);                               /* what is held, written (the computer synced or ejected) */
    const char *vendor, *product;                      /* what the computer calls it: 8 and 16 characters at most */
} plat_disk_t;
enum { PLAT_DISK_OFF, PLAT_DISK_WAITING, PLAT_DISK_MOUNTED, PLAT_DISK_EJECTED };
void plat_disk_mode(const plat_disk_t *d);             /* d: the FM-1 drops off USB and comes back as this disk; 0:
                                                        * flushed, then back as itself */
int plat_disk_poll(void);                              /* main loop: serve the computer -> PLAT_DISK_* (EJECTED: the
                                                        * computer let it go) */
uint32_t plat_disk_idle_ms(void);                      /* since the computer's last command */

/* code loaded at run time (fm1-ripple's currents: plug-ins copied from its disk into the pool and run there): the
 * guard's RAM code window (felucca-bsp fm1_guard.h, normally .ram_text alone) widened from .ram_text up to end, so
 * code there may run. Main loop, after the guards are on (app_init or later); host: nothing */
void plat_code_window(const void *end);
```

```text
"""Write a firmware's resource region into the attached FM-1 over USB-MIDI: an fm1-base firmware built with
resources = FILE (fm1.toml; device/res.c). After Melodee's tools/fm1_resources.py (Kerem Kilic, Ellic Studio; used
under MPL-2.0 with permission). tools/fm1_install.py runs it after an update when NAME-res.bin is beside the package.

    python3 tools/fm1_resources.py build/NAME-res.bin [--port NAME]

The file is build/NAME-res.bin (tools/build.py): the region as the FM-1 holds it, a 32-byte header (magic RES1, the
payload's length and CRC-32, the header's CRC-32) then the payload. The FM-1 takes only its own build's (the length
and CRC-32 its build knows), answers at once when it holds them already, and is stopped first (STOP FIRST). Then it
erases the region, pulls the payload (read requests, as a restore: tools/fm1_backup.py), checks it as written and
commits it.

Exit codes: 0 written or there already, 1 failed, 2 bad arguments or file, 3 FM-1 not found, 4 connection lost or the
FM-1 stopped answering, 5 playing (stop it first), 6 another build's resources.
"""
import argparse
import struct
import sys
import zlib
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import fm1_backup as B  # noqa: E402
import fm1_install as I  # noqa: E402

RES_REQ, MAGIC, HEAD = 0x44, 0x31534552, 32
EXIT = dict(B.EXIT, build=6)
ERRORS = {2: "the transfer (a read request unanswered)", 7: "a flash erase", 8: "a flash write",
          10: "the FM-1 is playing: STOP FIRST, then again", 20: "these resources are another build's than the FM-1 runs",
          21: "the FM-1 is still moving its projects (switch it off and on, then again)",
          22: "the check of what was written"}


class ResError(Exception):
    pass


def payload_of(region):
    """the payload of a NAME-res.bin (its header checked) -> (payload, crc)"""
    if len(region) < HEAD:
        raise ResError("too short for a resource file")
    magic, length, crc = struct.unpack_from("<3I", region)
    if magic != MAGIC or struct.unpack_from("<I", region, 28)[0] != zlib.crc32(region[:28]):
        raise ResError("not a resource file (tools/build.py's NAME-res.bin)")
    payload = region[HEAD:HEAD + length]
    if len(payload) != length or zlib.crc32(payload) != crc:
        raise ResError("cut short or damaged")
    return payload, crc


def push(dev, region, out=sys.stdout):
    """the region into the FM-1 found (fm1_install's device) -> 0, else an error code (ERRORS)"""
    payload, crc = payload_of(region)
    dev.link.drain()
    dev.link.send(B.frame(RES_REQ, struct.pack("<II", len(payload), crc)))
    try:
        return B.serve(dev.link, payload, out)
    finally:
        print(file=out)


def run(backend, path, port=None, out=sys.stdout):
    try:
        region = Path(path).read_bytes()
        payload_of(region)
    except OSError as e:
        raise I.InstallError("usage", f"cannot read {path}: {e.strerror}")
    except ResError as e:
        raise I.InstallError("badpkg", f"{path}: {e}")
    dev = B.find(backend, port)
    print(f"device: {dev.id.text}  ({dev.name})", file=out)
    try:
        code = push(dev, region, out)
    finally:
        dev.link.close()
    if code:
        print(f"error: resources not written: {ERRORS.get(code, 'code %d' % code)}", file=sys.stderr)

 * Ellic Studio; used under MPL-2.0 with permission): the build knows its payload's length and CRC-32 (build.py writes
 * fm1_res.h from the file), so a firmware finds whether the region holds its own. The package carries it and the
 * update loader writes it after the app (felucca-bsp loader/ldr_core.c ldr_res, as Melodee's), from any host; the host
 * can also write it itself (tools/fm1_resources.py, fm1_install.py, the installer page: RES_REQ below), and an update

#define RES_HEAD 32u
```

## Bottom line

None of the general-purpose English TTS engines fit. eSpeak NG, Flite, SVOX Pico, Espressif's esp-tts and every neural model need 0.7 to 300+ MB of flash or 0.3 to 2.5 MB of RAM. esp-tts is also Chinese only. For a fixed flashcard word list, three approaches fit the budget:

1. Store each word as compressed audio rendered offline by a good desktop TTS.
2. Store each word as LPC data, the Speak & Spell format (about 100 bytes per word).
3. Run a tiny formant synthesizer and store a phoneme string per word (about 10 bytes per word).

## Budget on this device (from the repo, not the web)

- **Chip:** JieLi AC791N, dual-core 32-bit RISC, up to 320 MHz. The datasheet says "Support FPU" (`tools/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK/doc/datasheet/AC791N规格书/datasheet/AC7911B_Datasheet_V1.3_20230303.pdf`). Your docs note a disagreement on whether it has an FPU; the datasheet says yes.
- **Flash:** the app limit is 581,564 B. Morse 0.2 takes 127,712 B of app and 28,444 of the 98,304 B `.data+.bss`. So a no-Bluetooth app has roughly 450 KB of flash and about 65 KB of RAM free. Bluetooth adds about 55–70 KB (`docs/dev/morse.md`, `docs/hardware/flash-map.md`).
- **Audio path:** fm1-base runs its own 44.1 kHz audio and links none of JieLi's audio libraries. Speech at 11.025 or 22.05 kHz upsamples by a whole number (×4, ×2). The 8 kHz codecs need fractional resampling.

English letter-to-sound rules are small. The NRL rules are 329 rules, about 90% of words correct ([DTIC](https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA021929.pdf)). SAM's reciter needed 8K of RAM on a C64, and Moonshine's rules file is about 13 KB of source. A flashcard app does not need runtime rules at all: generate exact phonemes per word offline.

Any 8 kHz format cuts off sound above 4 kHz. That blurs /s/, /f/ and /θ/ ("sink" vs "think"), which matters in a pronunciation app. ADPCM at 11 to 16 kHz avoids this.

## JieLi SDK findings

- **AC79 (your chip; checked in the local SDK):**
  - The audio service decodes "mp3、m4a、ape、flac、wav、amr、pcm、adpcm、wma、aac、spx、sbc、cvsd、msbc、opus" (`tools/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK/doc/stuff/AC79xx音频服务使用开发文档.pdf`). It does not list wtg or f1a.
  - The codec libraries are in `cpu/wl82/liba/` (`lib_mp3_dec.a`, `libspeex.a`, `lib_opus_dec.a`, `lib_amr_dec.a`, `lib_wav_dec.a`, `jla_codec_lib.a`).
  - The prompt sounds are plain MP3 files in `cpu/wl82/tools/audlogo/`, e.g. BtSucceed.mp3 at 16 kHz mono 96 kbps, 20,736 B. The tone player opens `tone/xxx.*` (`apps/wifi_story_machine/include/tone_player.h`).
  - The only TTS is a cloud one (`lib/net/tencent/tvs_sdk/src/tvs_tts_player.c`). There is no local TTS; the ASR and keyword-spotting libraries look like Chinese speech recognition.
  - I have not checked whether these binary decoders can be linked into fm1-base on their own. fm1-base links none of them today.
- **AC63 (GitHub):** `cpu/br34/tone_player.c` maps `{"wtg", AUDIO_CODING_G729}`, `{"wts", AUDIO_CODING_WTGV2}`, plus msbc, sbc, mty, aac, speex, opus, mp3 and wav, and can generate sine tones ([fw-AC63_BT_SDK](https://github.com/Jieli-Tech/fw-AC63_BT_SDK)). So `.wtg` is G.729.
- **AD14/15/16 voice-toy chips:** decode ".a/.b/.e, .f1a/.f1b/.f1c", UMP3, MIDI and WAV. The AD16N also has ima, opus, speex, sbc and jla_lw ([fw-AD15N](https://github.com/Jieli-Tech/fw-AD15N), [fw-AD16N](https://github.com/Jieli-Tech/fw-AD16N)). I could not find the bit rates of the .a/.f1a formats.

## Recommendation for 200–400 KB flash and 32–64 KB RAM

1. **Compressed audio rendered offline.** Render each word on a PC with Kokoro or Piper, then compress it.
   - Speex NB 3.95–5.95 kbps (BSD, open source): about 580–880 words in 300 KB after the decoder. The voice is natural but has noticeable artifacts.
   - IMA ADPCM at 11–16 kHz: about 60–90 words, the clearest sound. Only suits a core list.
   - Codec2 1200 holds about 2,000 words, but its decoder takes 128–380 KB of flash.
2. **TI LPC words**, generated from the same neural TTS with python_wizard: about 2,500–3,000 words in 300 KB. The decoder is a few KB with negligible RAM. Quality is Speak & Spell: understandable but buzzy, 8 kHz.
   - Licence: ArminJo's Talkie is GPL-3, so writing your own small LPC player avoids that.
3. **Moonshine Klatt (MIT) with per-word phonemes** made offline, e.g. from CMUdict. The vocabulary is effectively unlimited (5,000 words of phonemes is about 50–75 KB). Code is tens of KiB, RAM a few KiB, and it needs floats, which the FPU should cover. Quality is "robotic but understandable".
   - It could also be the fallback voice in option 1, for words not in the recorded set.

**Licensing:** GPL-3 parts (eSpeak NG, ArminJo Talkie) can't be legally distributed in a binary that includes JieLi's closed Bluetooth libraries (`ble = true` with JieLi's stack). LGPL-2.1 (Codec2) requires that users can relink it.

## What I could not verify

- How Moonshine Klatt sounds, and its compiled size with JieLi's clang.
- Speex and Codec2 decoder flash and RAM on this chip. I only have third-party figures, and the "87 KB" Codec2 figure is from a hobbyist write-up.
- Bit rates of JieLi's .a/.f1a formats.
- Whether JieLi's binary decoders can be linked without its audio framework.
- AMR patent status.
- The TMS5220 50-bit and 29-bit frame totals, which I added up from MAME's field widths.
- Piper's parameter count, where the sources disagree.

````text
# Flash 配置圖

FM-1 的 flash 是 1 MiB，分成 256 個 4 KiB 的 sector。誰把什麼放在哪裡，決定了換韌體時什麼會留下、什麼會被蓋掉。這頁把各個來源的說法和我自己備份的比對放在一起。

## 總覽

| 位址 | 內容 | 來源 |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00000`–`0x03FFF` | **boot head**：bootloader 與 boot 設定（16 KiB）。壞了就開不了機 | `[上游]` M-Flasher、Unbricker |
| `0x04000`–`0x92FFF` | **韌體區**。多數韌體（原廠 V15、SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1）佔這段 | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的寫入計畫 |
| `0x93000`–`0xE8FFF` | 原廠 V15 的**設定區**。社群韌體也把資料放在這裡面 | `[上游]` |
| `0xE9000` | Bluetooth 資料（配對） | `[上游]` |
| `0xEA000`–`0xFBFFF` | 原廠音色（factory voices） | `[上游]` |
| `0xFC000`–`0xFEFFF` | M-Flasher 的圖上標為 free；Felucca 系拿來放全域設定 | `[實機]` |
| `0xFF000`–`0xFFFFF` | key / MAC，裝置自己的資料 | `[上游]` |

M-Flasher 的 flash map 用顏色標的就是這些：BOOT `00–03`、FIRMWARE `04–92`、SETTINGS `93–E8`、PAIRINGS `E9`、SOUNDS `EA–FB`、free `FC–FE`、MAC `FF`。

## 韌體區不一定只到 `0x92FFF`

| 韌體 | 佔用範圍 | 來源 |
|---|---|---|
| SLOOP 2.8.5、Agent Deck 0.7、CTL-1 1.0.3 | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入到 `0x8FFFF`） | `[實機]` |
| Conductor 0.1（自製，fm1-base） | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入 `0x04000`–`0x8EFFF`、`0x91000`–`0x91FFF`） | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：140 sectors |
| Morse 0.1 / 0.2（自製，fm1-base） | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入：Conductor 0.3 → 0.1 是 `0x04000`–`0x21FFF`，0.1 → 0.2 是 `0x04000`–`0x23FFF`） | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：30、32 sectors |
| **ChoralRoot 0.41** | `0x04000`–**`0x9EFFF`** | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：152 sectors |
| **原廠 V16** | 到 **`0xA8FFF`** | `[上游]` Unbricker |

超出 `0x92FFF` 的韌體會直接蓋掉別人放在 `0x93000` 之後的資料。

## Felucca 系韌體的資料位置

Felucca、SLOOP、ChoralRoot 以及 Dinghy、fm1-base 系的韌體大多沿用同一套位址 `[上游]`：

| 位址 | 內容 |
|---|---|
| `0x97000` 起 | project（曲子） |
| `0x9F000` | SLOOP 的 autosave（和 ChoralRoot 的 FM6 bank 是同一個物件編號） |
| `0xA0000` 起 | samples |
| `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF` | 自製 [Morse](../dev/morse.md#flash) 的設定與學習進度（這台機器的備份裡這兩個 sector 都是空的） |
| `0xDC000` 起 | user preset bank；CTL-1 與 fm1-base 的 app（含 Conductor）用來放面板校正 |
| `0xDE000` | CTL-1 的 Bluetooth 設定 |
| `0xE0000` | 更新時暫存 update loader |
| `0xF2000`–`0xF3FFF` | RemoteFM1 第一次開 Bluetooth 時寫入 |
| `0xFC000` | 全域設定。**SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1 都寫這裡** |
| `0xFE000` | SLOOP autosave 的另一份 |

因為位址共用，韌體之間會互相踩到對方的資料，也會讀到對方留下的東西。

## 我的機器上實際發生的 `[實機]`

用各階段的完整備份逐 sector 比對：

| 動作 | 改變的 sector |
|---|---|
| 原廠 015 → 裝 SLOOP 並玩過 | 韌體區，加上 `0x97000`、`0x9F000`、`0xFC000`、`0xFD000`、`0xFE000` |
| → Agent Deck | 韌體區，加上 `0xFC000`（蓋掉 SLOOP 的設定） |
| → 回 SLOOP | 韌體區，加上 `0xFE000`。曲子還在 |
| → CTL-1 | 韌體區，加上 `0xDE000`、`0xDF000`、`0xFC000`、`0xFD000` |
| → ChoralRoot | `0x04000`–`0x9EFFF`，蓋掉了 `0x97000` 的 SLOOP project（已執行，尚未用備份比對確認其他 sector） |
| → Conductor | 韌體區 140 個 sector（`0x04000`–`0x8EFFF`、`0x91000`–`0x91FFF`）。開機後不寫任何資料（預演 `[模擬]`；實機尚未用備份比對） |

原廠出廠時 `0x93000`、`0xE9000`–`0xF2000`、`0xFA000`、`0xFB000` 有資料，`0xFC000`–`0xFE000` 是空的。

## 自己比對兩份備份

```python
S = 4096
a = open("backups/A/x.bin", "rb").read()
b = open("backups/B/y.bin", "rb").read()
print([hex(i * S) for i in range(256) if a[i * S:(i + 1) * S] != b[i * S:(i + 1) * S]])
```

## 這對操作的意義

- **只重裝韌體會保留資料區**，所以 SLOOP ↔ Agent Deck 來回曲子還在。
- **韌體比較大的（ChoralRoot、V16）會吃掉資料區**，回去時要還原備份。
- **共用的 `0xFC000` 每換一次就被蓋一次**，各韌體的全域設定不會跨韌體保留。
- **原廠音色在 `0xEA000`–`0xFBFFF`**，有些韌體會寫這一段。只有原廠備份救得回來。
````

```text
words.tsv: the screen's text <TAB> what to say, one a line ("#" starts a comment, unless the line has a tab: then
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**調研結論：FM-1（AC791N 360 MHz、app 可用約 464 KB RAM、韌體槽還剩約 450 KB）跑得動極小型 TTS，社群已有 SPELLBOX、Speak37、386DX 等 5 個會講話的韌體。這一輪要做到哪裡？**

Options:
- **調研文件 + 語音試聽 (Recommended)** - 把調研寫進 docs/，再用 host simulator 把 Klatt 與 LPC 兩種聲音各錄 20 個單字的 WAV 給你聽，聽完再決定 app 要用哪一種
- **直接規劃 app v1** - 調研文件 + firmware/vocab + host/vocab：內建字卡、FSRS 排程、Anki 匯入，一次規劃到底
- **只要調研文件** - 只把結論寫進 docs/，先不寫程式

**FM-1 上的發音方案要選哪一種？（這會決定 app 的 licence）**

Options:
- **Klatt 共振峰合成 (Recommended)** - Moonshine Klatt，MIT。電腦先把每個字轉成音素，每字約 10 B，字數幾乎無上限。聲音機械但聽得懂，也能唸任意輸入的字
- **預錄 LPC（Speak & Spell 式）** - 電腦用 Kokoro 合成後轉成 LPC，每字約 100 B，約 2500–3000 字。語調較自然，但是 8 kHz 的嗡嗡聲，s/f/th 不好分
- **沿用 GPL 的 386DX 引擎** - eSpeak NG 前端 + Klatt，已在 FM-1 上驗證過，但 app 會變成 GPL-3.0（你其他 app 都是 MIT）

**字卡（含 Anki 匯入的）要怎麼放進 FM-1？**

Options:
- **編進韌體映像 (Recommended)** - 換字卡 = 重新 build + 刷寫，每次都要你同意。只寫韌體區（跟 Morse 升級一樣），不碰 SLOOP 的資料，完全符合現有安全規則
- **App 自己寫入 flash 資料區** - 用 USB 隨時推新字卡、不必重刷。但要放寬 AGENTS.md「不直接 erase/program」的規則，而且會佔用 SLOOP 的 project/sample 區
- **只在連線時由電腦串流** - 完全不寫 flash，排程直接用 Anki 的；但離開電腦就不能用

**主要想背什麼內容？**

Options:
- **內建通用字表 + 自己的 Anki (Recommended)** - 內建 NGSL 約 2800 字（CC BY-SA）+ ECDICT 釋義（MIT，用 OpenCC 轉成台灣繁體），另外可以匯入自己的 .apkg
- **只用自己的 Anki deck** - 不做內建字表，只做 .apkg 匯入
- **特定考試字表** - 多益、全民英檢、大考 6000 字等。這些字表有版權限制，只能放在本機（git-ignored），不能進公開 repo


**Answer:** 調研文件 + 語音試聽 (Recommended), 感覺都想試試看 然後因為也還沒有打算發佈app 等要發佈了再說 （除非真的好用 那反正開源出來share也沒關係）, 感覺可以optionally允許使用flash資料區？, 內建通用字表 + 自己的 Anki + 特定考試字表 等等". Read the answers carefully — they may request clarification, changes, or that you not proceed — and follow what they actually say.

```text
fm1-fetch:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p downloads && cd downloads
    fetch() { # repo tag asset
      gh release download "$2" -R "$1" -p "$3" --clobber
      want=$(gh api "repos/$1/releases/tags/$2" --jq ".assets[] | select(.name==\"$3\") | .digest" | sed 's/^sha256://')
      got=$(shasum -a 256 "$3" | cut -d' ' -f1)
      if [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" = "$got" ]; then echo "ok   $3  $got"; else echo "FAIL $3: got $got, release says ${want:-<no digest>}" >&2; exit 1; fi
    }
    fetch jvitkauskas/m-flasher "v{{m_flasher_version}}" "M-Flasher-{{m_flasher_version}}-macos.dmg"
    fetch isod89/sloop-fm1 "v{{sloop_version}}" "sloop-{{sloop_version}}.fwsc"
    fetch isod89/sloop-fm1 "v{{sloop_version}}" "sloop-editor-{{sloop_version}}.html"

# Download the other firmwares I try (CTL-1, ChoralRoot, RemoteFM1) and verify them against the release digests.
fm1-fetch-more:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p downloads && cd downloads
    fetch() { # repo tag asset
      gh release download "$2" -R "$1" -p "$3" --clobber
      want=$(gh api "repos/$1/releases/tags/$2" --jq ".assets[] | select(.name==\"$3\") | .digest" | sed 's/^sha256://')
      got=$(shasum -a 256 "$3" | cut -d' ' -f1)
      if [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" = "$got" ]; then echo "ok   $3  $got"; else echo "FAIL $3: got $got, release says ${want:-<no digest>}" >&2; exit 1; fi
    }
    fetch charlesvestal/fm1-ctl "v{{ctl_version}}" "ctl-{{ctl_version}}.fwsc"
    fetch Quixotic7/ChoralRootFM1 "{{choralroot_tag}}" "{{choralroot_pkg}}"
    fetch Quixotic7/RemoteFM1 "v{{remote_version}}" "remote-{{remote_version}}.fwsc"

# Open the M-Flasher disk image (drag the app to Applications yourself).
fm1-install-flasher: fm1-fetch
    open "downloads/M-Flasher-{{m_flasher_version}}-macos.dmg"

# Open the M-Flasher window.
fm1-gui:
    open -a M-Flasher

# Open the offline SLOOP web editor in Chrome.
sloop-editor:
    open -a "Google Chrome" "downloads/sloop-editor-{{sloop_version}}.html"

# ---- emulator (never touches the unit) ---------------------------------------

# Download fm1-emu (macOS arm64) into tools/fm1-emu/ and verify it against the release digest.
emu-fetch:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    a="fm1-emu-{{fm1_emu_version}}-macos-arm64.tar.gz"
    mkdir -p downloads tools/fm1-emu
    gh release download "v{{fm1_emu_version}}" -R joakimeriksson/fm1-emu -p "$a" -D downloads --clobber
    want=$(gh api "repos/joakimeriksson/fm1-emu/releases/tags/v{{fm1_emu_version}}" --jq ".assets[] | select(.name==\"$a\") | .digest" | sed 's/^sha256://')
    got=$(shasum -a 256 "downloads/$a" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "FAIL $a: got $got, release says ${want:-<no digest>}" >&2; exit 1; }
    tar -xzf "downloads/$a" -C tools/fm1-emu --strip-components=1
    xattr -d com.apple.quarantine tools/fm1-emu/fm1-live tools/fm1-emu/fm1-emu 2>/dev/null || true
    tools/fm1-emu/fm1-live --version

# Download Agent Deck's package and verify its digest and build attestation.
agtdeck-fetch:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    a="agtdeck-{{agtdeck_version}}.fwsc"
    mkdir -p downloads
    gh release download "v{{agtdeck_version}}" -R kevinelliott/fm-1-agent-deck -p "$a" -D downloads --clobber
    want=$(gh api "repos/kevinelliott/fm-1-agent-deck/releases/tags/v{{agtdeck_version}}" --jq ".assets[] | select(.name==\"$a\") | .digest" | sed 's/^sha256://')
    got=$(shasum -a 256 "downloads/$a" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "FAIL $a: got $got, release says ${want:-<no digest>}" >&2; exit 1; }
    gh attestation verify "downloads/$a" --repo kevinelliott/fm-1-agent-deck \
      --signer-workflow zvenson/fm1-build/.github/workflows/build.yml >/dev/null
    echo "ok   $a  $got  (attestation verified)"

# Play a .fwsc in a window. chip: uc25hq80 (this unit, default) or p25q80. Saves persist per package+chip.
emu-run package chip="uc25hq80" *args:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p tools/emu-state
    state="tools/emu-state/$(basename "{{package}}" .fwsc)-{{chip}}.flash"
    exec tools/fm1-emu/fm1-live --fwsc "{{package}}" --flash-chip "{{chip}}" --flash "$state" {{args}}

# Headless boot for `ms` emulated ms; writes the LCD to tools/emu-state/<name>-<chip>.ppm and reports flash writes.
emu-shot package chip="uc25hq80" ms="6000":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p tools/emu-state/work
    name="$(basename "{{package}}" .fwsc)-{{chip}}"
    pkg="$(cd "$(dirname "{{package}}")" && pwd)/$(basename "{{package}}")"
    cd tools/emu-state
    ../fm1-emu/fm1-live --fwsc "$pkg" --flash-chip "{{chip}}" --flash "$name.flash" --midi none \
      --shot "{{ms}}" --lcd-only 2>&1 | grep -i -E "^flash:|fault|error" || true
    mv work/lcd.ppm "$name.ppm" && echo "LCD: tools/emu-state/$name.ppm"
```

```markdown
# FM-1 裝置端 TTS 調研 + 語音試聽 spike（背單字 app 的前置）

## Context 背景

你想知道 FM-1 能不能跑極小型的 edge TTS，如果可以，就沿用 Morse 的經驗做一個類似 WordBit 的背單字 app：要有學習曲線（spaced repetition），也要能匯入 Anki。

這一輪依你的選擇做兩件事：
- 把調研寫進 `docs/`
- 做語音試聽，各種方案都聽聽看

app 本身這一輪只寫構想，不寫程式。你目前不打算發佈，licence 等要發佈時再定。不過 **repo 是公開的**，commit 進去就等於公開，所以這一輪只 commit MIT 程式碼。GPL 引擎留在 git-ignored 的 `vendor/`，或是直接下載對方發佈的 `.fwsc` 來聽。

## 調研結論 Findings（會寫進 docs）

**硬體預算**
- JieLi AC791N 雙核，360 MHz，單精度 FPU。
- app 有 96 KB `.data/.bss` 加上 336 KB pool（`third_party/fm1-base/README.md:143-146`）。
- 韌體槽 581,564 B，Morse 0.3 用了 127,880 B，剩大約 450 KB。
- 有喇叭和 3.5 mm 耳機孔，`app_render` 輸出 44.1 kHz。
- 字型只有 ASCII，中文和 KK 音標需要另外做 glyph subset。

**FM-1 上已經有 5 個會講話的韌體**
| 韌體 | 做法 | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| Speak37 | espeak-ng 預先轉成 LPC，FM-1 版收 2576 字 | GPL-3.0 |
| SPELLBOX | LPC + 12k 字典 + 字母轉音規則；只支援舊 flash 晶片 | GPL-3.0 |
| 386DX | eSpeak NG 前端 + Klatt，在 96 KB RAM 內 | GPL-3.0 |
| Chimera Vocal | 聲道物理模型 | MIT |
| EVIL GENIUS | SAM | SAM 本身授權不明 |

沒有任何 FM-1 韌體做字卡、單字或 Anki。

**通用 TTS 都放不下**
- eSpeak NG 約 1.4 MB、Flite 約 2.3 MB、Pico 需要 1 MB 以上 RAM，神經網路 TTS 是 MB 到百 MB 級。
- 放得下的有三條路：
  1. **Moonshine Klatt**：MIT，C++17，程式幾十 KiB，RAM 幾 KiB。每字只存約 10 B 音素，字數幾乎無上限。
  2. **預錄 LPC**：每字約 100 B，大約 2500–3000 字。
  3. **ADPCM 11–16 kHz**：音質最好，但每字 3–5 KB，只夠幾十到一百字。

**排程**
- FSRS-6 從 py-fsrs（MIT）手動 port 成 C。每張卡的狀態約 6–12 B，需要 `expf`/`powf`。
- 機器沒有 RTC，所以日期要在連線時由電腦給。

**Anki 匯入**
- `.apkg` 是 zip。新版是 zstd 壓縮的 `collection.anki21b` 加上 protobuf `meta`。
- 自己寫一個 MIT reader 就夠：`zipfile` + `zstandard` + `sqlite3`。
- 雙向同步用 AnkiConnect。

   - JieLi SDK 的發現：AC79 只有雲端 TTS，提示音是 MP3
   - licence 注意事項：GPL 不能和 JieLi 閉源 BLE 函式庫一起散佈
   - 標籤：`[上游]` 附連結，`[調研]` 用於未驗證的項目

2. **新增 `docs/dev/vocab.md`「背單字 app 構想（草案）」**

   - **學習曲線**：FSRS 的遺忘曲線 R(t) 加上下次複習日；統計頁顯示每日複習量和卡片狀態。
   - **內容來源與 licence**：
     - 內建 NGSL（CC BY-SA 4.0，資料另放並附 LICENSE）
     - ECDICT 釋義（MIT），用 OpenCC `s2twp` 轉成台灣繁體
     - 自己的 Anki deck
     - 考試字表（多益、全民英檢、大考）只放本機 git-ignored 的 `decks/`，不進公開 repo
   - **中文與 KK**：只把 deck 用到的字做成 subset，用 Cubic 11（OFL-1.1）。2500 字 1-bit 約 40 KB。
   - **字卡傳輸**：
     - v1 編進韌體映像，換 deck 就要重刷，只寫韌體區。

       - 規則草稿寫在文件裡：只能用 `plat_data_*`，寫在一段事先宣告、並且在最新備份裡確認是空的 sector 範圍；要先跑 `just emu-rehearse`，也要更新 `flash-map.md`。
       - 這一輪**不改規則**，等真的要做時你再核准規則的文字。
   - **同步**：連線時電腦送日期給機器，機器回傳複習紀錄，再透過 AnkiConnect `answerCards`/`insertReviews` 寫回 Anki。
   - **flash 預算**與分階段 roadmap。
3. **其他文件與設定**
   - `zensical.toml` 的 nav 加入這兩頁。
   - `docs/resources.md` 的版本表加上 Step 2 下載的韌體。

### Step 2 — 在模擬器裡試聽社群的會講話韌體（不碰實機）

- **新增 `just voice-fetch`**
  - 照 `Justfile` 裡 `fm1-fetch-more` 的 `fetch()` 模式：`gh release download` 之後比對 release digest。
  - 對象是 Speak37（FM-1 版）、386DX、Chimera Vocal、EVIL GENIUS，SPELLBOX 有 release 才抓。
  - 版本號放進 Justfile 變數。實作時用 `gh release view` 確認 tag。沒有 digest 或找不到 FM-1 版的，就回報，不加進來。
- 依 AGENTS.md，每個都先用 `just emu-shot` 確認偵測到的是 FM-1 板，不是 SMK-37。
- 你用 `just emu-run downloads/X.fwsc` 實際玩。SPELLBOX 用 `p25q80` 晶片。
- 先確認 fm1-live 視窗會出聲。不會的話，在 tts.md 記下這個限制。
- 你的感想寫進 tts.md，標 `[模擬]`。

### Step 3 — Mac 上的語音實驗室 `host/voicelab/`（Python，MIT）

**測試字**：`host/voicelab/words.txt`，約 20 個字加 2 句，挑容易混淆的音：
- think/sink、three/tree、ship/sip、very/berry、light/right
- world、thought、measure、judge、rhythm
- vocabulary、pronunciation、comfortable、schedule、necessary
- 句子："Practice makes perfect."

**各方案的輸出**一律是 `build/voicelab/<engine>/<word>.wav`（git-ignored）：
1. **參考音**
   - macOS `say`，等於連線時用 USB audio 播的音質。
   - Kokoro（Apache-2.0）用 `uv run --with` 選用，因為要下載約 330 MB，預設不跑。
2. **Klatt（Moonshine，MIT）**
   - pinned commit clone 到 `vendor/moonshine`，用 CMake 做 host build。
   - 寫一個小的 C++ driver（`host/voicelab/klatt_render.cpp`，MIT，會 commit），呼叫 `BeginIpa`，並且也拿 `BeginText` 的內建 G2P 來比較。
   - IPA 來源是 CMUdict（BSD，抓到 `vendor/`），在 Python 裡把 ARPAbet 轉成 IPA。
3. **386DX 引擎（GPL-3.0）**
   - 依它的 README，clone 到 `vendor/`，加上 espeak-ng 1.52.0，用 `DX_HOST` build。
   - 它是唱歌引擎，用單一平音念字。
   - GPL 的程式碼和 driver 都只留在 `vendor/`，不 commit。
4. **LPC（TMS5220 式）**
   - 參考音轉 8 kHz，用 python_wizard（MIT，放 `vendor/`）編成 LPC frames。
   - 解碼器自己寫：**`firmware/common/lpc.{c,h}`（MIT，不依賴平台，host 和裝置共用）**。
   - 輸出 WAV，並記錄每字 bytes。
5. **ADPCM**：IMA 4-bit，11.025 與 16 kHz，用 Python 編碼再解碼，作為「預錄」的音質上限。

**試聽頁**：`build/voicelab/index.html`，單字 × 方案的表格，每格有 `<audio>`，附每字 bytes 和「3000 字需要多少 KB」。

**Just recipes**：`just voice-lab` 產生全部檔案，`just voice-open` 打開頁面。

**測試**
- `host/tests/test_voicelab.py`：ARPAbet→IPA 對照、ADPCM round-trip。
- LPC 解碼器的單元測試照 `just fw-common-test` 的模式。

### Step 4 — 裝置端程式路徑驗證 `firmware/voicelab/`（fm1-base app，MIT，不刷機）

- **內容**：用 fm1-base template 結構做一個 app，裝自己的 LPC 和 ADPCM 解碼器。
- **操作**：琴鍵對應測試字，按鈕切換方案。播放走 `app_render`，在 44.1 kHz 上重新取樣（輸出做法參考 `firmware/morse/tone.c`）。
- **Klatt 不放進來**：Moonshine 是 C++17，fm1-base 目前看起來只 build C，實作時要確認。是否 port 成 C，等你聽完再決定。
- **生成資料**：放 `firmware/voicelab/gen/`，`.gitignore` 加上 `firmware/*/gen/`。macOS `say` 的聲音不適合公開散佈。
- **驗證**
  - `just fw-test voicelab`：`tests/basic.txt` 用 host simulator 的 `wav FILE` 錄下來，這就是之前說的「用 host simulator 錄」。
  - `just fw-build voicelab`：回報大小和 `APP_SLOT` 的比較。
  - `just emu-run` 在 `uc25hq80` 和 `p25q80` 上都聽一次。
- 這一輪不刷實機。要在實機上聽是另一次韌體寫入，需要你核准並跑完 preflight。
```

```text
- JieLi AC791N 雙核，360 MHz，單精度 FPU。

- 有喇叭和 3.5 mm 耳機孔，`app_render` 輸出 44.1 kHz。
- 字型只有 ASCII，中文和 KK 音標需要另外做 glyph subset。

**FM-1 上已經有 5 個會講話的韌體**
| 韌體 | 做法 | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| Speak37 | espeak-ng 預先轉成 LPC，FM-1 版收 2576 字 | GPL-3.0 |
| SPELLBOX | LPC + 12k 字典 + 字母轉音規則；只支援舊 flash 晶片 | GPL-3.0 |
| 386DX | eSpeak NG 前端 + Klatt，在 96 KB RAM 內 | GPL-3.0 |
| Chimera Vocal | 聲道物理模型 | MIT |
| EVIL GENIUS | SAM | SAM 本身授權不明 |

沒有任何 FM-1 韌體做字卡、單字或 Anki。

**通用 TTS 都放不下**
- eSpeak NG 約 1.4 MB、Flite 約 2.3 MB、Pico 需要 1 MB 以上 RAM，神經網路 TTS 是 MB 到百 MB 級。
- 放得下的有三條路：
  1. **Moonshine Klatt**：MIT，C++17，程式幾十 KiB，RAM 幾 KiB。每字只存約 10 B 音素，字數幾乎無上限。
  2. **預錄 LPC**：每字約 100 B，大約 2500–3000 字。
  3. **ADPCM 11–16 kHz**：音質最好，但每字 3–5 KB，只夠幾十到一百字。

**排程**
- FSRS-6 從 py-fsrs（MIT）手動 port 成 C。每張卡的狀態約 6–12 B，需要 `expf`/`powf`。
- 機器沒有 RTC，所以日期要在連線時由電腦給。

**Anki 匯入**
- `.apkg` 是 zip。新版是 zstd 壓縮的 `collection.anki21b` 加上 protobuf `meta`。
- 自己寫一個 MIT reader 就夠：`zipfile` + `zstandard` + `sqlite3`。
- 雙向同步用 AnkiConnect。

## 這一輪的步驟 Steps

### Step 1 — 調研文件（`docs/`，繁體中文，依規則加標籤）

1. **新增 `docs/dev/tts.md`「裝置端語音合成」**
   - 硬體預算
   - 引擎比較表與預錄格式比較表（每字 bytes、300 KB 放得下幾字）
   - 社群會講話的韌體
   - JieLi SDK 的發現：AC79 只有雲端 TTS，提示音是 MP3
   - licence 注意事項：GPL 不能和 JieLi 閉源 BLE 函式庫一起散佈
   - 標籤：`[上游]` 附連結，`[調研]` 用於未驗證的項目
   - 試聽結果在 Step 2、3 之後補上
2. **新增 `docs/dev/vocab.md`「背單字 app 構想（草案）」**
   - **WordBit 對照**：開機就出現一張卡（取代鎖屏）、四個按鈕評分（Again/Hard/Good/Easy）、四選一、拼字（A–Z 放在琴鍵上，同 SPELLBOX 的排法）、自動播放的瀏覽模式。
   - **學習曲線**：FSRS 的遺忘曲線 R(t) 加上下次複習日；統計頁顯示每日複習量和卡片狀態。
   - **內容來源與 licence**：
     - 內建 NGSL（CC BY-SA 4.0，資料另放並附 LICENSE）
     - ECDICT 釋義（MIT），用 OpenCC `s2twp` 轉成台灣繁體
     - 自己的 Anki deck
     - 考試字表（多益、全民英檢、大考）只放本機 git-ignored 的 `decks/`，不進公開 repo
   - **中文與 KK**：只把 deck 用到的字做成 subset，用 Cubic 11（OFL-1.1）。2500 字 1-bit 約 40 KB。
   - **字卡傳輸**：
     - v1 編進韌體映像，換 deck 就要重刷，只寫韌體區。
     - 你同意「可選擇使用 flash 資料區」：
       - 這條路要先修改 AGENTS.md 的「不直接 erase/program」規則。
       - 規則草稿寫在文件裡：只能用 `plat_data_*`，寫在一段事先宣告、並且在最新備份裡確認是空的 sector 範圍；要先跑 `just emu-rehearse`，也要更新 `flash-map.md`。
       - 這一輪**不改規則**，等真的要做時你再核准規則的文字。
   - **同步**：連線時電腦送日期給機器，機器回傳複習紀錄，再透過 AnkiConnect `answerCards`/`insertReviews` 寫回 Anki。
   - **flash 預算**與分階段 roadmap。
3. **其他文件與設定**
   - `zensical.toml` 的 nav 加入這兩頁。
   - `docs/resources.md` 的版本表加上 Step 2 下載的韌體。
   - 修正過時描述：`docs/dev/index.md:5`「還沒刷進實機」，以及 `AGENTS.md` 的 "No own build has been flashed"。實際上 Conductor 0.1/0.2、Morse 0.1–0.3 都已經刷過，見 `docs/device-log.md`。
   - `AGENTS.md`：Layout 和 Commands 加上 voicelab 相關的列。

### Step 2 — 在模擬器裡試聽社群的會講話韌體（不碰實機）

- **新增 `just voice-fetch`**
  - 照 `Justfile` 裡 `fm1-fetch-more` 的 `fetch()` 模式：`gh release download` 之後比對 release digest。
  - 對象是 Speak37（FM-1 版）、386DX、Chimera Vocal、EVIL GENIUS，SPELLBOX 有 release 才抓。
  - 版本號放進 Justfile 變數。實作時用 `gh release view` 確認 tag。沒有 digest 或找不到 FM-1 版的，就回報，不加進來。
- 依 AGENTS.md，每個都先用 `just emu-shot` 確認偵測到的是 FM-1 板，不是 SMK-37。
- 你用 `just emu-run downloads/X.fwsc` 實際玩。SPELLBOX 用 `p25q80` 晶片。
- 先確認 fm1-live 視窗會出聲。不會的話，在 tts.md 記下這個限制。
- 你的感想寫進 tts.md，標 `[模擬]`。

### Step 3 — Mac 上的語音實驗室 `host/voicelab/`（Python，MIT）

**測試字**：`host/voicelab/words.txt`，約 20 個字加 2 句，挑容易混淆的音：
- think/sink、three/tree、ship/sip、very/berry、light/right
- world、thought、measure、judge、rhythm
- vocabulary、pronunciation、comfortable、schedule、necessary
- 句子："Practice makes perfect."

**各方案的輸出**一律是 `build/voicelab/<engine>/<word>.wav`（git-ignored）：
1. **參考音**
   - macOS `say`，等於連線時用 USB audio 播的音質。
   - Kokoro（Apache-2.0）用 `uv run --with` 選用，因為要下載約 330 MB，預設不跑。
2. **Klatt（Moonshine，MIT）**
   - pinned commit clone 到 `vendor/moonshine`，用 CMake 做 host build。
   - 寫一個小的 C++ driver（`host/voicelab/klatt_render.cpp`，MIT，會 commit），呼叫 `BeginIpa`，並且也拿 `BeginText` 的內建 G2P 來比較。
   - IPA 來源是 CMUdict（BSD，抓到 `vendor/`），在 Python 裡把 ARPAbet 轉成 IPA。
3. **386DX 引擎（GPL-3.0）**
   - 依它的 README，clone 到 `vendor/`，加上 espeak-ng 1.52.0，用 `DX_HOST` build。
   - 它是唱歌引擎，用單一平音念字。
   - GPL 的程式碼和 driver 都只留在 `vendor/`，不 commit。
4. **LPC（TMS5220 式）**
   - 參考音轉 8 kHz，用 python_wizard（MIT，放 `vendor/`）編成 LPC frames。
   - 解碼器自己寫：**`firmware/common/lpc.{c,h}`（MIT，不依賴平台，host 和裝置共用）**。
   - 輸出 WAV，並記錄每字 bytes。
5. **ADPCM**：IMA 4-bit，11.025 與 16 kHz，用 Python 編碼再解碼，作為「預錄」的音質上限。

**試聽頁**：`build/voicelab/index.html`，單字 × 方案的表格，每格有 `<audio>`，附每字 bytes 和「3000 字需要多少 KB」。

**Just recipes**：`just voice-lab` 產生全部檔案，`just voice-open` 打開頁面。

**測試**
- `host/tests/test_voicelab.py`：ARPAbet→IPA 對照、ADPCM round-trip。
- LPC 解碼器的單元測試照 `just fw-common-test` 的模式。

### Step 4 — 裝置端程式路徑驗證 `firmware/voicelab/`（fm1-base app，MIT，不刷機）

- **內容**：用 fm1-base template 結構做一個 app，裝自己的 LPC 和 ADPCM 解碼器。
- **操作**：琴鍵對應測試字，按鈕切換方案。播放走 `app_render`，在 44.1 kHz 上重新取樣（輸出做法參考 `firmware/morse/tone.c`）。
- **Klatt 不放進來**：Moonshine 是 C++17，fm1-base 目前看起來只 build C，實作時要確認。是否 port 成 C，等你聽完再決定。
- **生成資料**：放 `firmware/voicelab/gen/`，`.gitignore` 加上 `firmware/*/gen/`。macOS `say` 的聲音不適合公開散佈。
- **驗證**
  - `just fw-test voicelab`：`tests/basic.txt` 用 host simulator 的 `wav FILE` 錄下來，這就是之前說的「用 host simulator 錄」。
  - `just fw-build voicelab`：回報大小和 `APP_SLOT` 的比較。
  - `just emu-run` 在 `uc25hq80` 和 `p25q80` 上都聽一次。
- 這一輪不刷實機。要在實機上聽是另一次韌體寫入，需要你核准並跑完 preflight。

## 主要會動到的檔案 Files

- **新增**
  - `docs/dev/tts.md`、`docs/dev/vocab.md`
  - `host/voicelab/`（`words.txt`、`lab.py`、`klatt_render.cpp`、`index.html` 樣板）
  - `host/tests/test_voicelab.py`
  - `firmware/common/lpc.{c,h}` 與測試
  - `firmware/voicelab/`（Step 4）
- **修改**
  - `zensical.toml`（nav）
  - `docs/resources.md`（版本表）
  - `docs/dev/index.md`（過時描述）
  - `AGENTS.md`（Layout、Commands、過時描述）
  - `Justfile`（`voice-fetch`、`voice-lab`、`voice-open`，版本變數）
  - `.gitignore`
- **沿用**
  - `Justfile` 的 `fetch()` digest 驗證和 `emu-run`/`emu-shot`
  - `firmware/morse/tone.c` 的輸出方式
  - `firmware/common/README.md` 的模組慣例
  - host simulator 的 `wav` 指令（`third_party/fm1-base/host/plat_host.c:26`）
- **不動**
  - `firmware/morse`：另一個工作正在把它改成 submodule（fm1-morse），目前是 staged 狀態，只拿來參考。
  - working tree 裡還沒 commit 的 Morse 相關修改（`docs/dev/morse.md`、`device-log.md`、`docs/firmware/hub.md` 等）
  - `third_party/fm1-base`
- **協調**
  - `AGENTS.md`、`Justfile`、`firmware/common/README.md` 現在也有那批還沒 commit 的修改。
  - 開工前先確認那批已經 commit。我這邊的修改都只新增段落或列，不改寫既有內容。
  - 背單字 app 之後如果要上 Firmware Hub，可以比照 Morse 拆成獨立 repo 再掛成 submodule，這點寫進 vocab.md 的 roadmap。
- **不會 commit**：GPL 程式碼和生成的語音資料。

## Verification 驗證

1. `just docs-check` 通過，新頁面出現在 nav 裡。
2. `just voice-fetch`：每個檔案都是 `ok <sha256>`。`just emu-shot` 顯示 FM-1 板。
3. `just voice-lab` 產生每個方案 × 每個字的 WAV；`just voice-open` 的頁面可以播放，bytes/字 表格正確。
4. 這幾個都通過：
   - `uv run pytest host/tests/test_voicelab.py`
   - `just fw-common-test`（LPC 解碼器）
   - `just fw-test voicelab`（host simulator 錄出 WAV）
   - `just fw-build voicelab`（大小在 `APP_SLOT` 內）
   - `just emu-run` 兩種晶片都有出聲
5. 你聽完選定方案，結果寫回 `docs/dev/tts.md`，再決定 vocab app v1 用哪種語音、Klatt 要不要 port 成 C。
6. 這一輪沒有任何實機操作，`docs/device-log.md` 不變；commit 等你要求再做。
```

```text
# ---- own firmware (firmware/<app>, on third_party/fm1-base) -------------------

fm1_base := "third_party/fm1-base"

# One-time: submodules and the Python tools. Needs `brew install libraqm` (Pillow is built against it).
fw-setup:
    git submodule update --init --recursive third_party/fm1-base
    git submodule update --init firmware/morse
    uv sync --locked --all-groups

# Build an app's host simulator (no toolchain needed) and run its test script.
fw-test app="hello": fw-setup
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    uv run --locked --all-groups python "{{fm1_base}}/tools/build.py" "firmware/{{app}}" --host
    bin=$(ls firmware/{{app}}/build/host/*_host)
    cd "firmware/{{app}}" && "build/host/$(basename "$bin")" tests/basic.txt build/host
    echo "screenshots and audio: firmware/{{app}}/build/host/"

# One-time for device builds: JieLi toolchain and the pinned AC79 SDK into tools/ (about 1.2 GB).
fw-toolchain:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p tools/jieli
    test -e tools/jieli/toolchain || sh "{{fm1_base}}/tools/get_toolchain.sh" "$PWD/tools/jieli"
    test -d tools/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK || git clone --depth 1 --branch AC79NN_SDK_V1.2.1_2023-12-13 \
      https://gitee.com/Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK.git tools/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK

# Build an app's device package (firmware/<app>/build/*.fwsc). On macOS the tools run in a linux/amd64 container.
fw-build app="hello": fw-setup fw-toolchain
    JIELI_TOOLCHAIN="$PWD/tools/jieli/toolchain" AC79_SDK="$PWD/tools/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK" \
      uv run --locked --all-groups python "{{fm1_base}}/tools/build.py" "firmware/{{app}}"

# ---- Conductor: own agent console (firmware/conductor + host/conductor) ------

# Host daemon unit tests (protocol, slot memory, action checks; no hardware, no backend).
cond-test:
    uv run --locked --all-groups pytest -q

# The daemon against a text stand-in for the FM-1 (backend: fake, auto, hc or herdr).
cond-sim backend="fake" *args:
    PYTHONPATH=host uv run --locked --all-groups python -m conductor --backend "{{backend}}" --simulate {{args}}

# The daemon against a MIDI device named CONDUCTOR: the real unit, or `just cond-emu`.
# auto (default): hc and classic Herdr together.
cond-run backend="auto" *args:
    PYTHONPATH=host uv run --locked --all-groups python -m conductor --backend "{{backend}}" {{args}}

# macOS's Bluetooth MIDI window, opened by itself (click Connect next to FM-1 XXXX); waits for the port.
cond-ble:
    PYTHONPATH=host uv run --locked --all-groups python -m conductor.blelink

# The firmware in the emulator with the virtual USB cable plugged in (pair with `just cond-run`).
cond-emu chip="uc25hq80":
    just emu-run firmware/conductor/build/conductor.fwsc "{{chip}}" --usb

# firmware/common's own tests on this computer (hostlink's Bluetooth SysEx packets).
fw-common-test:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p build
    cc -Wall -Wextra -I firmware/common -o build/hostlink_test firmware/common/tests/hostlink_test.c
    build/hostlink_test

# hc end to end: two fake agents (label conductor-test=1), approve / deny / continue, then kill them.
cond-it:
    uv run --locked --all-groups python host/tests/integration_hc.py

# Agent Deck in the emulator with the virtual USB cable plugged in (pair with `just agtdeck-run`).
agtdeck-emu chip="uc25hq80": agtdeck-fetch
    just emu-run "downloads/agtdeck-{{agtdeck_version}}.fwsc" "{{chip}}" --usb

# Run the daemon against a MIDI device: a real FM-1 with Agent Deck, or the emulator
# started with `just emu-run downloads/agtdeck-{{agtdeck_version}}.fwsc uc25hq80 --usb`.
agtdeck-run backend="herdr" *args: agtdeck-clone
    uv run --locked --all-groups python vendor/fm-1-agent-deck/host/agtdeck.py --backend "{{backend}}" {{args}}

# ---- Morse: pocket Morse code machine (firmware/morse + host/morse) ----------

# Morse's firmware is its own repo (github.com/daviddwlee84/fm1-morse), a submodule at firmware/morse; it is built
# here with third_party/fm1-base (its own fm1-base submodule is for building it alone, and is not fetched here).
# Release package (identity FM-1_41 + XXYYZZ): just morse-release 0.3
morse-release version: fw-setup fw-toolchain
    JIELI_TOOLCHAIN="$PWD/tools/jieli/toolchain" AC79_SDK="$PWD/tools/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK" \
      uv run --locked --all-groups python "{{fm1_base}}/tools/build.py" firmware/morse --release "{{version}}"

# morse.c, learn.c and content.c on this computer: code table, timing, player, keyer, decoder, flash cards, content.
morse-unit:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p build
    cc -Wall -Wextra -o build/morse_test firmware/morse/tests/morse_test.c
    build/morse_test

# Host unit tests (protocol vectors shared with firmware/morse/tests/basic.txt, the host's answers).
morse-test:
    uv run --locked --all-groups pytest -q host/tests/test_morse.py

# The firmware in the emulator with the virtual USB cable plugged in (pair with `just morse-type` / `morse-send`).
morse-emu chip="uc25hq80":
    just emu-run firmware/morse/build/morse.fwsc "{{chip}}" --usb

# What you key or type on the FM-1, typed into the focused app (macOS, Accessibility). --dry-run prints it.
morse-type *args:
    PYTHONPATH=host uv run --locked --all-groups python -m morse type {{args}}

# The FM-1 plays TEXT as received ("-": lines from stdin).
morse-send +text:
    PYTHONPATH=host uv run --locked --all-groups python -m morse send {{text}}

# The host against a text stand-in for the FM-1 (lines you type are what it "read").
morse-sim:
    PYTHONPATH=host uv run --locked --all-groups python -m morse --simulate type --dry-run

# ---- upstream watch -----------------------------------------------------------

# Latest upstream releases, to compare with the version table in docs/resources.md.
fm1-versions:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    for r in jvitkauskas/m-flasher jvitkauskas/m-bootloader isod89/sloop-fm1 isod89/sloop3-fm1 \
             joakimeriksson/fm1-emu kevinelliott/fm-1-agent-deck charlesvestal/fm1-base charlesvestal/fm1-ctl; do
      printf '%-32s %s\n' "$r" "$(gh api "repos/$r/releases" --jq '.[0] | "\(.tag_name)  \(.published_at[0:10])\(if .prerelease then "  prerelease" else "" end)"' 2>/dev/null || echo '(no releases)')"
    done

# ---- device: read-only ------------------------------------------------------

# List units in download mode and units running on USB MIDI.
fm1-find:
```

Add voice-fetch recipe and download speaking firmwares

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("Justfile")
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('remote_version := "0.3.6"\n', '''remote_version := "0.3.6"
# firmwares that speak (docs/dev/tts.md): listened to in the emulator only
speak37_version := "1.0"
spellbox_version := "0.3"
dx386_version := "2.0"
chimera_version := "0.8.0"
evilgenius_version := "0.1.4"
''', 1)
anchor = '''    fetch Quixotic7/RemoteFM1 "v{{remote_version}}" "remote-{{remote_version}}.fwsc"
'''
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, anchor + '''
# Download the community firmwares that speak (docs/dev/tts.md) and verify them against the release digests.
# For listening in the emulator (`just emu-run downloads/FILE`); none is planned for the unit.
voice-fetch:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p downloads && cd downloads
    fetch() { # repo tag asset
      gh release download "$2" -R "$1" -p "$3" --clobber
      want=$(gh api "repos/$1/releases/tags/$2" --jq ".assets[] | select(.name==\\"$3\\") | .digest" | sed 's/^sha256://')
      got=$(shasum -a 256 "$3" | cut -d' ' -f1)
      if [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" = "$got" ]; then echo "ok   $3  $got"; else echo "FAIL $3: got $got, release says ${want:-<no digest>}" >&2; exit 1; fi
    }
    fetch genkigenki/Speak37 "v{{speak37_version}}" "speak37-fm1-{{speak37_version}}.fwsc"
    fetch pjac1810/spellbox "v{{spellbox_version}}" "spellbox-{{spellbox_version}}.fwsc"
    fetch seajaysec/386-DX-FM1-KaraokeBot "v{{dx386_version}}" "386dx-{{dx386_version}}.fwsc"
    fetch shan-sherif/fm-1-chimera-vocal "v{{chimera_version}}" "chimera-{{chimera_version}}.fwsc"
    fetch Quixotic7/evilgenius "v{{evilgenius_version}}" "evilgenius-{{evilgenius_version}}.fwsc"
''', 1)
p.write_text(s)
EOF
just voice-fetch
```

````text
# Text to Speech

A portable, dependency-free **formant (Klatt-style) text-to-speech** synth core.
The goal is *"robotic but understandable"* speech that fits a tight resource
envelope. It synthesizes the output audio in a streaming fashion, to keep memory usage minimal.

The core is C++17, **float-only math, no allocation in the audio inner loop, and
no third-party dependency** (not even kissfft or TFLM).

<!--TOC-->

- [Public API](#public-api)
- [Memory \& compute](#memory--compute)
- [Tests](#tests)
- [Tuning](#tuning)

## Public API

Single public entry header [`include/tts/tts.h`](include/tts/tts.h) — include
only this:

```cpp
tts::VoiceParams voice = tts::DefaultVoiceParams();
tts::StreamSynth synth(voice, arena, arena_size);   // caller-supplied arena
tts::StreamOptions opts; opts.sample_rate = 22050.0f;
synth.BeginText("hello world", opts);               // on-device G2P
// or synth.BeginIpa("h\u0259lo\u028a", opts);      // raw IPA, bypass G2P
float buf[256];
for (int n; (n = synth.Read(buf, 256)) > 0; )       // streams; never buffers
  emit(buf, n);                                       // ... the whole utterance
```

The remaining headers under `include/tts/` (`synth_stream.h`, `config.h`,
`klatt.h`, `synth_internal.h`, `phonemes.h`, `g2p_dict.h`) are transitive types
that `StreamSynth` exposes by value; the G2P internals are private in `src/`.

## Memory & compute

| Resource | Size | Notes |
| -------- | ---- | ----- |
| Flash (dictionary) | ~150 KiB | baked common-word G2P table (`src/g2p_dict_data.h`) |
| Flash (code) | ~tens KiB | Klatt synth + G2P rules (linked into firmware `.text`) |
| RAM (static) | ~0 extra | per-frame tracks live in the caller-supplied arena |
| RAM (arena peak) | few KiB | reuses idle TFLM tensor arena after STT finishes |
| Heap (transient) | few KiB | tokenizer / segment list in `BeginText` only; none in `Read()` |

`Read()` renders one frame at a time; the full utterance PCM is never buffered.
Recognition and synthesis never run at once, so the synth adds essentially **no
static SRAM** beyond the shared arena the app already provisions.

### Latency @ 250 MHz

| Operation | Latency | Compute (approx.) | Notes |
| --------- | ------- | ----------------- | ----- |
| `StreamSynth` letter/digit | ~400–800 ms reply | ~0.5 MMAC typical (~1 MMAC/s out) | e.g. "bee" ~430 ms, "zero" ~830 ms @ 22.05 kHz |
| `Read()` inner loop | faster than real-time | ~5 KMAC per 5 ms frame (~1 MMAC/s out) | six biquad resonators × ~110 samples/frame |

Measured output lengths with `DefaultVoiceParams()` at 22.05 kHz: "ee" ~320 ms,
"bee" ~430 ms, "seven" ~760 ms, "double u" ~1.0 s. `Read()` renders one frame at
a time; the full utterance PCM is never buffered. Recognition and synthesis never
run at once.

## Tests

`tests/tts_test.cc` (TFLM `micro_test.h`) covers the G2P front-end (text → phone
tokens, number normalization) and an end-to-end `StreamSynth` smoke test
(non-empty, in-range PCM). It runs entirely on the host.

## Tuning

Voice parameters ship as compiled-in defaults in `DefaultVoiceParams()`
(`src/config.cc`). Optional `.cfg` files can override them at runtime on the
desktop build for listening tests; the firmware uses the defaults only.

// tts -- portable, dependency-free formant (Klatt-style) text-to-speech.
//
// This is the single public header for the module. Include only this; it pulls
// in the public synth types. The remaining headers under include/tts/ are the
// transitive implementation types that StreamSynth exposes by value (the Klatt
// resonators, the per-frame parameter tracks, the voice config); the G2P
// internals live privately in src/.
//
// The core is intentionally self-contained: C++17, float-only math, small fixed
// state, no allocation in the audio inner loop, and NO third-party dependency
// (not even kissfft or TFLM). Only the streaming synthesis path used on the MCU
// is included here.
//
// Typical use (the platform glue -- USB command loop, arena ownership -- lives
// in the example, not here):
//
//   tts::VoiceParams voice = tts::DefaultVoiceParams();
//   tts::StreamSynth synth(voice, arena, arena_size);
//   tts::StreamOptions opts; opts.sample_rate = 22050.0f;
//   synth.BeginText("hello world", opts);          // or BeginIpa(...)
//   float buf[256];
//   for (int n; (n = synth.Read(buf, 256)) > 0; )  // stream PCM, never buffers
//     emit(buf, n);

#ifndef TTS_TTS_H_
#define TTS_TTS_H_

#include "config.h"        // tts::VoiceParams, tts::DefaultVoiceParams
#include "synth_stream.h"  // tts::StreamSynth, StreamOptions, StreamStatus

#endif  // TTS_TTS_H_
````
