```text
# Portable formant (Klatt-style) text-to-speech synth core.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.13)

add_library(tts STATIC
  src/phonemes.cc
  src/klatt.cc
  src/synth_internal.cc
  src/synth_stream.cc
  src/config.cc
)

target_include_directories(tts
  PUBLIC  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include
  PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include/tts
          ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)

# The grapheme-to-phoneme front end is the shared g2p library (also used by
# neural-tts); synth_stream.h exposes g2p::Lexicon, so the dependency is
# PUBLIC.
target_link_libraries(tts PUBLIC g2p)

target_compile_features(tts PUBLIC cxx_std_17)

if(MOONSHINE_MICRO_BUILD_TESTS)
  add_subdirectory(tests)
endif()
// Streaming, caller-arena formant synthesizer for the RP2350 (and desktop).
//
// Unlike the batch Synthesize() (synth.h), which materializes the whole PCM
// waveform in a std::vector and peak-normalizes it, StreamSynth produces audio
// in arbitrary-length chunks on demand and never holds the full utterance:
//
//   * the second-largest buffer -- the per-frame parameter tracks -- lives in a
//     caller-supplied arena (on the MCU this is the otherwise-idle TFLM tensor
//     arena, since recognition and synthesis never run at the same time);
//   * the largest buffer -- the PCM -- is never materialized; frames are
//     rendered one at a time into a tiny scratch and copied into the caller's
//     output buffer as Read() drains them.
//
// Because the global peak isn't known while streaming, the final loudness stage
// differs from batch: a fixed VoiceParams::output_gain plus a soft limiter
// replace peak-normalization. Everything upstream (segments, smoothing, F0) is
// the shared, bit-identical code in synth_internal.*.
//
// Lifecycle: construct, begin an utterance, pull audio chunks until done:

#ifndef TTS_SYNTH_STREAM_H_
#define TTS_SYNTH_STREAM_H_

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <optional>
#include <string>

#include "config.h"
#include "g2p/g2p_dict.h"  // g2p::Lexicon
#include "klatt.h"
#include "synth_internal.h"

namespace tts {

// Per-utterance runtime options (the same shape as SynthOptions).
struct StreamOptions {
  float sample_rate = 22050.0f;
  float speed = 1.0f;     // >1 faster, <1 slower
  bool question = false;  // final rising boundary tone
};

// Return / status codes (0 == success, negative == error).
enum StreamStatus {
  kStreamOk = 0,
  kStreamErrBadArg = -1,     // null/empty argument
  kStreamErrArenaFull = -2,  // utterance needs more arena than provided
  kStreamErrNoPhones = -3,   // text/IPA produced no usable phones
};

class StreamSynth {
 public:
  // `vp` must outlive the synth (not copied). `arena`/`arena_size` is all the
  // working memory the audio path will use; nothing is heap-allocated per
  // sample. A few KiB of transient heap is used by the front-end (tokenizer /
  // segment list) inside Begin*, bounded by the input length.
  StreamSynth(const VoiceParams& vp, uint8_t* arena, size_t arena_size);

  // Begin a new utterance from plain text (on-device G2P). `overrides`, if
  // non-null, is consulted first (proper nouns etc.). Resets all stream state.
  int BeginText(const char* text, const StreamOptions& opts,
                const g2p::Lexicon* overrides = nullptr);

  // Begin a new utterance from an IPA string (bypasses the G2P; for isolating
  // the synthesizer). Resets all stream state.
  int BeginIpa(const char* ipa, const StreamOptions& opts);

  // Pull up to `max_samples` mono float samples (roughly [-1, 1]) into `out`.
  // Returns the number of samples written; 0 means the utterance is fully
  // drained (done() is then true). Chunks may be any size.
  int Read(float* out, int max_samples);

  bool done() const {
    return frame_idx_ >= nframes_ && frame_buf_pos_ >= frame_buf_len_;
  }
  int sample_rate() const { return sr_hz_; }
  int total_samples() const {
    return static_cast<int>(nframes_ * static_cast<size_t>(spf_));
  }

 private:
  int BeginPhones(const std::vector<std::string>& phones,
                  const StreamOptions& opts);
  void ArenaReset() { arena_used_ = 0; }
  float* ArenaFloats(size_t count);
  uint8_t* ArenaBytes(size_t count, size_t align);
  void RenderNextFrame();

  const VoiceParams& vp_;
  uint8_t* arena_;
  size_t arena_size_;
  size_t arena_used_ = 0;

  synth_detail::ParamTracks tracks_;
  size_t nframes_ = 0;
  int spf_ = 0;
  int sr_hz_ = 0;

  std::optional<KlattSynth> synth_;

  // Frame-at-a-time render scratch + drain cursor.
  float* frame_buf_ = nullptr;  // spf_ samples, in the arena
  int frame_buf_pos_ = 0;
  int frame_buf_len_ = 0;
  size_t frame_idx_ = 0;  // next frame to render

  // Global emitted-sample index, for edge fades.
  size_t out_idx_ = 0;
  size_t total_samples_ = 0;
  int fade_ = 0;
  float gain_ = 1.0f;
};

}  // namespace tts

#endif  // TTS_SYNTH_STREAM_H_

// English phoneme inventory for the formant synthesizer.
//
// Keyed by IPA (UTF-8), matching the G2P front-end output.
// Each entry carries the data a Klatt-style cascade synthesizer needs:
//   * a steady-state formant target (vowels / sonorants), or a formant
//     "locus" the transition engine aims at (obstruents),
//   * source amplitudes that decide what excites the resonators, and
//   * an intrinsic duration that prosody later scales.
//
// The numbers are adult-male reference values drawn from standard phonetics
// tables (Peterson-Barney vowels, Klatt locus theory). They are a starting
// point tuned for "robotic but understandable", not for naturalness, and are
// expected to be adjusted by ear.
//
// Only monophthongs and single consonants live in the table. Diphthongs and
// affricates are expanded to a pair of base symbols by the tokenizer (see
// TokenizeIpa), so the transition engine renders the glide/closure for free.

#ifndef TTS_PHONEMES_H_
#define TTS_PHONEMES_H_

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace tts {

enum class PhoneClass : uint8_t {
  kVowel,
  kNasal,
  kStop,
  kFricative,
  kApproximant,
  kLateral,
  kSilence,
};

enum class Source : uint8_t {
  kVoiced,     // glottal pulse only
  kVoiceless,  // noise only (frication / aspiration)
  kMixed,      // voicing + frication (voiced fricatives)
  kSilence,
};

struct Phone {
  const char* ipa;  // UTF-8 key
  PhoneClass cls;
  Source src;

  // Formant targets (vowels/sonorants) or consonant loci (obstruents), Hz.
  float f1, f2, f3;
  // Resonator bandwidths, Hz.
  float b1, b2, b3;

  float dur_ms;  // intrinsic duration before prosodic scaling

  // Nasal pole/zero (nasals only); 0 if unused.
  float fnp, fnz;

  // Frication / burst noise centre frequency, Hz (fricatives + stop bursts).
  float fric_cf;

  // Relative source amplitudes in [0, 1].
  float av;  // voicing
  float af;  // frication
  float ah;  // aspiration
};

// Look up a phone by exact IPA key in the built-in default table. Returns
// nullptr if unknown. (Runtime synthesis goes through VoiceParams::Lookup so a
// loaded config can override these; this is just the compiled-in default.)
const Phone* LookupPhone(const std::string& ipa);

// A fresh, mutable copy of the built-in default phone table. The `ipa` pointers
// still reference static string literals (stable for the program lifetime), so
// callers may mutate the numeric fields but must not free or rewrite `ipa`.
std::vector<Phone> DefaultPhoneTable();

// NOTE: the IPA tokenizer (TokenizeIpa) moved to the shared g2p library
```

```text
// clang-format on

const std::unordered_map<std::string, const Phone*>& PhoneIndex() {
  static const std::unordered_map<std::string, const Phone*> index = [] {
    std::unordered_map<std::string, const Phone*> m;
    for (const Phone& p : kPhones) {
      m.emplace(p.ipa, &p);
    }
    return m;
  }();
  return index;
}

}  // namespace

const Phone* LookupPhone(const std::string& ipa) {
  const auto& idx = PhoneIndex();
  auto it = idx.find(ipa);
  return it == idx.end() ? nullptr : it->second;
}

std::vector<Phone> DefaultPhoneTable() {
  return std::vector<Phone>(kPhones.begin(), kPhones.end());
}

}  // namespace tts
```

```text
size_t Utf8Len(unsigned char lead) {
  if (lead < 0x80) return 1;
  if ((lead >> 5) == 0x6) return 2;
  if ((lead >> 4) == 0xE) return 3;
  if ((lead >> 3) == 0x1E) return 4;
  return 1;
}

      if (plen == 0 || i + plen > n) continue;
      if (ipa.compare(i, plen, r.pattern) == 0) {
```

````text
add73ebf3c8fed306225dffd2e0229aee1a38e8f Mon Oct 21 09:16:45 2024 +0200
### Updates to base python_wizard

- Added "lpcplayer" package (based on talkie) to support Play feature in GUI. 

- Added dirty support for other LPC coding tables. TMS5100 is default now.
  ```
    -T {tms5220,tms5100}, --tablesVariant {tms5220,tms5100}
                          Tables variant
  ```                        

- Support for python formatted output
  ```
    -f {arduino,C,hex,python}, --outputFormat {arduino,C,hex,python}
                          Output file format
  ```
- Small fixes and enhancements in GUI



------
This project is a python port of the great macOS tool BlueWizard (https://github.com/patrick99e99/BlueWizard), which is written in objective C and I was not familiar enough with this C dialect to make an portable command line application out of it.

It is intended to convert (voice) audio streams into LPC bitstreams used in the TMS 5220 chip or e.g. in the Arduino library Talkie. Now you can generate your own LPC streams and make your chips say the things you want them to.

Compared to BlueWizard some minor features have been added:
1. Ability to downsample a wave file automatically
2. Automated output formatters for C, Arduino (C-Dialect) and plain hex

Prerequisites:
- Python 2.7
- SciPy >= 0.18.1

Usage: 
```
       python_wizard.py [-h] [-u UNVOICEDTHRESHOLD] [-w WINDOWWIDTH] [-U] [-V]
                        [-S] [-p] [-a PREEMPHASISALPHA] [-d] [-r PITCHRANGE]
                        [-F FRAMERATE] [-m SUBMULTIPLETHRESHOLD]
                        [-f {arduino,C,hex}]
                        filename

positional arguments:
  filename              File name of a .wav file to be processed

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -u UNVOICEDTHRESHOLD, --unvoicedThreshold UNVOICEDTHRESHOLD
                        Unvoiced frame threshold
  -w WINDOWWIDTH, --windowWidth WINDOWWIDTH
                        Window width in frames
  -U, --normalizeUnvoicedRMS
                        Normalize unvoiced frame RMS
  -V, --normalizeVoicedRMS
                        Normalize voiced frame RMS
  -S, --includeExplicitStopFrame
                        Create explicit stop frame (needed e.g. for Talkie)
  -p, --preEmphasis     Pre emphasize sound to improve quality of translation
  -a PREEMPHASISALPHA, --preEmphasisAlpha PREEMPHASISALPHA
                        Emphasis coefficient
  -d, --debug           Enable (lots) of debug output
  -r PITCHRANGE, --pitchRange PITCHRANGE
                        Comma separated range of available voice pitch in Hz.
                        Default: 50,500
  -F FRAMERATE, --frameRate FRAMERATE
  -m SUBMULTIPLETHRESHOLD, --subMultipleThreshold SUBMULTIPLETHRESHOLD
                        sub-multiple threshold
  -f {arduino,C,hex}, --outputFormat {arduino,C,hex}
                        Output file format
````

```text
class userSettings(object):

    tablesVariant = "tms5100"

    def import_from_argparse(self, raw):
        v = vars(raw)
        self.import_from_dict(v)

    def import_from_dict(self, input_dict):
        error_list = []
        for key in input_dict:
            if key == 'pitchRange':
                (self.minimumPitchInHZ, self.maximumPitchInHZ) = [int(x) for x in input_dict[key].split(",")]
            else:
                try:
                    self.__setattr__(key, type(self.__getattribute__(key))(input_dict[key]))
                except AttributeError:
                    logging.debug("Discarding argument {}={}".format(key, input_dict[key]))
                except ValueError:
                    error_list.append(key)
        if len(error_list) > 0:
            return error_list
        else:
            return None

    def export_to_odict(self):
        r = OrderedDict()
        for k in self.availableSettings:
            r[k] = self.__getattribute__(k)
        return r


settings = userSettings()
```

```text
import logging

class LpcDecoder:
    """Decode LPC encoded data"""
    
    def __init__(self, tms_coeff, batch=False):
        self.bitpos = 0
        self.tables = tms_coeff
        self.batch = batch
    
    def rev_byte(self, byte):
        out_byte = 0
        for i in range(8):
            bit = (byte >> (7 - i)) & 1
            out_byte = out_byte | (bit << i)
        return out_byte
    
    def get_bits(self, bits):
        listpos = self.bitpos // 8
        bitpos = self.bitpos % 8
        try:
            databyte = self.rev_byte(self.data[listpos])
            if bitpos + bits + 1 > 8 and listpos + 1 < len(self.data):
                databyte = databyte << 8 | self.rev_byte(self.data[listpos + 1])
                ret_bits = (databyte >> (15 - (bitpos + bits) + 1)) & ((1 << bits) - 1)
                self.bitpos += bits
            else:
                ret_bits = (databyte >> abs(7 - (bitpos + bits) + 1)) & (abs(1 << bits) - 1)
                self.bitpos += bits
        except IndexError as e:
            print(e)
            print("no more bits error")
            return -1
        return ret_bits
    
    def decode(self, lpc_data):
        self.bitpos = 0
        self.data = lpc_data
        synth = {}
        target_synth = {}
        synth['K1'] = 0
        synth['K2'] = 0
        synth['K3'] = 0
        synth['K4'] = 0
        synth['K5'] = 0
        synth['K6'] = 0
        synth['K7'] = 0
        synth['K8'] = 0
        synth['K9'] = 0
        synth['K10'] = 0
        synth['period'] = 0
        synth['energy'] = 0
        for k in synth:
            target_synth[k] = synth[k]
        period_counter = 0
        frame_counter = 0
        
        x0 = x1 = x2 = x3 = x4 = x5 = x6 = x7 = x8 = x9 = x10 = 0
        
        samples = []
        logging.debug(f" Frame:NN - | Energy   | R | Pitch     | koeff")
        while True:
            debug_r=""
            debug_p=""
            debug_k=""
            
            energy = self.get_bits(self.tables.energy_bits)
            debug_e=f" {str(bin(energy))[2:].zfill(self.tables.energy_bits)}, {energy:<2} |"

            if energy == -1:
                break
            if energy == 0:
                target_synth['energy'] = 0
            elif energy == 0b1111:
                logging.debug(f" Frame:{frame_counter:2d} - | 1111, 15 |")
                break
            else:
                target_synth['energy'] = self.tables.energytable[energy]
                repeat = self.get_bits(1)
                debug_r=f" {repeat} |"
                period = self.get_bits(self.tables.pitch_bits)
                target_synth['period'] = self.tables.pitchtable[period]
                debug_p=f"{str(bin(period))[2:].zfill(self.tables.pitch_bits)}, {period:<2} |"
                debug_k=""
                if repeat == 0:
                    for k in range(10):
                        if period == 0 and k >= 4:
                            continue
                        k_bits=self.get_bits(self.tables.kbits[k])
                        target_synth[f"K{k + 1}"] = self.tables.ktable[k][k_bits]
                        debug_k+=f' {str(bin(k_bits))[2:].zfill(self.tables.kbits[k])}, {k_bits:>2} |'
            
            logging.debug(f" Frame:{frame_counter:2d} - |{debug_e}{debug_r}{debug_p}{debug_k}")

            if frame_counter == 0:
                # copy target to current keys
                for k in target_synth:
                    synth[k] = target_synth[k]
            
            interp_count = 0
            for sample_num in range(200):
                # interpolation time
                if interp_count == 0 and sample_num > 0:
                    interp_period = int(sample_num / 25)
                    for k in target_synth:
                        synth[k] += (target_synth[k] - synth[k]) >> self.tables.interp_coeff[interp_period]
                
                if synth['energy'] == 0:
                    u10 = 0
                elif synth['period'] > 0:
                    # Voiced frame
                    if period_counter < synth['period']:
                        period_counter += 1
                    else:
                        period_counter = 0
                    if period_counter < len(self.tables.chirptable):
                        u10 = int(self.tables.chirptable[period_counter] * synth['energy'] >> 6)
                    else:
                        u10 = 0
                else:
                    # Unvoiced
                    synthRand = 1
                    synthRand = (synthRand >> 1) ^ (0xB800 if synthRand & 1 else 0)
                    u10 = synth['energy'] if (synthRand & 1) else -synth['energy']
                
                # Lattice filter forward path
                u9 = u10 - int((synth['K10'] * x9) >> 9)
                u8 = u9 - int((synth['K9'] * x8) >> 9)
                u7 = u8 - int((synth['K8'] * x7) >> 9)
                u6 = u7 - int((synth['K7'] * x6) >> 9)
                u5 = u6 - int((synth['K6'] * x5) >> 9)
                u4 = u5 - int((synth['K5'] * x4) >> 9)
                u3 = u4 - int((synth['K4'] * x3) >> 9)
                u2 = u3 - int((synth['K3'] * x2) >> 9)
                u1 = u2 - int((synth['K2'] * x1) >> 9)
                u0 = u1 - int((synth['K1'] * x0) >> 9)
                
                # Output clamp
                if u0 > 511:
                    u0 = 511
                if u0 < -512:
                    u0 = -512
                
                # Lattice filter reverse path
                x9 = x8 + int((synth['K9'] * u8) >> 9)
                x8 = x7 + int((synth['K8'] * u7) >> 9)
                x7 = x6 + int((synth['K7'] * u6) >> 9)
                x6 = x5 + int((synth['K6'] * u5) >> 9)
                x5 = x4 + int((synth['K5'] * u4) >> 9)
                x4 = x3 + int((synth['K4'] * u3) >> 9)
                x3 = x2 + int((synth['K3'] * u2) >> 9)
                x2 = x1 + int((synth['K2'] * u1) >> 9)
                x1 = x0 + int((synth['K1'] * u0) >> 9)
                x0 = u0
                
                sample = (u0 >> 2) + 0x80
                samples.append(sample)
                interp_count = (interp_count + 1) % 25
            # return
            frame_counter += 1
        if self.batch:
            return (self.bitpos // 8) + 1
        else:
            return samples
from typing import NamedTuple

    interp_coeff: tuple
```

```text
from pywizard.tools import BitHelpers
from pywizard.HexConverter import HexConverter
import logging


class BitPacker(object):
    @classmethod
    def raw_stream(cls, processor):
        frameData = processor.frames
        parametersList = [x.parameters() for x in frameData]
        raw_data = FrameDataBinaryEncoder.process(processor.codingTable,
                                                  parametersList)
        return HexConverter.preprocess(raw_data)

    @classmethod
    def pack(cls, processor):
        frameData = processor.frames
        parametersList = [x.parameters() for x in frameData]
        raw_data = FrameDataBinaryEncoder.process(processor.codingTable,
                                                  parametersList)
        return HexConverter.process(raw_data)


class FrameDataBinaryEncoder(object):
    @classmethod
    def process(cls, codingTable, parametersList):
        bits = codingTable.bits
        binary = ""
        for parameters in parametersList:
            params = codingTable.parameters()
            for (param_name, idx) in zip(params, range(len(params))):
                if param_name not in parameters:
                    break
                value = parameters[param_name]
                binaryValue = BitHelpers.valueToBinary(value, bits[idx])
                logging.debug("param_name={} idx={} value={} binaryValue={}".format(param_name, idx, value, binaryValue))
                binary += binaryValue
        return cls.nibblesFrom(binary)

    @classmethod
    def nibblesFrom(cls, binary):
        nibbles = []
        while len(binary) >= 4:
            nibble = binary[0:4]
            binary = binary[4:]
            nibbles.append(nibble)
        return nibbles
from pywizard.tools import formatSpecifier
from pywizard.userSettings import settings
import logging


class HexConverter(object):
    formats = {
        "arduino": formatSpecifier("const unsigned char FILENAME[] PROGMEM = {",
                                   "0x{:02X}",
                                   ",",
                                   "};"),
        "C":       formatSpecifier("const unsigned char FILENAME[] = {",
                                   "0x{:02X}",
                                   ",",
                                   "};"),
        "hex":     formatSpecifier("",
                                   "{:02x}",
                                   " ",
                                   ""),
        "python":   formatSpecifier("(",
                                    "0x{:02X}",
                                    ",",
                                    ")"),
                    }

    @classmethod
    def preprocess(cls, nibbles):
        '''
        Creates nibble swapped, reversed data bytestream as hex value list.
        Used to be NibbleBitReverser, NibbleSwitcher and HexConverter
        '''
        result = []
        for u, l in zip(nibbles[0::2], nibbles[1::2]):
            raw = (u+l)[::-1]
            result.append(int(raw, base=2))
        return result

    @classmethod
    def process(cls, nibbles):
        formatter = cls.formats[settings.outputFormat]
        logging.debug("Will format output using {} ({})".format(settings.outputFormat, formatter))
        result = [formatter.formatString.format(data) for data in cls.preprocess(nibbles)]
        return formatter.header + formatter.separator.join(result) + formatter.trailer
from lpcplayer.tables import tables


class CodingTable(object):
    kStopFrameIndex = 15

    rms = (0.0, 52.0, 87.0, 123.0, 174.0, 246.0, 348.0, 491.0, 694.0, 981.0,
           1385.0, 1957.0, 2764.0, 3904.0, 5514.0, 7789.0)

    def __init__(self, name):
        chip = tables[name]

        for k in range(1, 11):
            ks = list(chip.ktable[k-1])
            for i, k_value in enumerate(ks):
                ks[i] = k_value/512
            setattr(self, 'k'+str(k), ks)

        self.pitch = chip.pitchtable
        self.bits = (chip.energy_bits,)\
                     + (1,)\
                     + (chip.pitch_bits,)\
                     + chip.kbits

    def kSizeFor(self, k):
        if k > 10:
            raise Exception("RangeError")
        return 1 << self.bits[k+2]

    def rmsSize(self):
        return 1 << self.bits[0]

    def pitchSize(self):
        return 1 << self.bits[2]

    def kBinFor(self, k):
        mapping = {1: self.k1,  2: self.k2, 3: self.k3, 4: self.k4, 5: self.k5,
                   6: self.k6, 7: self.k7, 8: self.k8, 9: self.k9, 10: self.k10
                   }
        return mapping[k]

    @classmethod
    def parameters(cls):
        return [
             'kParameterGain',
             'kParameterRepeat',
             'kParameterPitch',
             'kParameterK1',
             'kParameterK2',
             'kParameterK3',
             'kParameterK4',
             'kParameterK5',
             'kParameterK6',
             'kParameterK7',
             'kParameterK8',
             'kParameterK9',
             'kParameterK10'
              ]

    bits = (4, 1, 6, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3)
```

````text
# firmware/common

Small modules shared by this repo's fm1-base apps. MIT. Each is a `.h` with the
API and usage, and a `.c` that the app includes into fm1-base's unity build.

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| `hostlink` | An app's own SysEx conversation with a program on the computer, over USB or Bluetooth: framing under `F0 7D id0 id1 ver`, HELLO on every transport until the host answers, HEARTBEAT after on the transport it answered by, host presence with a timeout, a new HELLO after a new USB session or a lost Bluetooth link. Bluetooth needs `ble_stack = "own"` (JieLi's stack drops incoming SysEx); `hl_sx_packet` puts the SysEx packets back together. |
| `ledfx` | Per-LED patterns on the single-colour LEDs: off, glow, mid, lit, pulse, blink, double blink, fast. Turns them into `plat_lights` + `plat_lights_mid` once a frame. |
| `chime` | A two-operator FM voice with a short note queue for notification sounds, mixed into the app's render. |

## Using them in an app

`fm1.toml`:

```toml
include = ["../common"]
```

`app.c`, after `#include "fastmath.h"` (chime needs `fm_sinf`, `fm_exp2f`):

```c
#include "hostlink.c"
#include "ledfx.c"
#include "chime.c"
```

They call fm1-base's `plat_*` functions, which are in scope in the unity build.
They keep no flash state.

`just fw-common-test` builds and runs `tests/` on the computer (hostlink's packet
cutting and reassembly). `firmware/conductor` is the first user; its `tests/basic.txt` exercises all three
in the host simulator. `firmware/morse` (now its own repo, a submodule) carries a copy of `hostlink` and `ledfx` in its `common/`; change
them here and copy them there, or the other way round.
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */

 * Figures are short note lists (MIDI note, length in ms); add your own with chime_notes(). */
````

```c
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* lpc: a TMS5220-style LPC speech decoder (the Speak & Spell's format, as the Talkie library and python_wizard
 * write it): ten-pole lattice filter, chirp or noise excitation, 8 kHz out. No platform calls, no allocation: the
 * same file builds on the computer (host/voicelab, tests/) and in an fm1-base app.
 *
 *   lpc_t s;
 *   lpc_begin(&s, word, word_len, 25);           a stream of frames, 25 ms each (python_wizard -F 25; 10 for -F 10)
 *   n = lpc_render(&s, pcm, 256);                up to 256 samples at 8 kHz (int16); fewer once the word ends
 *   lpc_done(&s)                                 the stop frame (energy 15) or the end of the data was reached
 *
 * The stream: per frame energy (4 bits; 0 silence, 15 stop), repeat (1), pitch (6; 0 unvoiced), then K1..K10
 * (5 5 4 4 4 4 4 3 3 3 bits) unless repeated, only K1..K4 when unvoiced. Bits are taken from each byte's lowest
 * first, each field assembled highest bit first: python_wizard's "nibble swapped, reversed" bytes. Tables: the
 * TMS5220's, from python_wizard's lpcplayer/tables.py (MIT, ptwz), which has them from MAME. */
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

typedef struct {
    const uint8_t *p;
    uint32_t n, bit;                 /* the stream, its length in bytes, the next bit */
    uint16_t spf, pos, step;         /* samples a frame, the sample in the frame, samples between interpolations */
    int32_t cur[12], tgt[12];        /* energy, period, K1..K10 (Q9): now, and where this frame goes */
    int32_t x[10];                   /* the lattice's backward path */
    uint16_t pc, rng;                /* pitch period counter, the noise generator */
    uint8_t done, started, jump;
} lpc_t;

void lpc_begin(lpc_t *s, const uint8_t *data, uint32_t n, uint32_t frame_ms);
uint32_t lpc_render(lpc_t *s, int16_t *out, uint32_t n);
static inline int lpc_done(const lpc_t *s) { return s->done; }
/* the frames' total bit count, for sizes (a dry run over the stream: no synthesis) */
uint32_t lpc_frames(const uint8_t *data, uint32_t n);
```

```c
static int32_t lpc_bits(lpc_t *s, uint32_t k)
{
    int32_t v = 0;
    if (s->bit + k > s->n * 8u)
        return -1;
    while (k--) {
        v = (v << 1) | ((s->p[s->bit >> 3] >> (s->bit & 7u)) & 1);
        s->bit++;

    return v;
}

static int32_t lpc_k(uint32_t i, int32_t code)

    if (i == 1) return lpc_k2[code];
    if (i < 7) return lpc_k3_7[i - 2][code];
    return lpc_k8_10[i - 7][code];
}

/* the next frame into tgt; 0 = the stream ended (stop frame or no more bits) */
static int lpc_frame(lpc_t *s)
{
    int32_t e = lpc_bits(s, 4), rep, per, i;
    int was_voiced = s->tgt[1] > 0, was_silent = s->tgt[0] == 0;
    if (e < 0 || e == 15)
        return 0;
    if (e == 0) {
        s->tgt[0] = 0;
        s->jump = 0;
        return 1;
    }
    rep = lpc_bits(s, 1);
    per = lpc_bits(s, 6);
    if (rep < 0 || per < 0)
        return 0;
    s->tgt[0] = lpc_energy[e];
    s->tgt[1] = lpc_pitch[per];
    if (!rep) {
        uint32_t nk = per ? 10u : 4u;
        for (i = 0; i < (int32_t)nk; i++) {
            int32_t c = lpc_bits(s, lpc_kbits[i]);
            if (c < 0)
                return 0;
            s->tgt[2 + i] = lpc_k((uint32_t)i, c);
        }
        if (!per)
            for (i = 4; i < 10; i++)
                s->tgt[2 + i] = 0;
    }
    /* as the chip: no gliding across a change of voicing or out of silence */
    s->jump = was_silent || (was_voiced != (per > 0));
    return 1;
}

void lpc_begin(lpc_t *s, const uint8_t *data, uint32_t n, uint32_t frame_ms)
{
    uint32_t i;
    s->p = data;
    s->n = n;
    s->bit = 0;
    s->spf = (uint16_t)(LPC_RATE * (frame_ms ? frame_ms : 25u) / 1000u);
    s->step = (uint16_t)(s->spf / 8u ? s->spf / 8u : 1u);
    s->pos = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < 12; i++)
        s->cur[i] = s->tgt[i] = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < 10; i++)
        s->x[i] = 0;
    s->pc = 0;
    s->rng = 0x1FFF;
    s->done = 0;
    s->started = 0;
    s->jump = 1;
}

uint32_t lpc_render(lpc_t *s, int16_t *out, uint32_t n)
{
    uint32_t w = 0, i;
    while (w < n && !s->done) {
        int32_t u, k;
        if (s->pos == 0) {
            if (!lpc_frame(s)) {
                s->done = 1;
                break;
            }
            if (!s->started || s->jump)
                for (i = 0; i < 12; i++)
                    s->cur[i] = s->tgt[i];
            s->started = 1;
        } else if (s->pos % s->step == 0) {
            uint32_t ip = s->pos / s->step;
            if (ip < 8)
                for (i = 0; i < 12; i++)
                    s->cur[i] += (s->tgt[i] - s->cur[i]) >> lpc_interp[ip];
        }
        /* excitation */
        if (s->cur[0] == 0) {
            u = 0;
        } else if (s->cur[1] > 0) {
            if (++s->pc >= s->cur[1])
                s->pc = 0;
            u = s->pc < 52 ? (lpc_chirp[s->pc] * s->cur[0]) >> 6 : 0;
        } else {
            s->rng = (uint16_t)((s->rng >> 1) ^ ((s->rng & 1u) ? 0xB800u : 0u));
            u = (s->rng & 1u) ? s->cur[0] : -s->cur[0];
        }
        /* lattice: forward path, then the backward one */
        for (k = 9; k >= 0; k--)
            u -= (s->cur[2 + k] * s->x[k]) >> 9;
        if (u > 511) u = 511;
        if (u < -512) u = -512;
        for (k = 9; k >= 1; k--)
            s->x[k] = s->x[k - 1] + ((s->cur[2 + k - 1] * 0) >> 9);   /* replaced below */
        out[w++] = (int16_t)(u * 64);
        if (++s->pos >= s->spf)
            s->pos = 0;
    }
    return w;
}

uint32_t lpc_frames(const uint8_t *data, uint32_t n)
{
    lpc_t s;
    uint32_t frames = 0;
    lpc_begin(&s, data, n, 25);
    while (lpc_frame(&s))
        frames++;
    return frames;
}
```

```c
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* lpc.c on the computer: frames packed by hand as python_wizard packs them, decoded and checked.
 *   cc -I.. -o /tmp/lpc_test lpc_test.c && /tmp/lpc_test      (just fw-common-test) */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "../lpc.c"

static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, msg) do { if (!(c)) { printf("FAIL %s\n", msg); fails++; } } while (0)

/* python_wizard's packing: fields highest bit first into one bit string, each byte holding its first bit lowest */
static uint8_t buf[256];
static uint32_t nbits;
static void put(uint32_t v, uint32_t k)
{
    while (k--) {
        uint32_t b = (v >> k) & 1u;
        if (b)
            buf[nbits >> 3] |= (uint8_t)(1u << (nbits & 7u));
        nbits++;
    }
}
static void voiced(uint32_t e, uint32_t pitch, const uint32_t k[10])
{
    uint32_t i;
    put(e, 4), put(0, 1), put(pitch, 6);
    for (i = 0; i < 10; i++)
        put(k[i], lpc_kbits[i]);
}
static void unvoiced(uint32_t e, const uint32_t k[4])
{
    uint32_t i;
    put(e, 4), put(0, 1), put(0, 6);
    for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        put(k[i], lpc_kbits[i]);
}

int main(void)
{
    static const uint32_t kv[10] = {20, 10, 9, 7, 8, 8, 7, 4, 3, 4}, ku[4] = {25, 12, 8, 8};
    int16_t pcm[4000];
    uint32_t n, i, peak = 0, zeros = 0;
    lpc_t s;

    memset(buf, 0, sizeof buf);
    nbits = 0;
    put(0, 4);                       /* silence */
    voiced(10, 30, kv);              /* voiced */
    put(10, 4), put(1, 1), put(30, 6);   /* repeat: same K's */
    unvoiced(9, ku);                 /* unvoiced */
    put(15, 4);                      /* stop */
    CHECK(nbits == 4 + 50 + 11 + 29 + 4, "bit count of the frames");
    CHECK(lpc_frames(buf, (nbits + 7) / 8) == 4, "four frames before the stop");

    lpc_begin(&s, buf, (nbits + 7) / 8, 25);
    n = lpc_render(&s, pcm, 4000);
    CHECK(n == 4 * 200, "25 ms frames: 200 samples each at 8 kHz");
    CHECK(lpc_done(&s), "the stop frame ends it");
    for (i = 0; i < 200; i++)
        zeros += pcm[i] == 0;
    CHECK(zeros == 200, "a silent frame is silent");
    for (i = 200; i < n; i++) {
        uint32_t a = (uint32_t)(pcm[i] < 0 ? -pcm[i] : pcm[i]);
        peak = a > peak ? a : peak;
    }
    CHECK(peak > 64 && peak <= 512 * 64, "voiced and unvoiced frames make sound, within 10 bits");
    CHECK(lpc_render(&s, pcm, 100) == 0, "nothing after the end");

    lpc_begin(&s, buf, (nbits + 7) / 8, 10);
    n = 0;
    while (!lpc_done(&s)) {
        uint32_t got = lpc_render(&s, pcm + n, 7);   /* small, odd chunks */
        n += got;
        if (!got)
            break;
    }
    CHECK(n == 4 * 80, "10 ms frames: 80 samples each, chunked");

    lpc_begin(&s, buf, 5, 25);       /* cut in the middle of the voiced frame */
    n = lpc_render(&s, pcm, 4000);
    CHECK(n == 200 && lpc_done(&s), "a cut stream ends at the last whole frame");

    printf(fails ? "lpc: %d failed\n" : "lpc: ok\n", fails);
    return fails != 0;
}
```

```c
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* firmware/common/lpc.c on the computer: an LPC stream (python_wizard's bytes) to 8 kHz mono s16le.
 *   lpc_decode IN.lpc FRAME_MS OUT.raw */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "lpc.c"

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    static uint8_t data[1 << 20];
    int16_t pcm[256];
    size_t n;
    uint32_t got;
    lpc_t s;
    FILE *in, *out;
    if (argc != 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: lpc_decode IN.lpc FRAME_MS OUT.raw\n");
        return 2;
    }
    in = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
    out = fopen(argv[3], "wb");
    if (!in || !out) {
        perror("lpc_decode");
        return 1;
    }
    n = fread(data, 1, sizeof data, in);
    lpc_begin(&s, data, (uint32_t)n, (uint32_t)atoi(argv[2]));
    while ((got = lpc_render(&s, pcm, 256)) > 0)
        fwrite(pcm, 2, got, out);
    fclose(in);
    fclose(out);
    return 0;
}
```

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Moonshine's Klatt formant TTS (vendor/moonshine/micro/klatt-tts, MIT) on the computer: one utterance to a WAV.
//   klatt_render ipa|text INPUT OUT.wav [RATE]
// ipa: an IPA string (stress marks welcome), the G2P bypassed; text: plain English through Moonshine's own G2P.
// Prints the samples written and the arena the utterance needed.
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <vector>

#include "tts/tts.h"

static void put32(FILE *f, uint32_t v) { fwrite(&v, 4, 1, f); }
static void put16(FILE *f, uint16_t v) { fwrite(&v, 2, 1, f); }

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  if (argc < 4) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "usage: klatt_render ipa|text INPUT OUT.wav [RATE]\n");
    return 2;
  }
  const bool ipa = std::strcmp(argv[1], "ipa") == 0;
  const float rate = argc > 4 ? static_cast<float>(std::atof(argv[4])) : 22050.0f;
  static uint8_t arena[256 * 1024];
  tts::VoiceParams voice = tts::DefaultVoiceParams();
  tts::StreamSynth synth(voice, arena, sizeof arena);
  tts::StreamOptions opts;
  opts.sample_rate = rate;
  const int rc = ipa ? synth.BeginIpa(argv[2], opts) : synth.BeginText(argv[2], opts);
  if (rc != tts::kStreamOk) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "klatt_render: begin failed (%d) for %s\n", rc, argv[2]);
    return 1;
  }
  std::vector<int16_t> pcm;
  float buf[256];
  for (int n; (n = synth.Read(buf, 256)) > 0;)
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      float v = buf[i] * 32767.0f;
      v = v > 32767.0f ? 32767.0f : v < -32768.0f ? -32768.0f : v;
      pcm.push_back(static_cast<int16_t>(v));
    }
  FILE *f = std::fopen(argv[3], "wb");
  if (!f) {
    std::perror("klatt_render");
    return 1;
  }
  const uint32_t sr = static_cast<uint32_t>(synth.sample_rate()), bytes = static_cast<uint32_t>(pcm.size() * 2);
  std::fwrite("RIFF", 1, 4, f), put32(f, 36 + bytes), std::fwrite("WAVEfmt ", 1, 8, f);
  put32(f, 16), put16(f, 1), put16(f, 1), put32(f, sr), put32(f, sr * 2), put16(f, 2), put16(f, 16);
  std::fwrite("data", 1, 4, f), put32(f, bytes), std::fwrite(pcm.data(), 2, pcm.size(), f);
  std::fclose(f);
  std::printf("%zu samples at %u Hz\n", pcm.size(), sr);
  return 0;
}
```

````text
# 386 DX Engine

This project is inspired by and an homage to Alexei Shulgin, an artist in Russia who performed
briefly as 386 DX, which he billed as “[the world’s first cyberpunk band](https://youtu.be/iZNdhuB3Lqo).” At shows, Alexei was
introduced by a computerized voice announcing that the human onstage was merely a decoration.
He’d then “perform” onstage, air-strumming a computer keyboard like an electric guitar as
text-to-speech singing voices played along to MIDI covers of pop songs.

In so many ways, Alexei was—and still is—ahead of his time, and he’s been an inspiration to many
who’ve discovered his music in the decades since 386 DX performed.

Watch it sing: [the 386DX trailer](https://youtu.be/pwLnpyxqBS4).

The singing voice of [386DX](https://github.com/seajaysec/386-DX-FM1-KaraokeBot), the karaoke-robot
firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, on its own. Give it a line of English words, a syllable number and the
notes that syllable is sung on (one, or several for a held vowel), and it sings that syllable at
those pitches for exactly that long: a robot voice that keeps time.

It is built on [eSpeak NG](https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng): its English front end turns the
words into phonemes and syllables, and its Klatt cascade-parallel synthesizer makes the sound. Around
them 386DX grew its own singing layer: the line is pronounced once and each syllable placed on its
notes, vowels held across notes and glided between them, consonants kept to their natural length,
the voice shaped by four settings (body, breath, edge, glide). It started close to its origins and
has become its own thing as it was fitted to the FM-1: a small processor, 96 KB of RAM, a second
core to sing on and every byte of flash counted. So it is small: no files at run time (the English
data is compiled in), no allocation once it has started, and plain C.

The engine was written for the firmware, and the firmware is where it shows what it can do: the
[386DX karaoke robot](https://github.com/seajaysec/386-DX-FM1-KaraokeBot) sings songs and typed lines in
it on the M-VAVE FM-1, and its [web page](https://386dx.linecross.ing) runs this same engine, compiled to
WebAssembly, in the browser: write a line, give it notes, and hear it sing before you install anything.

That should make it easy to carry to other projects. `src/` is the engine; `examples/sing.c` sings
"hello robot friend" into a WAV file on a computer.

## The calls

```c
#include "speech.h"
int dx_speech_init(void);                                 /* once: 0 when the voice is ready */
int dx_speech_scan(const char *text);                     /* how many syllables it hears */
void dx_speech_sound(const uint8_t sound[4]);             /* body, breath, edge, glide, 0..100 */
int dx_speech_sing_into(int slot, const char *text, unsigned syllable,
                        const dx_sing_note_t *notes, unsigned count, unsigned expression,
                        int16_t *dst, unsigned capacity); /* 0: dst holds dx_speech_length[slot] samples;
                                                     capacity at most DX_SPEECH_LONG_SAMPLES (4.5 s) */
int dx_speech_articulation(const char *text, uint16_t minimum[64]);  /* each syllable's shortest, in ms */
```

A note is `{samples, note}`: its length counted at 22050 Hz and its MIDI pitch. The sound comes out at
11025 Hz, 16-bit mono. The program supplies `void dx_speech_idle(void)`, called while the engine works
(the FM-1 feeds its watchdog there). Built with `DX_HOST` defined, the engine runs on the calling thread;
without it, `speech_runtime.c` is the FM-1's: the work runs on its second core.

## Building the example

You need Python 3, CMake, a C compiler and eSpeak NG 1.52.0 in `vendor/` (the build checks the revision,
patches a copy in `build/espeak/` and compiles its English data; the checkout itself is never changed):

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --branch 1.52.0 https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng.git vendor/espeak-ng
tools/build.py
build/sing              # writes build/sing.wav
```

[LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md) says where the code comes from.
````

```text
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only */
/* Sing a line, a syllable a note, into a WAV file (11025 Hz, mono, 16-bit).
 *   build/sing [out.wav] */
#include "speech.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

void dx_speech_idle(void) {}            /* called while the engine works: a watchdog would be fed here */

static void u16(FILE *f, unsigned n) { fputc(n & 255, f); fputc((n >> 8) & 255, f); }
static void u32(FILE *f, unsigned n) { u16(f, n); u16(f, n >> 16); }

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    static const char text[] = "hello robot friend";
    static const uint8_t tune[] = {60, 64, 67, 64, 72};          /* a MIDI note for each syllable */
    static int16_t out[11025 * 8];
    unsigned at = 0;
    if (dx_speech_init() != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "the engine did not start\n");
        return 1;
    }
    static const uint8_t sound[4] = {50, 20, 20, 20};             /* body, breath, edge, glide: 0..100 */
    int syllables = dx_speech_scan(text);
    printf("\"%s\": %d syllables\n", text, syllables);
    for (int s = 0; s < syllables && s < (int)sizeof tune; s++) {
        dx_sing_note_t note = {22050u * 45u / 100u, tune[s]};   /* 0.45 s, counted at the engine's 22050 Hz */
        dx_speech_sound(sound);
        unsigned room = sizeof out / 2 - at;                      /* one syllable: at most 4.5 s */
        int rc = dx_speech_sing_into(0, text, (unsigned)s, &note, 1, 0, out + at,
                                     room < DX_SPEECH_LONG_SAMPLES ? room : DX_SPEECH_LONG_SAMPLES);
        if (rc != 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "syllable %d was not sung (%d)\n", s, rc);
            return 1;
        }
        at += dx_speech_length[0];
    }
    const char *path = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "build/sing.wav";
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "wb");
    if (!f)
        return 1;
    fwrite("RIFF", 1, 4, f); u32(f, 36 + at * 2); fwrite("WAVEfmt ", 1, 8, f);
    u32(f, 16); u16(f, 1); u16(f, 1); u32(f, 11025); u32(f, 22050); u16(f, 2); u16(f, 16);
    fwrite("data", 1, 4, f); u32(f, at * 2);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < at; i++)
        u16(f, (uint16_t)out[i]);
    fclose(f);
    printf("%.2f s sung: %s\n", at / 11025.0, path);
    return 0;
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only
"""Build the example (examples/sing.c) against the engine with the computer's own compiler.
eSpeak NG 1.52.0 must be in vendor/espeak-ng (see README.md).

    tools/build.py        -> build/sing"""
import os, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
os.chdir(root)
sys.path.insert(0, str(root / "tools"))
from prepare_espeak import prepare
speech = prepare(root)                   # eSpeak NG, patched and its English data compiled, in build/espeak
out = root / "build/obj"
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
cc = os.environ.get("CC", "cc")
base = [cc, "-O2", "-ffp-contract=off", "-DDX_HOST=1", "-Ivendor/espeak-ng/src/include",
        "-Ivendor/espeak-ng/src/ucd-tools/src/include", "-Isrc", "-Ibuild/espeak/src", "-Wno-everything"]
units = list(speech) + [Path("src") / u for u in ("speech.c", "speech_runtime.c", "singing.c")]
def compile(f):
    f = Path(f).relative_to(root) if Path(f).is_absolute() else Path(f)
    obj = out / (str(f).replace("/", "_") + ".o")
    extra = ["-include", "src/espeak_port.h"] if str(f).startswith(("vendor/", "build/espeak/")) else []
    subprocess.run([*base, *extra, "-c", str(f), "-o", str(obj)], check=True)
    return obj
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as pool:
    objects = list(pool.map(compile, units))
subprocess.run([*base, "examples/sing.c", *map(str, objects), "-lm", "-o", "build/sing"], check=True)
print("build/sing")
```

```c
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* The 386DX engine (vendor/386dx-engine: eSpeak NG's English front end + Klatt, GPL-3.0) speaking a line at one
 * pitch, for the listening lab. This file is ours and only calls the engine's public API (speech.h); linked with the
 * engine, the binary is GPL-3.0 and stays in build/, never committed or shared.
 *   dx386_say TEXT OUT.wav [MIDI_PITCH]     (11025 Hz mono 16-bit) */
#include "speech.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

void dx_speech_idle(void) {}

static void u16(FILE *f, unsigned n) { fputc(n & 255, f); fputc((n >> 8) & 255, f); }
static void u32(FILE *f, unsigned n) { u16(f, n); u16(f, n >> 16); }

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    static int16_t out[DX_SPEECH_LONG_SAMPLES];
    static const uint8_t sound[4] = {50, 20, 20, 20};   /* body, breath, edge, glide: the example's */
    int pitch = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 50, rc;
    if (argc < 3) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: dx386_say TEXT OUT.wav [MIDI_PITCH]\n");
        return 2;
    }
    if (dx_speech_init() != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "dx386_say: the engine did not start\n");
        return 1;
    }
    dx_speech_sound(sound);
    rc = dx_speech_make_into(0, argv[1], pitch, out, DX_SPEECH_LONG_SAMPLES);
    if (rc < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "dx386_say: not spoken (%d)\n", rc);
        return 1;
    }
    unsigned n = dx_speech_length[0];
    FILE *f = fopen(argv[2], "wb");
    if (!f)
        return 1;
    fwrite("RIFF", 1, 4, f); u32(f, 36 + n * 2); fwrite("WAVEfmt ", 1, 8, f);
    u32(f, 16); u16(f, 1); u16(f, 1); u32(f, 11025); u32(f, 22050); u16(f, 2); u16(f, 16);
    fwrite("data", 1, 4, f); u32(f, n * 2);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; i++)
        u16(f, (uint16_t)out[i]);
    fclose(f);
    printf("%u samples at 11025 Hz\n", n);
    return 0;
}
```

```python
"""CMUdict pronunciations (ARPAbet) as IPA for Moonshine's Klatt synth (which reads IPA with stress marks).

CMUdict is BSD-licensed (Carnegie Mellon University); `just voice-vendor` puts cmudict.dict in vendor/cmudict/.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

# ARPAbet (CMUdict's 39 phonemes) -> IPA. AH and ER depend on stress: unstressed AH is schwa.
VOWELS = {
    "AA": "ɑ", "AE": "æ", "AO": "ɔ", "AW": "aʊ", "AY": "aɪ", "EH": "ɛ", "EY": "eɪ",
    "IH": "ɪ", "IY": "i", "OW": "oʊ", "OY": "ɔɪ", "UH": "ʊ", "UW": "u",
}
CONSONANTS = {
    "B": "b", "CH": "tʃ", "D": "d", "DH": "ð", "F": "f", "G": "g", "HH": "h", "JH": "dʒ", "K": "k", "L": "l",
    "M": "m", "N": "n", "NG": "ŋ", "P": "p", "R": "ɹ", "S": "s", "SH": "ʃ", "T": "t", "TH": "θ", "V": "v",
    "W": "w", "Y": "j", "Z": "z", "ZH": "ʒ",
}
STRESS = {"1": "ˈ", "2": "ˌ", "0": ""}


def phone_to_ipa(phone: str) -> str:
    """One ARPAbet phone ("AH0", "TH") as IPA, the stress mark (if any) in front of the vowel."""
    base, digit = (phone[:-1], phone[-1]) if phone[-1].isdigit() else (phone, "")
    if base in CONSONANTS:
        return CONSONANTS[base]
    if base == "AH":
        vowel = "ə" if digit == "0" else "ʌ"
    elif base == "ER":
        vowel = "ɚ" if digit == "0" else "ɝ"
    elif base in VOWELS:
        vowel = VOWELS[base]
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"not an ARPAbet phone: {phone}")
    return STRESS.get(digit, "") + vowel


def to_ipa(phones: list[str]) -> str:
    return "".join(phone_to_ipa(p) for p in phones)


def load(path: Path) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """cmudict.dict: "word PH1 PH2 ..." a line; the first pronunciation of each word ("word(2)" are variants)."""
    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="latin-1").splitlines():
        if not line or line.startswith(";;;"):
            continue
        word, *phones = line.split("#")[0].split()
        if "(" in word or word in out:
            continue
        out[word.lower()] = phones
    return out


def line_ipa(text: str, cmu: dict[str, list[str]]) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """A line of words as IPA (words joined by spaces) and the words CMUdict does not have."""
    words, missing = [], []
    for raw in text.split():
        w = "".join(c for c in raw.lower() if c.isalpha() or c == "'")
        if not w:
            continue
        if w in cmu:
            words.append(to_ipa(cmu[w]))
        else:
            missing.append(w)
    return " ".join(words), missing


def phone_count(text: str, cmu: dict[str, list[str]]) -> int:
    """Phones in the line (what a packed one-byte-a-phone table would store), stress included in the vowel."""
    return sum(len(cmu.get("".join(c for c in w.lower() if c.isalpha() or c == "'"), [])) for w in text.split())

```

```python
"""IMA ADPCM (4 bits a sample), the plainest "store the recording" codec: encode, decode, and its size.

A decoder on the FM-1 is a few dozen lines and no RAM to speak of. One block = a 4-byte header (predictor, step
index) then the nibbles, as IMA/DVI ADPCM in WAV does; BLOCK samples a block.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

INDEX = (-1, -1, -1, -1, 2, 4, 6, 8)
STEPS = (
    7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 28, 31, 34, 37, 41, 45, 50, 55, 60, 66, 73, 80, 88, 97,
    107, 118, 130, 143, 157, 173, 190, 209, 230, 253, 279, 307, 337, 371, 408, 449, 494, 544, 598, 658, 724, 796,
    876, 963, 1060, 1166, 1282, 1411, 1552, 1707, 1878, 2066, 2272, 2499, 2749, 3024, 3327, 3660, 4026, 4428, 4871,
    5358, 5894, 6484, 7132, 7845, 8630, 9493, 10442, 11487, 12635, 13899, 15289, 16818, 18500, 20350, 22385, 24623,
    27086, 29794, 32767,
)
BLOCK = 505  # samples a block: 1 in the header + 504 nibbles (256-byte blocks, as WAV's IMA ADPCM at 8-22 kHz)


def _clamp(v: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return lo if v < lo else hi if v > hi else v


def _step(code: int, pred: int, idx: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    step = STEPS[idx]
    diff = step >> 3
    if code & 4:
        diff += step
    if code & 2:
        diff += step >> 1
    if code & 1:
        diff += step >> 2
    pred = _clamp(pred - diff if code & 8 else pred + diff, -32768, 32767)
    return pred, _clamp(idx + INDEX[code & 7], 0, 88)


def encode(pcm: list[int]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for b in range(0, len(pcm), BLOCK):
        blk = pcm[b:b + BLOCK]
        pred, idx = blk[0], 0
        out += int(pred).to_bytes(2, "little", signed=True) + bytes((idx, 0))
        nib: list[int] = []
        for s in blk[1:]:
            step, diff, code = STEPS[idx], s - pred, 0
            if diff < 0:
                code, diff = 8, -diff
            if diff >= step:
                code |= 4
                diff -= step
            if diff >= step >> 1:
                code |= 2
                diff -= step >> 1
            if diff >= step >> 2:
                code |= 1
            pred, idx = _step(code, pred, idx)
            nib.append(code)
        if len(nib) % 2:
            nib.append(0)
        out += bytes(nib[i] | (nib[i + 1] << 4) for i in range(0, len(nib), 2))
    return bytes(out)


def decode(data: bytes, n: int) -> list[int]:
    """n samples back from encode()'s bytes."""
    out: list[int] = []
    blk_bytes = 4 + (BLOCK - 1 + 1) // 2
    for b in range(0, len(data), blk_bytes):
        blk = data[b:b + blk_bytes]
        pred, idx = int.from_bytes(blk[0:2], "little", signed=True), blk[2]
        out.append(pred)
        for byte in blk[4:]:
            for code in (byte & 15, byte >> 4):
                if len(out) >= n:
                    return out
                pred, idx = _step(code, pred, idx)
                out.append(pred)
    return out[:n]

```

```python
"""Mono 16-bit WAV in and out (the standard library's wave), and raw s16le."""

from __future__ import annotations

import array
import wave
from pathlib import Path


def read(path: Path) -> tuple[list[int], int]:
    with wave.open(str(path), "rb") as w:
        if w.getsampwidth() != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: not 16-bit")
        ch, rate = w.getnchannels(), w.getframerate()
        a = array.array("h", w.readframes(w.getnframes()))
    return list(a[::ch]), rate


def write(path: Path, pcm: list[int], rate: int) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as w:
        w.setnchannels(1)
        w.setsampwidth(2)
        w.setframerate(rate)
        w.writeframes(array.array("h", pcm).tobytes())


def raw_to_wav(raw: Path, wav_path: Path, rate: int, channels: int = 1) -> None:
    """s16le samples (channels interleaved; the first one kept) as a mono WAV."""
    a = array.array("h", raw.read_bytes())
    write(wav_path, list(a[::channels]), rate)
```

````text
=================== genkigenki/Speak37
<p align="center"><img src="docs/banner.png" width="100%" alt="Speak37: a talking synth for the SMK-37 and the FM-1, with MOPE the robot on the screen"></p>
# Speak37
[![License: GPL-3.0-only](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3.0--only-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
The "37" is where it started, the SMK-37; Speak37 runs on the FM-1 too.
**Watch it:** [Speak37 on YouTube](https://youtu.be/JkLWlMOAvNA) · **Install it:** <https://genkigenki.github.io/smk37/>
**Speech, played musically, on the M-Vave SMK-37 (SMK-37 Pro, Elite, MKE-P37) and the FM-1.** A speech synthesizer
in the style of the Speak & Spell: every key speaks the next word of a sentence, at the key's pitch. Pick a joke on
a pad and play it as a melody, a word a key; play a chord and the word comes out in harmony. Sing folk songs a word a key and the
Kyrie a syllable a key with a choir, chant robot mantras, play a beatbox kit, let PLAY speak a sentence in time over
a drum groove while the keys only choose its notes, write your own sentences on the instrument, or play to MOPE, a
gloomy robot that comments on what you play. Nine voices,
from the classic toy to a cold test-lab robot and a choir, delay, reverb, 16 drum grooves, and a green
vacuum-fluorescent display on the screen.
Speak37 runs on the keyboard's own chip, in place of the stock firmware. It is built on the platform layer of the
[Felucca](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca) firmware (Leo Kuroshita / Hügelton Instruments): the hardware
drivers, USB, the flash store and the update path. RHYTHM plays an 808 from M-VAVE's FM1 Open (MIT), ported to
fixed point. Felucca's README is kept as
[README-UPSTREAM.md](README-UPSTREAM.md).
One-page reference: [CHEATSHEET.md](CHEATSHEET.md).
> **Version 1.0.** Installing custom firmware is at your own risk; the stock firmware can always be put back (see
> [Install](#install) and [Safety](#safety)).
>
> **FM-1: Need feedback how to improve the usage on the FM-1.** The FM-1 has no pads, faders or wheels, so their jobs
> sit on its buttons and knobs (see [On the FM-1](#on-the-fm-1)); ideas and reports are welcome.
## Quick start
1. Install Speak37 (see [Install](#install)).
2. The pads are the 16 sentences of a bank (SONGS at first, sung by CHOIR). Tap one: the display shows it.
3. Play the keys: each key speaks (or sings) the next word or syllable, at its pitch. After the last the first again.
   A sung word holds its vowel while the key is held and sings the rest when you let go.
4. Play a chord: keys pressed together speak the same word, in harmony.
5. Turn K3 (VOICE): CLASSIC, VINTAGE, DEEP, CHILD, WHISPER, ROBOT, LAB AI, GIANT, CHOIR. K4 (BANK) changes the bank
   (a bank with its own voice, such as ROBOT or LAB AI, picks it).
6. SEQ PLAY: the sentence speaks itself in time (TEMPO); now the keys only choose its pitch. SEQ PLAY again stops.
7. SEQ: the RHYTHM page, the pads are 16 drum grooves. Tap BOSSA NOVA, then SEQ PLAY: the words land on the beat.
8. The last bank, USER: hold a pad 0.6 s and write a sentence of your own.
## Try it in your browser
The [Speak37 simulator](https://genkigenki.github.io/smk37/speak37-sim/) runs the firmware's own C sources (the
speech, the drums, MOPE, the screen and the SMK-37's panel) compiled to WebAssembly: fixed point as on the keyboard,
at its sample rate (44118 Hz). Click to start the sound, then play the keys with the mouse, a finger, the computer
keyboard (A W S E D ... = the keys, Z / X = the octave) or a MIDI keyboard. PATCH wakes MOPE.
Build it yourself (Emscripten):
```
sh web/sim/build.sh                           # build/sim: index.html, worklet.js, sim.wasm
node web/sim/sim_test.mjs build/sim/sim.wasm  # the wasm in Node: boots, speaks, MOPE talks, its game, its sulk
python3 -m http.server -d build/sim 8737      # then open http://localhost:8737
```
## The sound
**An LPC speech engine in the style of the TI TMS5220** (the Speak & Spell's family of chips): an excitation (a
pulse train, the chip's own chirp, a glottal pulse or noise) through a ten-stage lattice filter whose reflection
coefficients K1..K10, energy and pitch come from the word's frames.
- **The words are our own.** No TI ROM vocabulary is used: every word of the sentences, the letters A..Z, the
  numbers and the editor's word lists are spoken by the free speech synthesizer
  [espeak-ng](https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng) (its own voice for each language) and LPC-encoded at build
  time by Speak37's own encoder (`tools/gen_vocab.py`) into TMS5220-style frames (the chip's quantisation tables for
  energy, pitch and K1..K10). The SMK-37 build holds 2759 words (390 KB of frames, 19 minutes of speech), the FM-1
  build 2576. The frames are 10 ms (the chip used 25 ms): measured with a speech recogniser, 25 ms frames lost about
  half of the words that 10 ms frames keep. Words are rendered a little faster and coded with a repeat tolerance,
  which keeps the recogniser's score at about 60 % of the bytes.
- **At the key's pitch.** The voiced frames' excitation runs at the key's note (with OCTAVE, pitch bend, vibrato,
  glide): within a cent of the key, every voice. The word's own intonation (its frames' pitch against its median)
  rides on top, 0..200 % (INTONE); unvoiced frames stay noise. A held key at the word's end holds its vowel (HOLD).
- **Formants** (FORMANT, LFO 2): the lattice runs at 8 kHz x 2^(FORMANT/12), so the whole vocal tract scales, a child
  up, a giant down; its output is resampled to 44.1 kHz, smoothly or held for the original's grit (LOFI).
  Held, its images (every formant mirrored around the lattice's rate: an open A's F1 and F2 came back at 7 kHz, only
  13 dB down, and an A sounded like an I) are taken away by a 4th-order low-pass at the lattice's band edge, as the
  Speak & Spell's own output filter did (now some 30 dB down); the vowels' F1 and F2 are as espeak-ng said them
  (`tests/sp_test.c` checks an open A's F1 above 600 Hz, an I's below 450 Hz).
- **Twelve voices at once** (CHOIR takes three a note; fewer if the processor runs short: it measures itself). See
  [CPU](#cpu).
- **Sung words** (SONGS, CHURCH, the language banks' songs): while its key is held the voice stays on the
  word's vowel at exactly the key's pitch, and letting go sings the rest. SONGS and the language banks' songs sing
  whole words, a word a key (clearer than syllables); CHURCH sings syllables (*E LE I SON*).
- **Speech percussion** (the PERCUSSION bank, KIT mode): BOOM, UH, B, P, D, T, K, KA, TS, TSS, TCH, SH, PF, POP,
  TOK, HA: espeak-ng's consonant sounds cut short with a decaying energy, brought up to the loud words. In KIT mode
  each key and each pad (by its pressure) plays one hit.
| Voice | Character |
|---|---|
| CLASSIC | the clear default: pulse excitation, a little grit, a gentle intonation |
| VINTAGE | the first Speak & Spell chips' chirp as excitation, held samples: the toy as remembered |
| DEEP | formants 3 semitones down, darker |
| CHILD | formants 4 up, livelier intonation, a bit faster |
| WHISPER | noise only, no pitch: every frame unvoiced |
| ROBOT | monotone (no intonation), a metallic comb tuned to the note |
| LAB AI | a cold, clean test-lab voice: a smooth glottal pulse, formants slightly up, its intonation snapped to semitone steps, a short glide between them |
| GIANT | formants 6 down, slower |
| CHOIR | every note sung by three voices, slightly detuned and apart in formants and time, a glottal pulse, a slow attack, a big room |
**Effects:** DELAY (DIGITAL, TAPE with wow and darkening repeats, PING-PONG), REVERB (damped combs and all-passes,
SIZE), SPREAD, TONE, METAL, BREATH, two LFOs (vibrato; the formants' wobble), the mod wheel's vibrato, pitch bend
(SETUP: 1..12 semitones), glide, envelope (ATTACK, RELEASE, velocity).
**Note modes** (HOLD; ARP cycles them): ONE SHOT (the word plays out), GATE (letting go fades it), HOLD (the word
=================== pjac1810/spellbox
# SPELLBOX — jeu d'orthographe parlant pour M-VAVE FM-1
Firmware alternatif qui transforme le FM-1 en jeu d'orthographe parlant, sur le modèle du Speak & Spell de Texas Instruments (1978).
On y retrouve :
- la voix de synthèse LPC d'époque : 10 coefficients, 8 kHz, convertisseur 8 bits et petit haut-parleur ;
- l'afficheur fluorescent bleu-vert à 8 caractères derrière sa vitre rouge ;
- les jeux SPELL, LETTER, SAY IT, SECRET CODE et MYSTERY WORD, en anglais, sur 4 niveaux.
En plus :
- **SING** fait chanter les mots au clavier ;
- **LETTER SYNTH** fait du clavier un instrument dont chaque touche chante sa lettre ;
- **SPEAK** prononce ce que tu tapes, comme les synthétiseurs de parole des années 80 ;
- des réglages de « circuit bending » (horloge, pitch, coefficients corrompus, bégaiement…) imitent les Speak & Spell trafiqués.
C'est un projet indépendant, sans lien avec Texas Instruments ni M-VAVE :
- Aucune donnée des ROM d'origine n'est utilisée. Les mots, les phrases et les 42 phonèmes sont prononcés par le synthétiseur libre espeak-ng, puis recodés en trames LPC par `tools/gen_speech.py`.
- Les tables de quantification, l'excitation, les règles de lecture et les listes de mots sont les nôtres.
Il est bâti sur [foma](https://github.com/konsumer/foma) (plateforme Felucca), avec installeur web, mode secours et retour au firmware d'origine.
## Jouer
**Le clavier est alphabétique**, comme sur le jouet : A est la touche la plus grave (F3), puis B, C… jusqu'à Z. La touche la plus aiguë (G5) fait ENTRÉE. L'écran montre la lettre de chaque touche.
| Preset | Déroulement |
|---|---|
| SPELL | « Spell… » + un mot. Tape-le puis ENTRÉE. Juste : « That is correct ». Faux : « Wrong, try again ». Faux deux fois : l'appareil épelle le bon mot, qui apparaît lettre par lettre. Après 10 mots, il annonce le score (« Perfect score » et fanfare à 10/10). |
| LETTER | chaque touche dit et affiche sa lettre |
| SAY IT | le mot s'affiche, « Say it ! » : dis-le à voix haute, ENTRÉE pour l'entendre, ENTRÉE pour le suivant. Après 10 mots : « Now spell », et on épelle les mêmes. |
| SECRET CODE | tape un mot, ENTRÉE : il est codé lettre pour lettre (A↔Z, B↔Y…). Recoder le message codé le décode. |
| MYSTERY WORD | le pendu : propose des lettres, 7 erreurs permises. Les lettres déjà tentées restent allumées. ENTRÉE pour un nouveau mot. |
| SING | les touches deviennent des notes : le mot choisi (SELECT parcourt tout le vocabulaire) est chanté à la hauteur de la touche, et sa voyelle tient tant que la touche est enfoncée. Fonctionne aussi en MIDI. |
| LETTER SYNTH | le clavier devient un instrument de lettres : chaque touche chante sa propre lettre (A, B, C…) à sa hauteur, et la voyelle tient tant qu'on garde la touche. Avec SELECT, une seule lettre peut aussi être mise sur toutes les touches (« B » partout, par exemple) pour jouer une mélodie. L'afficheur montre la lettre et la note. Fonctionne aussi en MIDI. |
| SPEAK | tape un ou plusieurs mots (OCT+ = espace, OCT− ou REC = effacer, SEL = tout effacer), puis ENTRÉE : SPELLBOX les prononce. SEQ répète. |
**Comment SPEAK lit un mot** :
1. Il cherche le mot dans un dictionnaire de prononciation de 12 000 mots anglais courants.
2. Sinon, il cherche un mot connu suivi d'une terminaison : -S, -ES, -ED, -ING, -LY, -ER, -EST, -NESS (« RUNNING » = RUN + ING).
3. Sinon, il applique des règles de lecture, comme les puces des années 80. Les noms propres et les mots inventés sont donc lus à l'anglaise.
Les phonèmes s'enchaînent sans coupure, sur une voix grave (autour de 80 Hz), avec une intonation qui monte sur les syllabes accentuées et retombe en fin de phrase. SPEED et PITCH (page VOICE) l'ajustent encore.
| Commande FM-1 | Fonction |
|---|---|
| PRESETS (ou EDIT) | choix du preset |
| SELECT / ALGORITHM | niveau 1 à 4 (SING : le mot à chanter ; LETTER SYNTH : A-Z ou une seule lettre) |
| PLAY | ENTRÉE |
| REC | EFFACE la dernière lettre |
| SEQ | RÉPÈTE la consigne (SPEAK : redit le texte) |
| SEL | nouvelle partie (SPEAK : efface le texte) |
| HOME | VOICE : PITCH (±12 demi-tons), SPEED (débit), CLOCK (horloge de la puce, 4 à 14 kHz : tout bouge ensemble), TONE (haut-parleur) |
| ENV | BEND : BEND (coefficients corrompus), STUTTER (trames rejouées), MONO (intonation aplatie), CRUSH (convertisseur 8 à 3 bits) |
| GLO | active ou coupe les effets BEND d'un coup |
| SAVE | garde niveau, réglages et choix de lettre |
| OCT− / OCT+ | SING, LETTER SYNTH : octave du clavier ; SPEAK : effacer / espace |
| MASTER | volume |
## Les mots
100 mots en 4 niveaux de 25, de 8 lettres au plus (la taille de l'afficheur), de CAT et APPLE jusqu'à SERGEANT ou MORTGAGE.
Pour en changer, il suffit d'éditer les listes en tête de `tools/gen_speech.py`, puis de lancer `pip install espeakng-loader wordfreq scipy numpy` et `python3 tools/gen_speech.py`.
## Obtenir et installer le firmware
- **GitHub** : pousse ce dossier sur la branche `main` d'un dépôt. Le workflow compile tout.
  - Le `.fwsc` est dans l'artefact `spellbox-fwsc` et sur la branche `firmware`.
  - Avec Settings → Pages → Source : GitHub Actions, l'émulateur et l'installeur sont publiés sur GitHub Pages.
- **Docker Desktop** : `./fm1 build` ou `./fm1 dev` (http://localhost:8000).
L'installation se fait depuis la page Install (Chrome ou Edge, FM-1 branché en USB).
**Secours** : maintiens OCT− à l'allumage ; l'onglet Rescue remet le firmware M-VAVE V15. Installer un firmware non officiel se fait à tes risques.
## Développement
- `tools/gen_speech.py` génère `src/speech.h`. Il contient :
  - le vocabulaire et les 42 phonèmes coupés dans la parole d'espeak-ng ;
  - l'analyse LPC (Levinson, détection de hauteur et de voisement), la quantification entraînée et le flux de bits ;
  - le dictionnaire compressé et les règles lettre → son. Hors dictionnaire, les règles donnent environ 83 % de phonèmes justes.
- `src/speech.c` : la puce vocale en entiers. Elle comprend :
  - un treillis à 10 étages, interpolé 8 fois par trame ;
  - l'excitation par chirp ou par bruit, le convertisseur 8 bits et le haut-parleur ;
  - l'enchaînement des phonèmes et la tenue des voyelles ;
  - les bips et la file de ce qu'il faut dire.
- `src/tts.c` : la lecture d'un texte, par le dictionnaire, les terminaisons puis les règles, avec l'intonation.
- `src/main.c` : les jeux, l'afficheur 14 segments, le clavier, les LEDs et la sauvegarde.
- `tests/run.sh` : dit le vocabulaire et des phrases dans des WAV, puis fait un fuzz de la puce, du texte → parole et de tous les réglages (UBSan).
- Identité du paquet : `FM-1_57` (dans `firmware.json`).
## Licence
GPL-3.0-only. Crédits : [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md).
- La voix vient d'espeak-ng (GPL-3.0), utilisé seulement pour fabriquer les données.
- Le choix des mots du dictionnaire vient des listes de fréquence de [wordfreq](https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq) (CC BY-SA 4.0).
````

```python
"""Render every test word with every speech option into build/voicelab/<engine>/<slug>.wav.

Engines whose tools are missing are skipped with a note (`just voice-vendor` fetches and builds them). The reference
voice (macOS `say`, Samantha) is also the source the LPC and ADPCM options encode: it is fine for listening on this
Mac, but a deck to share needs a voice whose output may be redistributed (Kokoro, Apache-2.0).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from . import adpcm, arpabet, wav

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
OUT = ROOT / "build/voicelab"
BIN = OUT / "bin"
TMP = OUT / "tmp"
VENDOR = ROOT / "vendor"
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
MOONSHINE = VENDOR / "moonshine/micro"
WIZARD = VENDOR / "python_wizard/python_wizard"
DX386 = VENDOR / "386dx-engine"
CMUDICT = VENDOR / "cmudict/cmudict.dict"
EMU = ROOT / "tools/fm1-emu/fm1-live"
SPELLBOX = ROOT / "downloads/spellbox-0.3.fwsc"
SAY_VOICE = "Samantha"


@dataclass
class Engine:
    key: str
    name: str
    where: str
    licence: str
    shared: str = ""            # data every word shares (a dictionary, a voice), in words
    shared_kb: float = 0.0
    size_note: str = ""         # what the per-word bytes count
    items: dict[str, dict] = field(default_factory=dict)   # slug -> {"wav": rel path, "bytes": int | None}
    skipped: str = ""


ENGINES = [
    Engine("say", "macOS say（Samantha）", "電腦：連線時用 USB audio 從 FM-1 喇叭播", "Apple（只能自用）",
           size_note="不存進機器"),
    Engine("klatt-ipa", "Klatt 共振峰（Moonshine）＋ CMUdict 音素", "機器上合成；音素由電腦先查好", "MIT（CMUdict BSD）",
           size_note="一個音素 1 byte"),
    Engine("klatt-g2p", "Klatt 共振峰（Moonshine）＋ 它自己的 G2P", "機器上：直接念拼字", "MIT",
           shared="G2P 字典", shared_kb=150, size_note="只存拼字"),
    Engine("dx386", "386DX 引擎：eSpeak NG 前端＋Klatt", "機器上：任意英文", "GPL-3.0",
           shared="eSpeak 英文資料", shared_kb=305, size_note="只存拼字"),
    Engine("lpc25", "LPC，25 ms 一幀（TMS5220 原規格）", "電腦先編碼，機器解碼（firmware/common/lpc.c）", "解碼器 MIT",
           size_note="LPC 位元流"),
    Engine("lpc10", "LPC，10 ms 一幀（Speak37 的做法）", "同上", "解碼器 MIT", size_note="LPC 位元流"),
    Engine("adpcm11", "IMA ADPCM 11 kHz（預錄）", "電腦先編碼，機器解碼", "免費", size_note="4 bit 一個樣本"),
    Engine("adpcm16", "IMA ADPCM 16 kHz（預錄）", "同上", "免費", size_note="4 bit 一個樣本"),
    Engine("spellbox", "SPELLBOX 的 SPEAK（fm1-emu）", "FM-1 韌體本身：12k 字典＋規則 → LPC", "GPL-3.0",
           shared="字典＋音素庫", size_note="（韌體內建）"),
]


def slug(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.lower()).strip("-")


def load_words(path: Path = HERE / "words.txt") -> list[str]:
    return [ln.strip() for ln in path.read_text().splitlines() if ln.strip() and not ln.lstrip().startswith("#")]


def run(cmd: list, **kw) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run([str(c) for c in cmd], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, **kw)


# ---- tools -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_tools() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Compile the renderers this lab needs into build/voicelab/bin -> {engine key: why it is skipped}."""
    BIN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    skip: dict[str, str] = {}
    run(["cc", "-O2", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-I", ROOT / "firmware/common", HERE / "lpc_decode.c", "-o", BIN / "lpc_decode"])
    if (MOONSHINE / "klatt-tts").is_dir():
        k, g = MOONSHINE / "klatt-tts", MOONSHINE / "g2p"
        srcs = sorted((k / "src").glob("*.cc")) + sorted((g / "src").glob("*.cc"))
        inc = [f"-I{p}" for p in (k / "include", k / "include/tts", k / "src", g / "include", g / "include/g2p", g / "src")]
        run(["clang++", "-std=c++17", "-O2", *inc, *srcs, HERE / "klatt_render.cpp", "-o", BIN / "klatt_render"])
    else:
        skip["klatt-ipa"] = skip["klatt-g2p"] = "vendor/moonshine 不在（just voice-vendor）"
    if not CMUDICT.exists():
        skip["klatt-ipa"] = "vendor/cmudict 不在（just voice-vendor）"
    objs = sorted((DX386 / "build/obj").glob("*.o"))
    if objs:
        run(["cc", "-O2", "-DDX_HOST=1", f"-I{DX386 / 'src'}", "-Wno-everything", HERE / "dx386_say.c", *objs, "-lm",
             "-o", BIN / "dx386_say"])
    else:
        skip["dx386"] = "vendor/386dx-engine 還沒 build（just voice-vendor）"
    if not WIZARD.exists():
        skip["lpc25"] = skip["lpc10"] = "vendor/python_wizard 不在（just voice-vendor）"
    if not (EMU.exists() and SPELLBOX.exists()):
        skip["spellbox"] = "需要 fm1-emu（just emu-fetch）與 SPELLBOX（just voice-fetch）"
    return skip


# ---- engines ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ref_aiff(text: str) -> Path:
    TMP.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p = TMP / f"{slug(text)}.aiff"
    if not p.exists():
        run(["say", "-v", SAY_VOICE, "-o", p, text])
    return p


def resample(src: Path, dst: Path, rate: int) -> Path:
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    run(["ffmpeg", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-i", src, "-ar", str(rate), "-ac", "1", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", dst])
    return dst


def r_say(text: str, out: Path) -> int | None:
    resample(ref_aiff(text), out, 22050)
    return None


def r_klatt_ipa(text: str, out: Path, cmu: dict) -> int | None:
    ipa, missing = arpabet.line_ipa(text, cmu)
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(f"CMUdict has no {missing}")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    run([BIN / "klatt_render", "ipa", ipa, out])
    return arpabet.phone_count(text, cmu) + max(0, len(text.split()) - 1)


def r_klatt_g2p(text: str, out: Path) -> int | None:
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    run([BIN / "klatt_render", "text", text, out])
    return len(text)


def r_dx386(text: str, out: Path) -> int | None:
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    run([BIN / "dx386_say", text, out])
    return len(text)


def r_lpc(text: str, out: Path, frame_ms: int) -> int | None:
    w8 = resample(ref_aiff(text), TMP / f"{slug(text)}-8k.wav", 8000)
    hexs = run([sys.executable, WIZARD, "-T", "tms5220", "-F", str(frame_ms), "-f", "hex", w8]).stdout
    data = bytes.fromhex(hexs)
    lpc_bin, raw = TMP / f"{slug(text)}-{frame_ms}.lpc", TMP / f"{slug(text)}-{frame_ms}.raw"
    lpc_bin.write_bytes(data)
    run([BIN / "lpc_decode", lpc_bin, frame_ms, raw])
    wav.raw_to_wav(raw, out, 8000)
    return len(data)


def r_adpcm(text: str, out: Path, rate: int) -> int | None:
    src = resample(ref_aiff(text), TMP / f"{slug(text)}-{rate}.wav", rate)
    pcm, _ = wav.read(src)
    enc = adpcm.encode(pcm)
    wav.write(out, adpcm.decode(enc, len(pcm)), rate)
    return len(enc)


# SPELLBOX in the emulator: PRESET (encoder 6) +7 = SPEAK, the word typed on the alphabetical keys (F3 = A ...
# F#5 = Z), PLAY speaks it. The audio from PLAY on is the word.
_NOTES = ["C", "C#", "D", "D#", "E", "F", "F#", "G", "G#", "A", "A#", "B"]
EMU_RATE = 44118


def r_spellbox(text: str, out: Path) -> int | None:
    letters = [c for c in text.lower() if c.isalpha()]
    if len(letters) != len(text) or len(letters) > 16:
        raise RuntimeError("SPEAK 只測單字（句子要用 OCT+ 當空白，這裡不測）")
    ev, t = ["3000:e6:+7"], 3500
    for c in letters:
        m = 53 + ord(c) - ord("a")
        k = f"{_NOTES[m % 12]}{m // 12 - 1}"
        ev += [f"{t}:{k}@100", f"{t + 80}:{k}^"]
        t += 200
    play = t + 1200
    ev += [f"{play}:PLAY", f"{play + 100}:PLAY^"]
    work = TMP / "emu" / slug(text)
    rec = work / "rec"
    if work.exists():
        for p in sorted(work.rglob("*"), reverse=True):
            p.unlink() if p.is_file() else p.rmdir()
    (work / "work").mkdir(parents=True)
    env = {"FM1_BENCH_KEYS": ",".join(ev), "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin"}
    subprocess.run([str(EMU), "--fwsc", str(SPELLBOX), "--flash-chip", "uc25hq80", "--flash", str(work / "x.flash"),
                    "--midi", "none", "--shot", str(play + 3500), "--record", str(rec), "--lcd-only"],
                   cwd=work, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True)
    import array
    a = array.array("h", (rec / "audio.raw").read_bytes())
    mono = list(a[::2])[play * EMU_RATE // 1000:]
    # trim the silence after the word
    end = len(mono)
    while end > 0 and abs(mono[end - 1]) < 200:
        end -= 1
    wav.write(out, mono[:end + EMU_RATE // 10], EMU_RATE)
    return None


# ---- the lab ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build(only: set[str] | None = None) -> list[Engine]:
    skip = build_tools()
    cmu = arpabet.load(CMUDICT) if CMUDICT.exists() else {}
    words = load_words()
    renderers = {
        "say": r_say,
        "klatt-ipa": lambda t, o: r_klatt_ipa(t, o, cmu),
        "klatt-g2p": r_klatt_g2p,
        "dx386": r_dx386,
        "lpc25": lambda t, o: r_lpc(t, o, 25),
        "lpc10": lambda t, o: r_lpc(t, o, 10),
        "adpcm11": lambda t, o: r_adpcm(t, o, 11025),
        "adpcm16": lambda t, o: r_adpcm(t, o, 16000),
        "spellbox": r_spellbox,
    }
    engines = [e for e in ENGINES if not only or e.key in only]
    for e in engines:
        if e.key in skip:
            e.skipped = skip[e.key]
            print(f"skip {e.key}: {e.skipped}")
            continue
        print(f"{e.key} ...", flush=True)
        for text in words:
            out = OUT / e.key / f"{slug(text)}.wav"
            try:
                n = renderers[e.key](text, out)
                e.items[slug(text)] = {"text": text, "wav": f"{e.key}/{slug(text)}.wav", "bytes": n}
            except (RuntimeError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as err:
                msg = getattr(err, "stderr", None) or str(err)
                e.items[slug(text)] = {"text": text, "error": str(msg).strip()[:200]}
    (OUT / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"words": words, "engines": [e.__dict__ for e in engines]}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    return engines

```
